items.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'Europe finit dans le vert, la baisse des rendements compense la débâcle de la "tech"
items.author: Diana Mandia
items.creator: Diana Mandia
items.summary: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en hausse jeudi, profitant de la forte baisse des rendements obligataires dans un contexte de ventes massives dans le secteur technologique, qui est à nouveau l'objet de la méfiance du marché en raison de son niveau d'endettement élevé.
items.body:
Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en hausse jeudi, profitant de la forte baisse des rendements obligataires dans un contexte de ventes massives dans le secteur technologique, qui est à nouveau l'objet de la méfiance du marché en raison de son niveau d'endettement élevé.
À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) a gagné 0,78% à 7.934,70 points. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) a pris 0,33% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) a progressé de 1,08%.
L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) a perdu 0,36%, mais le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) a fini sur un gain de 0,37% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) a pris 0,38%.
Les places européennes ont été épargnées jeudi, moins exposées au secteur technologique que New York, Tokyo ou Séoul, et ont même pu reprendre un peu leur souffle grâce à un recul des rendements de la dette souveraine.
De l'autre côté de l'Atlantique, le Nasdaq recule en revanche au cours d'une séance où le coût de l'assurance contre le défaut de paiement des groupes liés à l'IA a atteint dans certains cas des niveaux records.
L'opérateur américain de centres de données CoreWeave (CRWV.O) attire tous les regards, au coeur d'une nouvelle tempête sur le marché du crédit, déclenchée par une l'inflation américaine qui ne cesse de s'accélérer et qui pourrait conduire la banque centrale à relever davantage ses taux d'intérêt.
Le groupe doit près de 50 milliards de dollars à ses créanciers et cette dette, tout comme celle d'autres entreprises du secteur contractée pour financer la course à l'intelligence artificielle (IA), pourrait s'avérer encore plus coûteuse dans le cadre d'une politique monétaire restrictive.
Les indicateurs économiques récents, notamment l'indice des prix à la consommation aux Etats-Unis, ont ravivé les craintes inflationnistes, remettant brièvement sur le tapis la possibilité d'une hausse des coûts d'emprunt par la Fed en octobre, un scénario qui avait pourtant été écarté.
Mais les rendements obligataires reculent nettement jeudi, les investisseurs recherchant avant tout la sécurité offerte par la dette souveraine et semblant convaincus que la banque centrale attendra cette fois-ci.
"Même si l'inflation reste élevée, le risque est qu'elle puisse nuire à la croissance à long terme ; les inquiétudes liées à l'IA et la possibilité d'un fléchissement des Bourses renforcent les arguments en faveur d'une fuite vers la qualité", souligne Collin Martin, analyste au Schwab Center for Financial Research.
Les opérateurs sont également attirés par les rendements attractifs après leur récente flambée, avec des pics inégalés depuis plus de deux décennies pour les échéances longues, tant en Europe qu'aux États-Unis.
VALEURS Les actions des fabricants européens de puces électroniques et des groupes liés à l'IA ont reculé, ASML (ASML.AS) , STMicroelectronics (STMPA.PA) , BESI (BESI.AS) , Infineon (IFXGn.DE) et ASMI (ASMI.AS) clôturant sur des baisses allant de 3,7% à 7%.
Legrand (LEGD.PA) et Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) , dont l'activité est très dépendante des centres de données, ont perdu 1,2% et 2,4% respectivement.
L'indice technologique du Stoxx 6000 (.SX8P) a abandonné 1,54%, réduisant ses pertes après être tombé en séance à son plus bas niveau depuis plus de trois semaines, à 998,99 points.
Dans le reste de l'actualité des entreprises, Pernod Ricard (PERP.PA) a pris 0,76% après avoir fait état d'une baisse moins importante que prévu de son chiffre d'affaires du premier trimestre.
Ailleurs en Europe, le fabricant d'équipements télécoms Ericsson (ERICb.ST) a grimpé de 6,8% après avoir publié un bénéfice d'exploitation trimestriel avec une baisse moins marquée qu'initialement anticipé.
A WALL STREET Les indices de la Bourse de New York évoluent en ordre dispersé à l'heure de la clôture des Bourses européennes, le Nasdaq réduisant quelque peu les pertes enregistrées en début de séance.
Le Dow Jones (.DJI) prend 0,91%, le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) grappille 0,05% et le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) cède 0,39%.
CoreWeave (CRWV.O) abandonne 2,2% après avoir chuté de 15% mercredi et Nvidia (NVDA.O) perd 1,5%.
L'indice Philadelphia SE Semiconductor (.SOX) affiche un recul de 1,74%, prolongeant ainsi une baisse qui dure déjà depuis sept séances.
LES INDICATEURS DU JOUR Les prix à la production (PPI) aux États-Unis [USN:L8N4611JP TEXT:"ont enregistré"] en septembre leur plus forte hausse en quatre ans et demi, sous l'effet de l'augmentation des coûts des biens et des services, dernier signe en date d'un élargissement des pressions inflationnistes au-delà des produits énergétiques.
Les ventes au détail ont pour leur part [USN:L8N4611BG TEXT:"augmenté"] plus que prévu le mois dernier, portées par la hausse des prix de l'essence, même si les dépenses dans d'autres secteurs sont restées modérées.
Le nombre de personnes ayant déposé une nouvelle demande d'allocation chômage a en outre légèrement augmenté la semaine dernière, dans un contexte de faible nombre de licenciements qui contribue à la stabilité du marché du travail.
Dans la zone euro, la production industrielle [USN:ZRN00ENSW TEXT:"a diminué"] de façon inattendue en août, selon les données publiées jeudi par Eurostat, l'office statistique de l'Union européenne.
En France, l'inflation harmonisée selon les normes européennes (IPCH) [USN:L6N4610EX TEXT:"a accéléré"] comme attendu à 3,4% sur un an en septembre, montrent les données définitives de l'Insee.
TAUX Les rendements des Bunds, l'obligation de référence de la zone euro, ont atteint jeudi leur plus bas niveau depuis plusieurs semaines, les craintes liées à la technologie poussant les investisseurs à se réfugier dans la dette souveraine.
Le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans a perdu près de 6 points de base pour finir la séance à 3,4068%. Celui de l'obligation à deux ans a perdu 2,2 points de base à 3,0781%.
En France, le rendement de l'OAT à dix ans a abandonné 9,2 points de base à 4,7887%.
Les anticipations concernant l'évolution des taux de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) restent globalement inchangées, les marchés monétaires tablant sur un statu quo en octobre avant une nouvelle hausse en décembre.
Selon Alvaro Santos Pereira, membre du conseil des gouverneurs de l'institution de Francfort, l'inflation liée aux prix de l'énergie [USN:L6N4610KY TEXT:"ne se répercute"] pas sur les autres prix, ce qui constitue un signe rassurant.
Eurostat doit publier vendredi les données définitives sur l'inflation dans le bloc monétaire en septembre.
Les investisseurs sont également attentifs aux actualités concernant la présidence de la BCE, après que Reuters [USN:L6N4610Y6 TEXT:"a rapporté"] que le Forum économique mondial (WEF) pourrait nommer Christine Lagarde à sa tête dès le mois prochain.
Aux Etats-Unis, le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans affiche un recul de 9,7 points de base et ressort à 5,0933%. Le deux ans cède 3,8 points de base à 4,7636%.
CHANGES Le dollar recule après avoir atteint mercredi son plus haut niveau depuis 18 mois, la forte baisse des rendements des bons du Trésor pesant sur la devise américaine.
Le billet vert perd 0,43% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , tandis que l'euro gagne 0,45% à 1,1206 dollar .
PÉTROLE Les cours du pétrole peinent à trouver une orientation, les investisseurs analysant les perspectives d'approvisionnement et les tensions persistantes au Moyen-Orient.
Le Brent cède 0,06% à 106,00 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) avance de 2,68% à 97,64 dollars.
L'Agence internationale de l'énergie (AIE) [USN:L6N46110V TEXT:"a déclaré"] jeudi que le volume total des stocks qui seront mis sur le marché dépasserait les 400 millions de barils initialement convenus en mars, ses membres s’étant engagés à accélérer la mise à disposition des volumes restants.
La tension reste toujours palpable, l'armée iranienne [USN:L8N4611EX TEXT:"ayant déclaré"] jeudi qu'un pétrolier "en infraction" était en feu dans la partie orientale du détroit d'Ormuz, selon un communiqué relayé par les médias d'État.
A SUIVRE LE 16 OCTOBRE : [USN:L8N45V1FC]
(Certaines données peuvent accuser un léger décalage)

items.title: CAS review: Sebi announces last 30-minute VWAP method for settlement
items.author: Khushboo Tiwari
items.summary: Sebi has revised the closing auction session framework, adopting the last 30-minute VWAP for derivatives settlement and changing trading hours from December 7, 2026.
items.body: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Thursday announced the much-awaited revisions to the closing auction session (CAS) framework, introducing changes to the settlement methodology, trading timings, and the transition of unexecuted iceberg orders. An iceberg order is a large order split into smaller orders where only a fraction of the total quantity is visible in the order book displayed to the public. The revised framework will take effect from December 7, 2026, except for changes relating to the transition of unexecuted limit and iceberg orders from the continuous trading session (CTS) to CAS, which will come into force from February 8, 2027. Retaining the earlier method, the settlement price of index derivatives will be based on the volume-weighted average prices (VWAP) of constituent securities during the last 30 minutes of the CTS (3.00 pm to 3.30 pm) in the equity cash segment. For expiring stock derivatives, clearing corporations will determine settlement prices using the VWAP of the underlying stock during the last 30 minutes of the CTS across all stock exchanges. Exchanges will provide the VWAP and quantity traded to clearing corporations and continuously disseminate indicative values to market participants in real time during this period. Under the revised timings, CAS will operate as a separate 10-minute session from 3:30 pm to 3:40 pm on all trading days. The order-entry period will close randomly between 3:38 pm and 3:40 pm. Trading in index derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm on regular trading days, but contracts expiring that day will stop trading at 3:30 pm. Trading in stock derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm, including on expiry days. The post-close session in the cash segment will run from 3:50 pm to 4 pm, with trades executed at the closing prices of securities. CAS became effective on August 3 and saw an uproar from the trading community over the settlement price, sharp spikes, and low liquidity. The latest changes were announced following a consultation paper that received over 20,000 suggestions, which was followed by deliberations of the market regulator’s Secondary Market Advisory Committee on Thursday. The regulator had also proposed a blended mechanism, on which several market participants had raised concerns, given the low liquidity in the window. Traders and brokers had favoured the 30-minute VWAP method stating that participants were more familiar with this mechanism and that it was more transparent and operationally well understood. On Thursday, Sebi also specified how unexecuted orders will move from the CTS to CAS. Pending limit orders will generally be carried forward, except stop-loss orders and orders priced beyond the applicable CAS price bands. Unexecuted iceberg orders within the applicable price bands will be converted into fully disclosed limit orders (at fixed/pre-determined price), unless market participants opt out when placing the original orders. These converted orders will have lower time priority than other limit orders carried forward from the continuous session, but higher priority than limit orders placed during CAS. At present, CAS is a 20 minute window from 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm where the reference price calculation and transition from CTS to CAS happens from 3:15 pm to 3:20 pm. In this period, no order entry is allowed. The next five minutes order entry period remains. From 3.25 pm to 3.30 pm, the order entry period is restricted to limit orders only, and no modifications or cancellations of market orders are allowed. In this period, trading closes randomly in the last two minutes. In its consultation paper, Sebi had also proposed prohibiting cancellation of limit orders placed beyond 1 per cent range of the reference price during CAS. However, the regulator skipped this change in the final circular.

items.title: Putin says Ukrainian refinery attacks caused little damage, Interfax reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that recent Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries had not caused significant damage and vowed that Moscow would respond, Interfax reported.
items.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that recent Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries had not caused significant damage and vowed that Moscow would respond, Interfax reported.
"They hit here and there. Nothing particularly significant. Nevertheless they are carrying on," Putin said.
His comments came after a major Ukrainian drone attack [USN:L8N4610DI TEXT:"ignited a fire"] at an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region on Thursday morning, according to the regional governor.
It was the first confirmed Ukrainian attack on a Russian energy facility since US President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire.
On Wednesday, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak [USN:S8N45E0CE TEXT:"said"] that Ukraine had attacked oil refineries in the Saratov and Ryazan regions, although Ukraine denied any involvement.

items.title: Patria: cómo consultar los US$150 del Bono Integral que comenzó a pagarse en Venezuela
items.author: Fátima Romero
items.summary: El pago del Bono de Ingreso Integral de octubre de 2026 comenzó el miércoles a través de la Plataforma Patria.
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — El pago del Bono de Ingreso Integral de octubre comenzó el miércoles 14 a través de la Plataforma Patria, con un monto de 131.550,00 bolívares, equivalentes a US$150 a la tasa de 877,00 bolívares del Banco Central de Venezuela (BCV). Ver más: Inflación de septiembre 2026 en América Latina, país por país, de México hasta Argentina La cifra representa un aumento de 4,40% en moneda nacional frente a septiembre, cuando el beneficio se pagó en 126.000,00 bolívares. Los beneficiarios son los trabajadores activos de la Administración Pública de Venezuela y los jubilados que cobran cestatickets (bono de alimentación). La entrega arrancó por el personal de Educación y Salud y sigue este jueves 15 en el resto de las instituciones públicas. En ambos sectores, el personal activo recibe US$150 y los jubilados 133; el mismo esquema aplica para la Corpoelec. Quedan pendientes de asignación el estipendio del movimiento Somos Venezuela, sin fecha anunciada, y el Bono de Corresponsabilidad y Formación, dirigido a los docentes que participan en procesos de formación con la Universidad Nacional del Magisterio (UNEM). Las próximas entregas podrían extenderse a alcaldías, cuerpos policiales, Metro de Caracas y otros organismos públicos, informaron canales independientes a la plataforma. Este bono se acredita automáticamente en el Monedero Patria, por lo que no hace falta escanearlo, activarlo o enviar mensajes de texto al 3532. Ver más: FMI revela proyección positiva para Venezuela en 2026: ¿de qué depende su crecimiento? Cada beneficiario recibe la confirmación por un SMS del número corto de la plataforma o por la aplicación móvil oficial de VeMonedero. Para verificar el depósito basta con entrar a patria.org.ve con usuario y contraseña y revisar la sección Monedero , donde aparecen el saldo y los movimientos recientes. Como la acreditación avanza por etapas durante la jornada, si el pago no aparece todavía no hay ninguna gestión que hacer, solo conviene revisar la plataforma más adelante. Una vez acreditado, el saldo puede transferirse de inmediato a una cuenta de banca pública o privada vinculada al titular, o usarse para pagar servicios básicos, recargar el teléfono y comprar en comercios afiliados a la red BioPago. Precisamente porque el pago no requiere gestiones, Patria advierte que no hay que abrir mensajes ni enlaces que prometan “liberar” o “activar” el beneficio, ni entregar claves o datos personales: toda la información oficial se publica en los canales del Sistema Patria. El bono cubre cerca del 15% de la canasta básica. La Cesta Cedice, que reúne 61 bienes y servicios para un hogar de tres personas, se ubicó en septiembre en US$974,48 (833.822,94 bolívares), según el Observatorio de Gasto Público de Cedice Libertad. La diferencia es mayor aún en moneda nacional, porque mientras el bono subió 4,40%, los precios de la cesta aumentaron 12,05% en el mes y acumulan 242,87% en lo que va de año.

items.title: Huesos hallados en cueva iraquí apuntan a existencia de violencia y compasión entre los neandertales
items.author: Will Dunham
items.creator: Will Dunham
items.summary: Los huesos de un neandertal hallados en una cueva de la región del Kurdistán iraquí aportan pruebas tanto de violencia como de compasión en los parientes evolutivos más cercanos de nuestra especie, ya que presentan una herida aparentemente causada por un ataque con lanza, así como signos de una lesión anterior no mortal que podría haber dado lugar a cuidados compasivos.
items.body:
Los huesos de un neandertal hallados en una cueva de la región del Kurdistán iraquí aportan pruebas tanto de violencia como de compasión en los parientes evolutivos más cercanos de nuestra especie, ya que presentan una herida aparentemente causada por un ataque con lanza, así como signos de una lesión anterior no mortal que podría haber dado lugar a cuidados compasivos.
Los investigadores han descubierto en la cueva de Shanidar, en los montes Zagros del norte de Irak, un esqueleto parcial de un neandertal de unos 45 años que incluía un omóplato izquierdo o escápula con un agujero circular de 15 milímetros de ancho, indicativo de una puñalada profundamente penetrante.
Los huesos de este individuo, al que denominan "Shanidar A", fueron desenterrados bajo unos 7,5 metros de rocas y sedimentos en el interior de la cueva y datan de hace unos 75.000 años. Los investigadores no pudieron determinar su sexo.
Los investigadores afirmaron que la forma de la herida sugiere que fue causada por una estocada contundente con una lanza de madera afilada —un tipo de arma que se sabe que utilizaban los neandertales—, en lugar de una lanza con punta de piedra. Se trataba de un arma empleada en la caza de grandes mamíferos, que constituían una importante fuente de alimento.
"La lanza habría atravesado la piel y los músculos principales, sobre todo los pectorales, así como la caja torácica y los músculos entre las costillas, y el pulmón", explicó la antropóloga biológica Emma Pomeroy, de la Universidad de Cambridge (Inglaterra), autora principal del estudio publicado el jueves en la revista Scientific Reports.
"La ubicación podría parecerse al tipo de 'disparo al corazón' que utilizan los cazadores para matar con rapidez a los animales perforándoles el corazón, pero eso es un poco especulativo. Consideramos que los disparos al corazón son una estrategia de caza tanto en la actualidad como en el registro arqueológico. Los neandertales habrían sabido que esto provocaría una muerte rápida", señaló Pomeroy.
Graeme Barker, arqueólogo de la Universidad de Cambridge y coautor del estudio, que ha dirigido las excavaciones de la cueva de Shanidar desde 2015, señaló que el escenario más probable es la violencia interpersonal.
Los investigadores ven probable que la violencia se produjera entre miembros de un grupo concreto de neandertales o entre miembros de grupos rivales de neandertales, pero consideran menos probable que se tratara de un ataque de un Homo sapiens o de una lesión accidental.
Los investigadores encontraron fragmentos de hueso desplazados por el impacto del arma. La lesión indicaba que la lanza entró desde arriba con una trayectoria descendente, penetrando en la cavidad torácica izquierda desde la parte delantera y atravesando el cuerpo antes de perforar la escápula, lo que provocó una muerte rápida.
OTRA LESIÓN Además de la escápula, los investigadores encontraron algunas costillas, una mano derecha casi completa y siete dientes, en su mayoría de la parte delantera de la mandíbula inferior, pertenecientes a Shanidar A.
Los dientes mostraban indicios de que este neandertal sobrevivió a una lesión brutal al menos un año antes de su muerte: un golpe en la cara que le provocó la fractura y la pérdida de los dientes frontales. Un diente estaba partido, con la mitad girada dentro de la boca y los demás desplazados de su posición.
"El dolor debió de ser extremo, y las necesidades básicas como comer y beber le habrían resultado difíciles, lo que tal vez significara que Shanidar A necesitaba que le trituraran la comida y poder descansar. Es probable que Shanidar A necesitara cierto cuidado por parte de los miembros del grupo para satisfacer algunas necesidades básicas durante su recuperación", afirmó Pomeroy.
Shanidar A fue uno de los cinco neandertales —cuatro adultos y un bebé— cuyos cuerpos fueron colocados tras un pilar rocoso en la cueva, formando un grupo funerario en el que los fallecimientos ocurrieron con un intervalo de aproximadamente una generación. La cueva fue ocupada por neandertales durante decenas de miles de años como campamento estacional y, más tarde, por el Homo sapiens.
Los neandertales tenían una complexión más robusta que los Homo sapiens, con arcos superciliares más pronunciados. Vivían como cazadores-recolectores y habitaron Eurasia, desde la costa atlántica hasta los montes Urales, desde hace unos 400.000 años hasta poco después de hace 40.000 años, desapareciendo tras el establecimiento del Homo sapiens en la región.
Las dos especies se cruzaron, por lo que las poblaciones humanas modernas no africanas portan ADN neandertal residual.
La cueva, con vista al valle del río Gran Zab, ha sido una fuente de información sobre los neandertales desde los años 50, y ahora Shanidar A ofrece nuevos datos sobre su comportamiento.
"Vemos pruebas de dos facetas contrapuestas de la naturaleza humana —el cuidado y la violencia— yuxtapuestas en un mismo individuo", afirmó Pomeroy.
"Hoy en día vemos pruebas a nuestro alrededor de que tanto la violencia como el cuidado son aspectos de nuestro comportamiento humano, y esto también lo vemos aquí, en Shanidar A", afirmó Pomeroy.
"Los neandertales eran como nosotros en muchos aspectos, tanto en lo bueno como en lo malo, y este hallazgo realmente lo pone de relieve, contradiciendo los estereotipos que describen a los neandertales como hombres y mujeres de las cavernas poco inteligentes e indiferentes", agregó.

items.title: What does Alberta's referendum on separation from Canada mean?
items.author: Maria Cheng
items.creator: Maria Cheng
items.summary: Alberta is holding a nonbinding referendum on Monday to ask residents if they want to remain part of Canada, marking the first time the oil-rich province has ever put the question of separation to the public. Polls have consistently shown most Albertans — about 70% — want to stay in Canada, with roughly a quarter of residents supporting an independent Alberta.
items.body:
Alberta is holding a nonbinding [USN:L6N41X1E1 TEXT:"referendum "]on Monday to ask residents if they want to remain part of Canada, marking the first time the oil-rich province has ever put the question of separation to the public. Polls have consistently shown most Albertans — about 70% — want to stay in Canada, with roughly a quarter of residents supporting an [USN:L6N42Y0YK TEXT:"independent Alberta."]
WHAT WILL RESIDENTS BE ASKED? There are 10 questions, each with its own color-coded ballot. The last ballot voters see is question 10, on whether Alberta should remain a Canadian province or start the legal process required to hold a binding referendum on separation. A simple majority in favor of separation could trigger that process. There are [USN:L6N3ZF146 TEXT:"nine other nonbinding questions "]about immigration, access to provincial services — including education, social care and healthcare — and voter identification requirements.
WHY IS ALBERTA HAVING THIS REFERENDUM? Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said in May it was “time to have a vote, understand the will of Albertans on this subject, and move on,” when she announced the government would add a question on separation. Smith’s decision followed months of campaigning by a small but vocal group of separatists, who argue Alberta’s energy wealth is subsidizing poorer parts of the country and that bureaucracy in Ottawa has stifled the province’s economy. Some members of the group had backed Smith's candidacy for premier. Smith says she voted for Alberta to remain in Canada during advance polling, according to a video she posted on social media on Wednesday.
HAVE THERE BEEN PREVIOUS SEPARATIST REFERENDUMS IN CANADA? Yes, but not in Alberta. The majority French-speaking province of Quebec has had two referendums, in 1980 and 1995. Quebecers voted to remain in Canada both times, but by the slimmest of margins in 1995. The separatist Parti Quebecois won a provincial election [USN:L1N4590X4 TEXT:"earlier this month"] and has pledged to hold a third referendum, but only after US President Donald Trump has left office and if the party holds a majority. The PQ was elected with a minority government on October 5, meaning it will rely on smaller parties to pass legislation.
Canada is a federation of 10 provinces and three territories. While Ottawa is responsible for matters of national interest, such as defense, trade and foreign policy, the provinces and territories hold significant power over medical care, education and land rights.
WHEN WILL THE RESULTS BE KNOWN? Polls are scheduled to close at 8 p.m. on Monday (0200 GMT on Tuesday). Elections Alberta says it will count ballots by hand and that the question on separation will be counted first.
It will publish results on the Elections Alberta website as they are received, and unofficial results are expected within 48 hours after voting ends.
WHAT HAPPENS IF MOST ALBERTANS VOTE TO START THE PROCESS OF LEAVING CANADA? Smith has said she will respect the result and quickly begin the process to hold a legally binding referendum. But separation would not happen imminently. After the 1995 Quebec referendum, Canada's Parliament passed the Clarity Act in 2000, which says talks about secession can only be triggered if there is a clear majority from the public, without specifying the necessary threshold. The act also states provinces and territories have no unilateral right to leave Canada and that a constitutional amendment negotiated by provincial, territorial and federal governments is required.
First Nations groups have objected to the idea of an independent Alberta, as their land treaties with Canada predate Alberta's entry into Confederation. In May, an Alberta court judge [USN:L6N41R10Y TEXT:"ruled "]the province’s chief electoral officer was wrong to allow separatists to collect signatures requesting a referendum, because the process should have prompted a consultation with Indigenous peoples whose rights might be violated by separation. Alberta has appealed the decision.
WHAT HAS PRIME MINISTER MARK CARNEY SAID ABOUT THE REFERENDUM? Carney, who was largely raised in Alberta, has previously said “the best place for Alberta is in Canada” and that the country cannot succeed if it's divided. He released a video on Canadian Thanksgiving, October 12, saying national unity is critical as Canada fights threats from abroad, including a [USN:SPN44J009 TEXT:"trade war"] with the US. Carney has campaigned for Alberta to remain in Canada.

items.title: How are Yemen’s Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia so effectively?
items.author: The Straits Times
items.summary: LONDON, Oct 15 - Houthi militants who control northwestern Yemen have in the past week attacked Riyadh international airport and hit the headquarters of Saudi Aramco, the world's largest oil company, in air assaults that have laid bare Saudi Arabia's vulnerability to threats from its enemy next door.
items.body:
How are Yemen’s Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia so effectively?
Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox

A satellite image taken on July 2, 2026, shows the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in Dhahran before it was attacked on Tuesday night, October 13, causing what the kingdom's energy ministry said in a statement was a limited fire. Pleiades Neo © Airbus DS 2026/Handout via REUTERS THIS IMAGE HAS BEEN SUPPLIED BY A THIRD PARTY. NO RESALES. NO ARCHIVES. MANDATORY CREDIT. Verification lines: The headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in Dhahran was attacked on Tuesday night, October 13, causing what the kingdom's energy ministry said in a statement was a limited fire. The ministry also said the attack caused no injuries or death. Coordinates: 26.31217384734252, 50.131677108398165 TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY

Published   Oct 16, 2026, 12:06 AM

Updated   Oct 16, 2026, 12:06 AM

Set as preferred source

LONDON, Oct 15 - Houthi militants who control northwestern Yemen have in the past week attacked Riyadh international airport and hit the headquarters of Saudi Aramco, the world's largest oil company, in air assaults that have laid bare Saudi Arabia's vulnerability to threats from its enemy next door.
The attacks are shattering the illusion of Saudi Arabia as a safe international investment hub as it tries to attract foreign money and diversify away from oil.
This nightmare scenario for a key US ally in the Gulf has been years in the making, weapons and regional experts say.

They attribute Saudi Arabia's vulnerability to a ragtag group of Yemeni fighters to a perfect storm of factors that include Tehran helping the Houthis reach near self-sufficiency in producing and deploying advanced weapons, and the impact of the US war on Iran that has depleted stocks of interceptors.
TRAINING TO SELF-SUFFICIENCY BY IRAN
Iran has been giving weapons, money and training to the Houthis, known formally as Ansar Allah, for more than a decade, although Tehran has officially denied arming the Houthis in violation of a UN arms embargo.

While Iran has come under its own financial and military strains due to war and sanctions, the Houthis have learned – with Iranian help – how to assemble their own weapons, including drones and missiles, the experts interviewed by Reuters said.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards and members of Iran's other ally, Lebanese Hezbollah, initially gave the Houthis knowledge of missile systems and their operation, said Andreas Krieg, senior security studies lecturer at King's College London.
"Former Yemeni military engineers and a growing generation of locally trained specialists have helped institutionalise these capabilities," he said.

"Tehran has not simply supplied the Houthis with weapons. It has helped create an indigenous military-industrial learning process that becomes progressively harder to dismantle, even if direct Iranian supply routes are disrupted."
Iranian analysts said that the Houthis have in this way become one of the most cost-effective and valuable military proxies of Iran.
"The Revolutionary Guards were forward-looking. They looked at what happened if the Houthis couldn't receive equipment or weapons directly (from Iran), or if these were seized by US-allied forces," said Hamid Nikou, a former political advisor to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Nikou said this strategy included teaching the Houthis how to assemble dual-use parts to make drones and even ballistic missiles.
"Iran has basically taught the Houthis how to fish," Nikou said.
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting against the Houthis in Yemen says it has intercepted a number of missiles fired by the Houthis at Saudi cities, and that it has destroyed 127 Houthi weapons storage facilities and launch platforms.
Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki told a press conference the Houthis had acquired advanced military technology with the help of "regional actors," including ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats.
DIVERSIFYING WEAPONS IMPORTS AND TECHNOLOGY
A key strength of the Houthis in building their own weapons is that they don't rely solely on Iranian-made equipment or imports coming from Iran.
The Conflict Armament Research organization said in a report this week that the Houthis were attempting to make advanced medium-range ballistic missiles using parts shipped from China, after Yemen's internationally recognised government seized one such shipment.
"China has emerged as a particularly important commercial source, while Iran continues to provide specialised military technology, technical expertise and components that are difficult to obtain commercially," Krieg said.
The Houthis have also experimented with artificial intelligence in efforts to improve their weapons' effectiveness.
Anthropic said last month that "a cell of threat actors based in northern Yemen" had used its Claude AI assistant to help develop software for a guided rocket, a planned ballistic missile with a range of more than 2,000 km (1,240 miles) and a missile variant incorporating a hypersonic glide vehicle.
WAR FATIGUE, DEPLETED MUNITIONS
While the Houthis have improved their weapons production, US allies in the region have seen their air defences stretched since the war that began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
The United States has used large amounts of the missile interceptors it deploys in the region to protect its bases and its allies, which include Israel and Gulf countries, leaving some vulnerable, Saudi Arabia in particular.
"Saudi Arabia, in terms of the sophistication of the military and the development of an integrated air defence network, is not really yet at the level of either Israel or Ukraine, and it just has a very tough job to do," said Farzan Sabet, a Middle East expert at the Geneva Graduate Institute.
Saudi Arabia's sheer size makes defence against air attacks harder than defending Israel or a US base, he said.
WAR EXPERIENCE
The Houthis have learned from the increased levels of violence in the region in recent years, Sabet said.
A Yemeni civil war, in which the Houthis battled Saudi-backed forces from 2014, settled into a shaky ceasefire in 2022. But after Israel’s assault on Gaza in 2023, which followed deadly Hamas-led attacks on Israel, the Houthis began firing rockets at Israel and targeting shipping through the Red Sea.
The fallout from the US-Iran war this year reignited the Yemeni civil war, by which time the Houthis had developed new capabilities.
"They haven't been sitting still," Sabet said. "They were basically diversifying their supply chains... and as they gain operational experience, they're able to make those weapons more sophisticated." REUTERS

items.title: Competition Bureau says Quebec real estate board violated abuse of dominance rules
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: The Competition Bureau says it has reached a settlement with Quebec’s real estate industry association to loosen restrictions that violated the Competition Act.
items.body: The Competition Bureau says it has reached a settlement with Quebec’s real estate industry association to loosen data-sharing restrictions that violated the Competition Act. The watchdog says the Quebec Professional Association of Real Estate Brokers and its subsidiary, Société Centris, broke abuse of dominance rules by refusing to provide its members with a real estate data feed, while also restricting how such data could be used. The bureau says lack of access to that data was likely meant to “impede innovation and limit competition in the real estate brokerage services market.” As part of a consent agreement reached with the association, it will now provide its members with a real estate data feed containing information about sale prices, listing history and property characteristics. Pierre-Olivier Simard, president of the QPAREB board of directors, says in a statement that the solution is “tailored to the Quebec reality,” given that Quebec’s laws are more restrictive than those in the rest of Canada when it comes to the protection of personal information. The bureau launched its investigation into QPAREB’s data-sharing practices in 2023 after a previous case against the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board, in which the watchdog challenged rules that prevented brokers in that region from sharing certain real estate data with their clients through secure online platforms. --- Sammy Hudes, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 15, 2026.

items.title: How are Yemen’s Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia so effectively?
items.author: John Davison
items.creator: John Davison
items.summary: Houthi militants who control northwestern Yemen have in the past week attacked Riyadh international airport and hit the headquarters of Saudi Aramco, the world's largest oil company, in air assaults that have laid bare Saudi Arabia's vulnerability to threats from its enemy next door.
items.body:
Houthi [USN:L6N4010N9 TEXT:"militants"] who control northwestern Yemen have in the past week [USN:L6N4600NM TEXT:"attacked"] Riyadh international airport and hit the headquarters of Saudi Aramco, the world's largest oil company, in air assaults that have laid bare Saudi Arabia's vulnerability to threats from its enemy next door.
The attacks are shattering the illusion of Saudi Arabia as a safe [USN:L6N4600CJ TEXT:"international investment hub"] as it tries to attract foreign money and diversify away from oil.
This nightmare scenario for a key US ally in the Gulf has been years in the making, weapons and regional experts say.
They attribute [USN:L1N46108L TEXT:"Saudi Arabia's vulnerability"] to a ragtag group of Yemeni fighters to a perfect storm of factors that include Tehran helping the Houthis reach near self-sufficiency in producing and deploying advanced weapons, and the impact of the US war on Iran that has depleted stocks of interceptors.
TRAINING TO SELF-SUFFICIENCY BY IRAN Iran has been giving [USN:L1N43P0D6 TEXT:"weapons, money and training"] to the Houthis, known formally as Ansar Allah, for more than a decade, although Tehran has officially denied arming the Houthis in violation of a UN arms embargo.
While Iran has come under its own financial and military strains due to war and sanctions, the Houthis have learned – with Iranian help – how to assemble their own weapons, including drones and missiles, the experts interviewed by Reuters said.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards and members of Iran's other ally, Lebanese Hezbollah, initially gave the Houthis knowledge of missile systems and their operation, said Andreas Krieg, senior security studies lecturer at King's College London.
"Former Yemeni military engineers and a growing generation of locally trained specialists have helped institutionalise these capabilities," he said.
"Tehran has not simply supplied the Houthis with weapons. It has helped create an indigenous military-industrial learning process that becomes progressively harder to dismantle, even if direct Iranian supply routes are disrupted."
Iranian analysts said that the Houthis have in this way become one of the most cost-effective and valuable military proxies of Iran.
"The Revolutionary Guards were forward-looking. They looked at what happened if the Houthis couldn't receive equipment or weapons directly (from Iran), or if these were seized by US-allied forces," said Hamid Nikou, a former political advisor to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Nikou said this strategy included teaching the Houthis how to assemble dual-use parts to make drones and even ballistic missiles.
"Iran has basically taught the Houthis how to fish," Nikou said.
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting against the Houthis in Yemen says it has intercepted a number of missiles fired by the Houthis at Saudi cities, and that it has destroyed 127 Houthi weapons storage facilities and launch platforms.
Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki [USN:L1N4610M8 TEXT:"told a press conference"] the Houthis had acquired advanced military technology with the help of "regional actors," including ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats.
DIVERSIFYING WEAPONS IMPORTS AND TECHNOLOGY A key strength of the Houthis in building their own weapons is that they don't rely solely on Iranian-made equipment or imports coming from Iran.
The Conflict Armament Research organization said in a report this week that the Houthis were attempting to make advanced medium-range ballistic missiles using parts shipped from China, after Yemen's internationally recognised government seized one such shipment.
"China has emerged as a particularly important commercial source, while Iran continues to provide specialised military technology, technical expertise and components that are difficult to obtain commercially," Krieg said.
The Houthis have also experimented with artificial intelligence in efforts to improve their weapons' effectiveness.
Anthropic said last month that "a cell of threat actors based in northern Yemen" had used its Claude AI assistant to help develop software for a guided rocket, a planned ballistic missile with a range of more than 2,000 km (1,240 miles) and a missile variant incorporating a hypersonic glide vehicle.
WAR FATIGUE, DEPLETED MUNITIONS While the Houthis have improved their weapons production, US allies in the region have seen their air defences stretched since the war that began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
The United States has used large amounts of the missile interceptors it deploys in the region to protect its bases and its allies, which include Israel and Gulf countries, leaving some vulnerable, Saudi Arabia in particular.
"Saudi Arabia, in terms of the sophistication of the military and the development of an integrated air defence network, is not really yet at the level of either Israel or Ukraine, and it just has a very tough job to do," said Farzan Sabet, a Middle East expert at the Geneva Graduate Institute.
Saudi Arabia's sheer size makes defence against air attacks harder than defending Israel or a US base, he said.
WAR EXPERIENCE The Houthis have learned from the increased levels of violence in the region in recent years, Sabet said.
A Yemeni civil war, in which the Houthis battled Saudi-backed forces from 2014, settled into a shaky ceasefire in 2022. But after Israel’s assault on Gaza in 2023 , which followed deadly Hamas-led attacks on Israel, the Houthis began firing rockets at Israel and targeting shipping through the Red Sea.
The fallout from the US-Iran war this year reignited the Yemeni civil war, by which time the Houthis had developed new capabilities.
"They haven't been sitting still," Sabet said. "They were basically diversifying their supply chains... and as they gain operational experience, they're able to make those weapons more sophisticated."

items.title: IEA to speed up oil stocks release including over 20 million barrels of diesel
items.author: Forrest Crellin, Robert Harvey, Pietro Lombardi
items.creator: Forrest Crellin, Robert Harvey, Pietro Lombardi
items.summary: The International Energy Agency agreed on Thursday to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to the market as soon as possible and any oil remaining from a record emergency reserves release pledged in March to help supply and cool soaring prices.
items.body:
The International Energy Agency agreed on Thursday to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to the market as soon as possible and any oil remaining from a record emergency reserves release pledged in March to help supply and cool soaring prices.
US President Donald Trump has pressed European Union countries to draw down reserves or face a potential US diesel export ban as he seeks to lower prices ahead of November 3 [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"].
Prices for diesel have surged to record highs in many markets on disrupted supply from the war in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine conflict, posing inflation and cost-of-living threats to governments and consumers.
The 32-nation IEA's board met on Thursday to discuss the scale and timing of stock releases.
"The IEA governing board reaffirmed its commitment to continue delivering on the March 2026 Collective Action in response to the Strait of Hormuz crisis," it said in a statement after the meeting.
In March, countries had pledged to release more than 400 million barrels of crude and oil products as prices soared.
On Thursday members "agreed to accelerate the release of the remaining volumes, with specific plans already in place, including over 20 million barrels of diesel as soon as possible."
SOME DISAPPOINTMENT OVER LACK OF EXTRA BARRELS The figure of 20 million barrels of diesel is lower than the [USN:B5N44301Y TEXT:"50 million barrels"] that had been considered earlier, according to a source familiar with details of the discussion.
Reuters reported this month that EU governments were discussing a [USN:S8N43A07P TEXT:"French proposal"] for the release of 50 million barrels of diesel alongside 50 million barrels of crude from IEA members.
After the IEA statement on Thursday, Europe's benchmark gas oil contract, a fuel type which includes diesel , ticked higher to $1,430.75 per metric ton as of 1512 GMT, although it was still lower on the day.
"Gas oil prices ticking higher suggests some disappointment that we are not seeing any firm commitment to add additional barrels here and now," said Ole Hansen, an analyst at Saxo Bank.
"Prices are high but we are not dealing with any shortages as such, so with that in mind it probably makes sense to keep the powder dry for now."
The IEA, which coordinates industrialised nations' releases of oil from emergency stocks, said some members had already released more than they pledged in March and that others planned to do so.
Approximately 330 million barrels have been released so far, the IEA said.
The United States told fellow IEA members that current release plans do not go far enough to quell rising fuel prices, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
The White House, when asked by Reuters if it was unhappy with the IEA's commitment to draw down reserves, provided the IEA's statement from Thursday on the releases.
Spain [USN:L8N4610R5 TEXT:"said on Thursday"] it would release 4.4 million barrels from strategic reserves in October without specifying what it would release.
Spain so far has released 3.7 million of the 11.5 million barrels it pledged in March.

items.title: Nasdaq reports network disruption, US equities data feeds impacted
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Nasdaq , home to some of the biggest US tech companies, is experiencing a network disruption at its Carteret facility in New Jersey that is causing intermittent data gaps across all of its US equities markets, the exchange operator said on Thursday.
items.body:
Nasdaq (NDAQ.O) , home to some of the biggest US tech companies, is experiencing a network disruption at its Carteret facility in New Jersey that is causing intermittent data gaps across all of its US equities markets, the exchange operator said on Thursday.
The technical issue is affecting multiple multicast groups and impacting both hardware and software feeds for Nasdaq, Nasdaq Texas and Nasdaq PSX, according to an alert issued by the company at 11:27:50 a.m. ET.
Both the primary "A" and secondary "B" feeds originating from the Carteret facility have been compromised by the outage, it said. Nasdaq has advised clients to switch their systems to unaffected backup feeds originating from its Chicago facility to ensure market access.
The exchange operator also instructed clients experiencing data gaps to submit recovery requests for any missing data.
"Nasdaq is actively investigating the issue," it said. "We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience."
Nasdaq did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment seeking further clarification.
Technical glitches on exchanges can roil markets, dampen traders' confidence and attract scrutiny from the Securities and Exchange Commission.
While Nasdaq's electronic platforms are typically reliable, the exchange operator has faced several notable technical glitches in recent years that briefly affected market activity.
In March 2024, a severe connectivity issue struck the exchange shortly before the opening bell, disrupting premarket trading and impairing the software system responsible for matching buy and sell orders for more than two hours.
Shares of Nasdaq, which lists Apple (AAPL.O) , Tesla (TSLA.O) and Nvidia (NVDA.O) among thousands of other companies, were unaffected by the network disruption. They have fallen about 3.8% so far in 2026.

items.title: Bitcoin cae por debajo de US$80.000 por primera vez en casi un mes: las razones
items.author: Emma Haidar, Sidhartha Shukla
items.summary: Las criptomonedas se encuentran atrapadas entre dos fuerzas: el optimismo de los analistas de activos digitales, por un lado, y una tendencia defensiva generalizada en los mercados especulativos, por ...
items.body: Bloomberg — El bitcoin cayó brevemente por debajo de los US$80.000 por primera vez en casi un mes, arrastrado por un retroceso generalizado de los activos de riesgo, ya que una venta masiva impulsada por la IA en Wall Street socavó el intento de las criptomonedas de reconstruir un tono alcista. El mayor activo digital se debilitó al abrir a la baja las acciones estadounidenses, con el Nasdaq 100 cayendo hasta un 1,8% después de que los indicios de desaceleración en el crecimiento de los ingresos de Anthropic intensificaran las dudas sobre el sector de la inteligencia artificial. Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro cayeron a medida que los inversores buscaban refugio en ellos, mientras que los datos de precios al productor y las ventas minoristas mejores de lo esperado no lograron alterar las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal mantendrá las tasas de interés altas durante más tiempo. Ver más: Bitcoin cae hasta 2,3% mientras la inflación y las tasas presionan a los activos de riesgo Las criptomonedas se encuentran atrapadas entre dos fuerzas: el optimismo de los analistas de activos digitales, por un lado, y una tendencia defensiva generalizada en los mercados especulativos, por el otro. Jeff Anderson, director de STS Digital en EE.UU., afirmó que los datos de inflación “perjudicarán seriamente el apetito por el riesgo” a medida que los mercados entren en el período de restricción de la Reserva Federal, con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés “en un punto crítico”. El activo digital original cayó hasta un 2,4%, situándose en US$79.720, su nivel más bajo desde el 18 de septiembre. Posteriormente, bitcoin redujo la caída a medida que las acciones fluctuaban entre ganancias y pérdidas. Ver más: El Salvador cambia su apuesta cripto: Bukele recurre a stablecoins tras limitado uso del bitcoin en pagos Los operadores interpretan la caída como una señal de alerta de un posible descenso generalizado del precio de bitcoin, y se están alejando de los objetivos de precio anteriores de US$100.000. En la plataforma de opciones de criptomonedas Derive.xyz, la probabilidad de que bitcoin alcance los US$100.000 para Navidad cayó 2,8 puntos porcentuales, hasta el 9,7%, en las últimas 24 horas, según declaró Nick Forster, fundador de Derive.xyz. “Este retroceso inmediato en las apuestas alcistas a largo plazo, junto con una cobertura agresiva a corto plazo, muestra un cambio de régimen drástico, en el que los participantes institucionales están reevaluando rápidamente su exposición al riesgo macroeconómico a medida que el panorama de las tasas de interés vuelve a ser incierto”, añadió Forster. items.title: Israel says commercial goods no longer entering Gaza after merchants suspend coordination
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Israel said commercial goods were no longer entering Gaza over what it said was a dispute over taxes between local merchants and Hamas, shutting off a vital source of food and other goods in the territory where the population is dependent on aid.
items.body:
Israel said commercial goods were no longer entering Gaza over what it said was a dispute over taxes between local merchants and Hamas, shutting off a vital source of food and other goods in the territory where the population is dependent on aid.
COGAT, the Israeli military body that oversees humanitarian affairs in Gaza, made the announcement in a statement on Wednesday, citing what it said was a decision by Gazan merchants to stop coordinating with COGAT on the entry of commercial goods.
It said the Gazan merchants had told COGAT that they had made the decision in response to a 10,000 shekel ($3,220) fee imposed by Hamas on each truck entering Gaza and a demand for 30% of all of their sales in Gaza to be carried out in cash.
Hamas later said that the 10,000 shekel fee was a voluntary payment by wealthy Gazans to a national fund that seeks to provide for those in need such as widows and orphans. It also said that cash payments were encouraged due to what it described as an acute cash shortage in the war-torn territory.
A majority of Gazans are dependent on aid supplies, following three years of war, repeated displacement and severe restrictions imposed by Israel on aid deliveries.
A global hunger monitor in July warned that more than two thirds of Gazans could face acute hunger by the year-end. Around 2 million Gazans live in the territory, most in makeshift shelters.
Nahed Shhaibar, the head of the private transport union in Gaza, said that not a single truck carrying commercial products from Israel entered Gaza on Thursday. However, he said trucks carrying humanitarian aid had entered, as had trucks carrying commercial goods from Egypt via an Israeli-controlled crossing.
COGAT said the decision by Gazan merchants would cut the total number of trucks, which carry both humanitarian and commercial goods, entering Gaza each day to around 300 — or half.
Diplomats say that far fewer than 600 trucks normally enter Gaza each day. Shhaibar said the figure was closer to 300, with two thirds carrying commercial goods.
Israel is obliged under a US-mediated agreement to allow a minimum of 600 trucks carrying humanitarian aid to enter Gaza each day. However, it says it is required to allow only 600 trucks and that commercial goods are needed to supplement aid supplies.
($1 = 3.1038 shekels)

items.title: ASML's 'sold out' outlook forces investors to look beyond demand
items.author: Toby Sterling, Nathan Vifflin
items.creator: Toby Sterling, Nathan Vifflin
items.summary: In April, computer chip equipment maker ASML's CEO Christophe Fouquet told shareholders that Europe's most valuable company would avoid becoming the chip industry's bottleneck "by all possible means".
items.body:
In April, computer chip equipment maker ASML's CEO Christophe Fouquet told shareholders that Europe's most valuable company would avoid becoming the chip industry's bottleneck "by all possible means".
Six months later, Fouquet acknowledged ASML's supply of chip-printing tools used to make the advanced logic and memory chips powering the AI boom will [USN:L6N4600AA TEXT:"fall short"] of demand in both 2027 and 2028.
For customers, investors and ASML, whose shares have risen nearly 70% this year, the focus is shifting to whether the company can increase capacity fast enough to profit from the huge demand. At the same time, market jitters are increasing over the durability of the AI boom and forecasts that stretch years into the future.
"ASML itself is now the bottleneck," said Han Dieperink, chief investment officer at wealth management firm Aureus, which holds ASML shares, adding that management was openly acknowledging that planned 30% capacity additions in 2027 and in 2028 will not be enough.
Dieperink said discussions about future orders were already extending into 2029 and 2030, which he viewed as evidence that demand could continue to outstrip supply well beyond the current cycle.
THE VALUATION DEBATE ASML's plans to address the backlog include shortening assembly times, upgrading machines already operating in the field and introducing faster models. It had planned to raise annual capacity to 110 of its $200 million EUV lithography machines by 2028, but is now looking at adding perhaps a dozen more.
It is also expanding manufacturing capacity in [USN:L6N4510PI TEXT:"Eindhoven"], although the first phase is not expected to come online until 2029.
Fouquet reassured investors on one point on Wednesday: ASML's own supply chain, including key optical systems supplier Zeiss, is not the limiting factor.
Investors say uncertainties increase after 2028 and the company's valuation reflects that. Since June, even as financial analysts ratcheted up earnings estimates, ASML's stock price drifted lower on a relative basis to its future earnings.
Mark Sloan, Senior Analyst at Stonehage Fleming, whose Global Best Ideas fund has a 3.5% position in ASML, said a decline in the company's valuation to about 30 times forward earnings from more than 45 times in June had made the stock attractive given its growth prospects and market dominance.
"We are watching AI adoption and innovation, along with capital spending plans at key customers closely," he said. "We believe supply rather than demand is likely to remain ASML's key constraint."
ASML has said it will also benefit from price increases in 2027 and 2028.
AI SELLOFF FEARS Not all investors are convinced. Sceptics question whether the surge in spending on AI infrastructure will ultimately generate returns that justify the billions of dollars being invested today.
Chip stocks have also [USN:L6N4610MM TEXT:"come under pressure"] from concerns that higher interest rates could make financing large AI and data-centre projects more difficult. The cost of insuring against defaults in the US technology sector hit [USN:L1N46104Z TEXT:"record highs"] on Thursday.
Jefferies analyst Janardan Menon said concerns about financing AI investment, along with constraints on data-centre expansion such as power availability, could weigh on ASML. Its shares fell 5% on Thursday as part of a broader market selloff.
"The primary factor driving this derating is scepticism about very high 2028 and 2029 expectations," said Menon, adding ASML's price-to-earnings ratio could fall into the low 20s during a downturn.
WE DON'T WANT TO SAY 'WE'RE SOLD OUT' ASML's customers continue to jockey for access to its unrivaled high-end chipmaking tools. The company is now demanding sizeable down payments on orders, which CFO Roger Dassen said are "enough to hurt" if customers later try to cancel.
Top customer TSMC (2330.TW) , which makes chips for Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Apple (AAPL.O) , said in July it did not expect equipment supply to constrain its expansion plans. It maintained 2026 capital spending plans of $60 billion to $64 billion [USN:L1N461004 TEXT:"on Thursday"].
Samsung (005930.KS) , SK Hynix (000660.KS) and Micron (MU.O) have also been booking ASML capacity amid strong demand for AI memory chips.
Potential new customers could add further pressure. Elon Musk's proposed TeraFab project, which has yet to produce its first chip, could emerge as a significant buyer of advanced tools, while US restrictions on China remain a risk for sales of ASML's mid-range DUV tools. China is expected to account for about 20% of ASML's sales this year.
Despite strong demand, ASML is holding off on accepting orders for 2029 and 2030 while it assesses both customers' readiness and its own ability to meet future demand.
"We don't want now to accept orders from customer A, B, and C and then to tell customer D, who hasn't given orders yet for 2029 and 2030, sorry, we're sold out," Dassen told analysts on the post-earnings call.

WASHINGTON, Oct 15 : Nvidia and Apple each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private donations for the project.
The Adelson family, longtime financial supporters of Trump and his Republican Party, committed $25 million as well, as did billionaire Charles Ergen, co-founder and chairman of telecommunications company Dish Network, the report added. 
The president himself is not on the list, according to the Post.
Reuters has not verified the report. The White House said it would not release information about the donors, which spokesman Davis Ingle said "represent a wide array of great American companies."

"The same critics who are alleging fake conflicts of interests, would also complain if American taxpayers were footing the bill for these long-overdue renovations," Ingle told Reuters.
Nvidia said it was proud to make a donation to a nonpartisan trust that serves Americans. "As an American company, our support for the United States is paramount, and independent of any business interests," a spokesperson said.
Apple declined to comment.
The scale of the ballroom project and the administration’s handling of fundraising and disclosures have drawn criticism from watchdog groups and legal experts, who say it raises questions about transparency, donor influence and adherence to longstanding ethics and oversight norms.
Trump initially said he and wealthy donors would pay for the estimated $400 million project, but he later unsuccessfully sought $1 billion from Congress for an underground bunker and security features to harden the facility.
The Post reported that the "vast majority of the funds raised came from companies and wealthy individuals with interests before the federal government" and that half the total came from companies or executives of firms that have had federal government contracts in Trump's second White House term.
The planned ballroom is among several projects Trump is pursuing in his efforts to remake Washington with sweeping, unilateral changes that his opponents have challenged in court and called a power grab.
The US Supreme Court, in a 5-4 ruling in August, allowed Trump to continue construction of the ballroom while he challenges a judicial order that would halt much of the development. In a dissent, Chief Justice John Roberts said the project was "likely unlawful."
The ballroom, which Trump has said will seat 1,000 guests, has faced public backlash. Preservationists and opponents say Trump exceeded his authority by demolishing the historic East Wing, which housed the first lady's offices and the White House movie theater, to make room for the structure.
Trump says a planned 90,000-square-foot (8,360-square-meter) White House ballroom will include bomb shelters, medical facilities, defenses against drones and missiles and other security features. Confronted with criticism of the project, his administration now says the facility is needed for national security, an argument the president has also made about a proposed triumphal arch.

Source: Reuters

items.title: 米、ＡＩから「ＳＩ」への呼称変更主張　ＩＭＦ声明巡り＝財務次官
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Andrea Shalal

[バンコク　１５日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Andrea Shalal

[バンコク　１５日　ロイター] - ブラウン米財務次官（国際問題担当）は１５日、ロイターとのインタビューで、国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）が準備中の声明で、人工知能（ＡＩ）の名称を「スーパーインテリジェンス」（超知能、ＳＩ）に変更するよう求めていると明らかにした。関係者によると、米国は関連会合でも名称変更を主張し、参加者から驚きの声が上がったという。

トランプ大統領は今年９月、新名称を使用するよう政府機関に指示。ブラウン氏によると、ＩＭＦの運営委員会、国際通貨金融委員会（ＩＭＦＣ）が起草中の声明で、新しい用語を使用するかどうか協議しているという。

米国は今年、２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）の議長国を務めており、ブラウン氏は名称変更が定着することを望んでいると述べた。「ＳＩ」は技術をより適切に表現しており、変更は米国の明確な優先事項だと説明した。

名称変更が受け入れられずに米政権が声明を支持しない場合、ＩＭＦＣ議長のサウジアラビアのジャドアーン財務相が「議長声明」に切り替える可能性がある。関係者は、ＳＩやＡＩを直接は盛り込まず「新技術」とするような妥協案も考えられると指摘した。

ＩＭＦＣは１７日、ジャドアーン氏とＩＭＦのゲオルギエワ専務理事が記者会見を開き、声明を発表する予定。

items.title: How Aramco learned to keep pumping oil under fire
items.author: Dmitry Zhdannikov
items.creator: Dmitry Zhdannikov
items.summary: When attack drones struck Saudi Aramco's biggest oil pipeline last month, satellite images showed one of its pumping stations burnt to ashes. By the next day, scores of bulldozers were already building a new pipeline.
items.body:
When attack drones struck Saudi Aramco's (2222.SE) biggest oil pipeline last month, satellite images showed one of its pumping stations burnt to ashes. By the next day, scores of bulldozers were already building a new pipeline.
Within days pumping resumed.
The speed of the recovery illustrates how the world's biggest oil producer has transformed its ability to operate under attack after years of assaults on energy infrastructure across the region.
"Today, our teams can handle multiple incidents simultaneously, and we continue to build this capability," Saudi state oil firm Aramco's chief executive Amin Nasser told Reuters in an interview last week.
Nasser said Aramco has built specialised rapid-response teams, expanded emergency stockpiles for repairs and deployed drones to assess damage even while incidents are still unfolding.
Lessons on how to operate under fire came after drones and missiles hit Aramco's major oil processing facility in Abqaiq in 2019, temporarily knocking out half of Aramco's production.
"After Abqaiq in 2019, we came up with the idea of rapid response teams, or what we call zero-hour responders," Nasser said.
The company, long-viewed as one of the most technically advanced oil producers, then began to prepare for the possibility of multiple attacks on its facilities at the same time, Nasser said.
Those capabilities have been repeatedly tested since the US and Israel attacked Iran in February this year and Iran and its proxies retaliated with strikes that hit Middle Eastern [USN:L6N4610JI TEXT:"infrastructure"].
The firm's crisis-management capabilities were tested again on Tuesday when a Houthi attack struck the company's headquarters complex, [USN:L6N4600QH TEXT:"causing extensive damage"].
DRONES AND WAREHOUSES SPEED RECOVERY Saudi daily oil output dropped below 7 million barrels for most of the first six months of the war, down from over 10 million barrels before the war, according to data from the International Energy Agency.
Like other Gulf producers, Saudi Arabia's oil exports have been constrained by attacks on tankers and a shortage of ships restricting crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
Yet Aramco has managed to repair damaged facilities and restore operations quickly thanks to specialised response teams, years of contingency planning, drone technology and abundant spare parts.
Technology has allowed Aramco to compress the time between an attack and the start of repairs, Nasser said.
The company's response to incidents was now more than six times faster than the industry average, he added, meaning it often takes just days to restart a facility even after significant damage.
Normally, oil firms first contain an incident and then assess the damage, but Aramco begins assessment with drones while an incident is still unfolding, Nasser said.
"Inspection drones provide an exceptional level of visibility and detail," Nasser said. "By the time the situation is under control, we are ready to get to work."
Response teams can quickly send repair materials to a site before work begins, Nasser said.
Some 90% of materials needed for repairs are produced locally or held in a local warehouse as Aramco has spent years building up supply chains and inventories.
The ability to maintain production despite repeated attacks has become an important selling point with Aramco's customers, Nasser said.
"They see that Aramco is able to deliver under different scenarios."
While Saudi oil production recovered to about 8 million barrels a day in September, export routes remain vulnerable to disruptions beyond Aramco's control.
The company is studying possible alternative routes to the Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and Suez, Nasser said, without elaborating.
"Details will be disclosed if and when a final decision is made," he said.

[ワシントン　１５日　ロイター] - 米商務省が１５日発表した８月の企業在庫は、前月比０．４％増加し、エコノミスト予想と一致した。売上高が堅調に伸びる中、在庫も緩やかな増加となった。

items.title: ヒズボラ、レバノン押収の爆薬所有認め返還要求　「イスラエル攻撃用」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ベイルート １５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ベイルート １５日 ロイター] - イラン支援下にあるレバノンの武装組織ヒズボラに所属する議員は１５日、同国の治安部隊が先週押収した数百キログラムの爆薬について、ヒズボラのものだと明らかにした。政府が進めるヒズボラの武装解除を巡り、緊張が続いている。

レバノン当局は先週、東部ベカー地方の検問所で爆薬を積んだ車両を発見し、乗っていた２人を逮捕した。

当局は当時、車両が誰のものか明らかにしなかったため、国内では車爆弾による暗殺や、国内の不安定化を狙った別の攻撃に爆薬が使われるのではないかとの懸念が広がった。

ヒズボラのハサン・ファドララ議員は１５日、レバノン議会で記者団に対し、爆薬はイスラエルに対して使用する予定だったと説明した。イスラエル軍はレバノン領の広い範囲を制圧・占領している。

ファドララ氏によると、ヒズボラは直ちに治安機関に連絡し、車両と積み荷が同組織のものであると説明。爆薬などの返還と、拘束された２人の釈放を要求した。

同氏が所有を認めたことは、国内の全ての武器を国家の管理下に置くという政府の方針にもかかわらず、ヒズボラが国内で武器の輸送を継続していることを示している。

米国の仲介によるレバノンとイスラエルの協議で成立した合意に基づき、レバノン政府はヒズボラの武装解除を約束した。しかし、ヒズボラはイスラエル軍がレバノン領内にとどまる限り武装解除を拒否するとしており、イスラエルもレバノン南部各地で攻撃を続けている。

items.title: FBI, US Postal Service investigate suspicious mailings to election officials, lawmakers
items.author: David Shepardson
items.creator: David Shepardson
items.summary: The FBI and US Postal Service's law enforcement arm said on Thursday they were investigating suspicious mailings, including some sent to state election officials and lawmakers' offices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
items.body:
The FBI and US Postal Service's law enforcement arm said on Thursday they were investigating suspicious mailings, including some sent to state election officials and lawmakers' offices ahead of the November 3 [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"].
The FBI said some of the letters contained an unknown substance.
A spokesperson for Senator Alex Padilla, a California Democrat, said his office received a notification from the FBI that the US Postal Service intercepted a letter containing a suspicious substance mailed to one of Padilla's offices.
Brendan Donahue, a deputy chief inspector with the US Postal Inspection Service, said some of the letters had been intercepted and that an investigation was ongoing.
"We are committed to protecting our nation's election officials from threatening and dangerous mail. Any threat or attack on an election official is unacceptable," Donahue told reporters.
The National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors said late on Wednesday a series of suspicious letters was sent to state election offices.
The US House of Representatives sergeant at arms, the House's chief law enforcement officer, told staff in an email seen by Reuters that some letters containing suspicious white powder substances were received by public officials.
Earlier on Thursday, US Postmaster General David Steiner said USPS was "absolutely ready" to handle millions of ballots for the midterm elections that will determine control of the US Congress and other key races.
POSTAL SERVICE PLANS NEW MEASURES The Postal Service said this month it would take "extraordinary measures" for the 2026 election, including extending hours at some retail locations and expediting handling, extra deliveries and special pickups of ballots.
The extraordinary measures start October 24 "to expedite completed ballots to election offices during the final stretch of the election season," Steiner said, adding they include "local turnaround to bypass all processing when it's absolutely necessary to get ballots on time."
On September 14, the US Supreme Court declined to let USPS enforce a rule targeting mail-in ballots, dealing a setback to President Donald Trump's effort to restrict voting by mail. USPS said it would not enforce the rule under the order.
The agency adopted the measure after Trump issued a March executive order aimed at tightening rules governing mail voting.
In 2024, USPS delivered 99.2 million ballots to and from voters in the presidential election. About 30% of votes were cast by mail in the November 2024 presidential election, down from 46% in 2020.
Trump's fellow Republicans are locked in a tight battle to retain control of Congress in the midterms. Restricting mail-in ballots would benefit Republicans because Democratic voters disproportionately use mail-in ballots, according to various surveys.
Under the rule that was blocked, states would have had to provide lists of mail-ballot recipients to USPS and use agency-approved outbound and return ballot mail envelopes outfitted with unique barcodes. The Postal Service could then have refused to send out ballots that did not comply or were associated with voters not appearing on the lists.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[１５日 ロイター] - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は１５日、南部アデンにあるイエメン暫定政府の本拠地となっている施設に向けて５発のミサイルを発射した。暫定政府当局者がロイターに明らかにした。この攻撃で警備員２人が死亡したが、施設内にいた暫定政権の首相と閣僚らは無事という。

フーシ派系サバ通信は軍当局者の話として、フーシ派はこの施設内にあるサウジアラビア軍の軍事作戦本部と武器庫を標的にしたと報じた。ロイターはこの情報を独自に確認できていない。

フーシ派のヤヒヤ・サリー報道官は、今回の攻撃は「サウジ軍の集結地点を所在場所にかかわらず攻撃する」というフーシ派の方針の一環だと述べた。

items.title: Selling the losers in your stock portfolio can help save you tax
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: Nobody likes taking a loss when selling stocks, but experts say now is the time to look at your portfolio and see if there are any investments that haven’t worked out as you hoped that might help you ...
items.body: OTTAWA — Nobody likes taking a loss when selling stocks, but experts say now is the time to look at your portfolio and see if there are any investments that haven’t worked out as you hoped that might help you reduce your tax bill. Reviewing your portfolio and taking a look at what gains you’ve seen and how you might be able to offset them with any losses should be part of your year-end tax planning. Kris Kibler, tax planning lead at Wealthsimple, says if you are selling shares at a loss, that deficit can be used to offset capital gains on better performing stocks, reducing the amount of tax you will owe. He explained that if you bought shares for $10,000 and later sold them for $7,000, the $3,000 capital loss could be deducted against capital gains. That deduction will reduce the amount of tax you might owe when you file your return next year. Kibler says it is important that tax-loss selling isn’t done in a vacuum. “You don’t necessarily engage in tax-loss harvesting or tax-loss selling in order to just take advantage of the tax implication with disregard for the investment portfolio overall,” he says. “This always wants to be kind of done in tandem with your overall investment and financial plan as a whole.” It is also important to ensure you don’t run afoul of the rules governing what losses you can claim. Tax-loss selling only applies to taxable or non-registered accounts. Losses in accounts such as your TFSA, RRSP or RESP cannot be used to offset your taxable gains outside those accounts. The losses can only be used to offset any taxable capital gains you have. They can’t be deducted from your regular income. If you don’t have any capital gains to offset this year, your losses can be used to reduce your taxable capital gains going back three years or you can carry the losses forward to use in future years. CRA also doesn’t allow what is referred to as a superficial loss, which prevents you from claiming the loss if the same or identical security is repurchased within a 61-day window starting 30 calendar days before the sale and extending 30 days after the sale. The superficial loss rules don’t just apply to your account, but also extend to your spouse or common-law partner, corporations you or your spouse control, or what the CRA calls an affiliated person. “What the CRA doesn’t want you to do is get the advantages of the tax-loss harvesting or tax-loss selling strategy in order to get the benefit and then purchase the exact same securities again and continue in the same portfolio,” Kibler said. Julie Petrera, director of financial planning at Edward Jones, says it is important to remember that tax-loss selling is not an investment strategy. “It should support your long-term goals but not drive your long-term investing goal,” she said. “I wouldn’t make decisions on what I’m holding in my portfolio just for short-term tax reasons.” Petrera said losses are part of investing at times, but tax-loss selling is the “silver lining” when you have securities that have gone down. “While you have lost money on that security or on that investment, the money that you’ve lost could be made up for in tax savings applied to another investment,” she said. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 15, 2026. Craig Wong, The Canadian Press

items.title: US regional lender First Horizon to offload $4.5 billion of consumer mortgages
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: First Horizon said on Thursday it had struck a deal to sell about $4.5 billion of select lower-yielding consumer mortgages, as the US regional lender looks to boost its earnings.
items.body:
First Horizon (FHN.N) said on Thursday it had struck a deal to sell about $4.5 billion of select lower-yielding consumer mortgages, as the US regional lender looks to boost its earnings.
Shares of the Memphis, Tennessee-based bank, which jumped 4% in morning trading, have slipped 5% this year as of last close.
Here are some other details:
The realignment of the mortgage business is part of a broader push by First Horizon to overhaul its balance sheet and focus on core customers.
The residential mortgage loan sale will improve the bank's loan-to-deposit ratio, free up balance sheet capacity and support share buybacks.
"The strategic actions clean up the optics of the balance sheet and likely produce a more profitable franchise going forward," Citi analyst Benjamin Gerlinger said.
First Horizon swung to a loss in the third quarter from a year earlier, as it booked a $473 million loss on the pending mortgage portfolio sale.
The bank, which had $84.3 billion in assets as of September 30, plans to partially redeploy proceeds from the mortgage sale into higher-yielding loans in the coming quarters.
"We expect the debate to center on how quickly the proceeds are redeployed into higher-yielding commercial loans and whether deposit cost pressure eases enough to support NII as countercyclical fee income softens," Jefferies analyst David Chiaverini said, adding the biggest takeaway from the quarter was the mortgage business realignment.
The sale, which is expected to close in the fourth quarter, is anticipated to boost 2027 profit by 4% after tax.
