items.title: コアウィーブ株再び急落、25年5月以来安値　ＡＩ投資に債務懸念
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Aditya Soni　Anhata Rooprai

[１５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Aditya Soni　Anhata Rooprai

[１５日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービスを提供するコアウィーブの株式と社債が１５日、再び急落した。最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が受注残の多さを強調したにもかかわらず、借入金による資金調達にますます依存するＡＩインフラの拡充を巡り、信用不安が高まっていることが鮮明となった。株価は一時、８．３％下落し、２０２５年５月以来の安値を付けた。

同社は約５００億ドルの債務を抱えており、データセンターブームが信用により支えられているという懸念の象徴となっている。また、新興企業の経営を圧迫しているほか、グーグルの持ち株会社アルファベットやメタ・プラットフォームズのような大手企業のキャッシュフローにまで圧力をかけている。

同社が４月に発行した２０３１年償還の社債の利回りは１６．２％となり、通常は財務悪化を示唆する水準を上回った。トレードウェブのデータによると、同社債の直近の価格は額面１ドルに対し０．０１１ドル安の０．７８４ドル。同社の債務に対するデフォルト保険コストは約１０００ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）に上昇し、５年以内のデフォルト確率が約６３％であることを示唆する水準となった。１年前の同確率は約３０％だった。

同社の株価は１４日にも約１５％下落しており、ハイテク株売りの中でも下落幅の大きい銘柄の一つとなっている。

ＩＧグループのチーフテクニカルアナリスト、アクセル・ルドルフ氏は「ＡＩ需要と、収益性のあるビジネスモデルとは全く別物だということに市場は気付き始めている」と指摘。「現時点では、ＡＩコンピューティングへの需要が突然冷え込んだというよりは、投資家がインフラ拡充の資金調達方法を疑問視しているように見える。ただ、資本コストが上がり続ければ、需要が堅調であっても、過剰にレバレッジを掛けている企業を守るには十分でなくなる可能性がある」と述べた。

一方、同社の第２位の株主で約１０％の株式を保有する半導体大手エヌビディアのジェンスン・フアンＣＥＯは、こうした懸念を一蹴。ストックホルムでのイベントで記者団に対し「コアウィーブの財務力は日々改善している」とした上で、エヌビディアによる同社への支援は必要ないとの認識を示した。「私は楽観的だ。コアウィーブの資本コストは実際に下がっている」と語った。

コアウィーブ株再び急落、25年5月以来安値　ＡＩ投資に債務懸念
0:03 配信

コアウィーブのロゴ。7月20日撮影のイメージ写真。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Aditya Soni　Anhata Rooprai

[１５日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービスを提供するコアウィーブの株式と社債が１５日、再び急落した。最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が受注残の多さを強調したにもかかわらず、借入金による資金調達にますます依存するＡＩインフラの拡充を巡り、信用不安が高まっていることが鮮明となった。株価は一時、８．３％下落し、２０２５年５月以来の安値を付けた。

同社は約５００億ドルの債務を抱えており、データセンターブームが信用により支えられているという懸念の象徴となっている。また、新興企業の経営を圧迫しているほか、グーグルの持ち株会社アルファベットやメタ・プラットフォームズのような大手企業のキャッシュフローにまで圧力をかけている。

同社が４月に発行した２０３１年償還の社債の利回りは１６．２％となり、通常は財務悪化を示唆する水準を上回った。トレードウェブのデータによると、同社債の直近の価格は額面１ドルに対し０．０１１ドル安の０．７８４ドル。同社の債務に対するデフォルト保険コストは約１０００ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）に上昇し、５年以内のデフォルト確率が約６３％であることを示唆する水準となった。１年前の同確率は約３０％だった。

同社の株価は１４日にも約１５％下落しており、ハイテク株売りの中でも下落幅の大きい銘柄の一つとなっている。

ＩＧグループのチーフテクニカルアナリスト、アクセル・ルドルフ氏は「ＡＩ需要と、収益性のあるビジネスモデルとは全く別物だということに市場は気付き始めている」と指摘。「現時点では、ＡＩコンピューティングへの需要が突然冷え込んだというよりは、投資家がインフラ拡充の資金調達方法を疑問視しているように見える。ただ、資本コストが上がり続ければ、需要が堅調であっても、過剰にレバレッジを掛けている企業を守るには十分でなくなる可能性がある」と述べた。

一方、同社の第２位の株主で約１０％の株式を保有する半導体大手エヌビディアのジェンスン・フアンＣＥＯは、こうした懸念を一蹴。ストックホルムでのイベントで記者団に対し「コアウィーブの財務力は日々改善している」とした上で、エヌビディアによる同社への支援は必要ないとの認識を示した。「私は楽観的だ。コアウィーブの資本コストは実際に下がっている」と語った。

items.author: CNA
items.summary: Oct 15 : The bones of a Neanderthal from a cave in Iraq's Kurdistan region are offering evidence of both violence and compassion in the closest evolutionary cousins of our species, exhibiting a wound apparently from a fatal spear attack as well as signs of an earlier nonfatal injury that may have elicited kindly car

Bones from Iraqi cave hint at violence and compassion in Neanderthals

The entrance to Shanidar Cave in Iraq's Kurdistan region, a site of important Neanderthal remains, is seen in an undated photograph released on October 15, 2026. Prof Graeme Barker/Handout via REUTERS NO RESALES. NO ARCHIVES. THIS IMAGE HAS BEEN SUPPLIED BY A THIRD PARTY

FAST

Oct 15 : The bones of a Neanderthal from a cave in Iraq's Kurdistan region are offering evidence of both violence and compassion in the closest evolutionary cousins of our species, exhibiting a wound apparently from a fatal spear attack as well as signs of an earlier nonfatal injury that may have elicited kindly care.
Researchers have discovered at Shanidar Cave in the Zagros Mountains of northern Iraq a partial skeleton of a Neanderthal, aged in the mid-40s, that included a left shoulder blade, or scapula, with a circular hole six-tenths of an inch (15 mm) wide indicative of a deeply penetrating stab.
The bones of this individual, who they call Shanidar A, were unearthed from under about 25 feet (7.5 meters) of rocks and sediment inside the cave and date to about 75,000 years ago. The researchers were unable to determine Shanidar A's sex.
The researchers said the injury's shape suggests it was caused by a forceful thrust using a sharpened wooden spear, a type of weapon Neanderthals are known to have used, rather than a spear with a stone tip. It was a weapon employed in hunting large mammals that were an important food source.

"The spear would have gone through the skin and major muscles, especially the pectoralis, as well as the ribcage and muscles between the ribs, and the lung," said biological anthropologist Emma Pomeroy of the University of Cambridge in England, lead author of the study published on Thursday in the journal Scientific Reports.
"The location could be like the kind of 'heart shot' hunters use to kill animals quickly by puncturing the heart, but that is a bit speculative. We do see heart shots as a hunting strategy both today and in the archaeological record. Neanderthals would have known this would lead to a quick death," Pomeroy said.
University of Cambridge archaeologist and study co-author Graeme Barker, who has led Shanidar Cave excavations since 2015, said the likeliest scenario is interpersonal violence.
The researchers said the violence probably occurred either between members of a particular Neanderthal group or between members of rival Neanderthal groups, calling a Homo sapiens attack or an accidental injury less likely.
The researchers found shards of bone displaced by the weapon. The injury indicated that the spear entered from above with a downward trajectory, penetrating the left chest cavity from the front and traveling through the body before punching the hole in the scapula, causing quick death.
ANOTHER INJURY
In addition to the scapula, the researchers found some ribs, a nearly complete right hand and seven teeth, mostly from the front of the lower jaw, belonging to Shanidar A. The teeth bore evidence that this Neanderthal had survived brutal injury at least a year before death — a blow to the face resulting in front teeth being smashed and lost. One tooth was split, with half remaining rotated in the mouth and others pushed out of position.
"The pain would have been extreme, and basic needs like eating and drinking would have been difficult, perhaps meaning Shanidar A needed food mashing and being able to rest. It's likely that Shanidar A did need some care from members of the group for some basic needs during recovery," Pomeroy said.
Shanidar A was one of five Neanderthals, four adults and one infant, whose bodies were carefully tucked behind a rock pillar in the cave in a burial cluster within a generation or so of each other. The cave was occupied by Neanderthals for tens of thousands of years as a seasonal campsite, and later by Homo sapiens.
Neanderthals were more robustly built than Homo sapiens, with larger brows. They lived as hunter-gatherers and inhabited Eurasia from the Atlantic coast to the Ural Mountains from about 400,000 years ago until a bit after 40,000 years ago, disappearing after Homo sapiens became established in the region.
The two species interbred, with modern non-African human populations bearing residual Neanderthal DNA.
The cave, overlooking the Great Zab river valley, has been a source of information about Neanderthals since the 1950s, with Shanidar A now offering new insight into their behavior.
"We see evidence of two contrasting facets of human nature – care and violence – juxtaposed in the same individual," Pomeroy said.
"We see evidence all around us today that violence and care are both aspects of how we humans behave, and we see this here in Shanidar A, too. Neanderthals were like us in many respects, both the good and the bad, and this find really highlights that, going against stereotypes of Neanderthals as unintelligent, uncaring cavemen and cavewomen," Pomeroy said.

Source: Reuters

items.title: L’AIE va accélérer la mise sur le marché des stocks de pétrole, dont plus de 20 millions de barils de diesel
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: L’Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) est convenue jeudi de mettre sur le marché plus de 20 millions de barils de diesel dès que possible, ainsi que les volumes restants des réserves d’urgence libérées en mars, afin de contribuer à approvisionner le marché et à freiner la flambée des prix.
items.body:
L’Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) est convenue jeudi de mettre sur le marché plus de 20 millions de barils de diesel dès que possible, ainsi que les volumes restants des réserves d’urgence libérées en mars, afin de contribuer à approvisionner le marché et à freiner la flambée des prix.
Le président américain Donald Trump a exhorté les pays de l’Union européenne à puiser dans leurs réserves, menaçant de restreindre les exportations américaines de diesel afin de contenir la hausse des prix avant les élections de mi-mandat du 3 novembre.
Les prix du diesel ont atteint des niveaux records sur de nombreux marchés liés à la guerre au Moyen-Orient et au conflit entre la Russie et l’Ukraine, faisant peser des risques inflationnistes et aggravant le coût de la vie pour les gouvernements et les consommateurs.
Le conseil d’administration de l’AIE, qui compte 32 pays membres, s’est réuni jeudi pour examiner l’ampleur et le calendrier des mises sur le marché des stocks.
"Le conseil de direction de l’AIE a réaffirmé son engagement à poursuivre la mise en œuvre de l’action collective de mars 2026 en réponse à la crise dans le détroit d’Ormuz", a indiqué l’agence dans un communiqué publié à l’issue de la réunion.
En mars, les pays membres s’étaient engagés à libérer plus de 400 millions de barils de pétrole brut et de produits pétroliers, alors que les prix s’envolaient.
Jeudi, les membres "sont convenus d’accélérer la mise sur le marché des volumes restants, des plans précis étant déjà en place, notamment pour libérer plus de 20 millions de barils de diesel dès que possible".
Le volume de 20 millions de barils de diesel est inférieur aux 50 millions de barils envisagés précédemment, selon une source au fait des discussions.
DÉCEPTION FACE À L’ABSENCE DE VOLUMES SUPPLÉMENTAIRES Reuters a rapporté ce mois-ci que les gouvernements de l’Union européenne examinaient une proposition française visant à libérer 50 millions de barils de diesel, auxquels s’ajouteraient 50 millions de barils de pétrole brut provenant des stocks des pays membres de l’AIE.
À la suite du communiqué publié jeudi par l’AIE, le contrat de référence européen du gazole, un produit pétrolier comprenant notamment le diesel , a progressé à 1.430,75 dollars (1.277 euros) la tonne à 15h12 GMT, bien qu’il soit resté en baisse sur la séance.
"La hausse des prix du gazole laisse penser à une certaine déception face à l’absence d’engagement ferme en faveur de volumes supplémentaires immédiats", a déclaré Ole Hansen, analyste chez Saxo Bank.
"Les prix sont élevés, mais nous ne sommes pas confrontés à de véritables pénuries. Dans ce contexte, il est probablement judicieux de conserver nos réserves pour le moment."
Selon l'AIE, certains membres ont déjà mis sur le marché des volumes supérieurs à leurs engagements de mars, tandis que d’autres prévoient de faire de même.
Environ 330 millions de barils ont été mis sur le marché à ce jour, a précisé l’AIE.
Les États-Unis ont indiqué aux autres membres de l’AIE que les plans actuels de libération des réserves ne suffisaient pas à freiner la hausse des prix des carburants, a rapporté jeudi Bloomberg News, citant des sources proches du dossier.
La Maison blanche n’a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaire de Reuters.
L’Espagne a annoncé jeudi qu’elle mettrait sur le marché 4,4 millions de barils de ses réserves stratégiques en octobre, sans préciser quels produits seraient concernés. Le pays a jusqu’à présent mis sur le marché 3,7 millions des 11,5 millions de barils qu’il s’était engagé à débloquer en mars.

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday (Oct 15) the execution of the Fort Hood gunman would not be livestreamed but that immediate families of the victims would be able to view it in person.
"I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device," Trump wrote.
"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed. That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness JUSTICE!"
Some of Trump's fellow Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, as well as religious leaders and international observers, had expressed doubts about the Pentagon's plan to livestream the Dec 3 execution of Nidal Hasan. Recent polls have also shown a majority of Americans opposed livestreaming it.
Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, was found guilty in a military trial of fatally shooting 13 people at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009.

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday (Oct 15) the execution of the Fort Hood gunman would not be livestreamed but that immediate families of the victims would be able to view it in person.
"I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device," Trump wrote.
"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed. That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness JUSTICE!"
Some of Trump's fellow Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, as well as religious leaders and international observers, had expressed doubts about the Pentagon's plan to livestream the Dec 3 execution of Nidal Hasan. Recent polls have also shown a majority of Americans opposed livestreaming it.
Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, was found guilty in a military trial of fatally shooting 13 people at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009.

items.body:
［ニューヨーク　１５日　ロイター］ - １５日午前の米株式市場は、ナスダック総合が約１カ月ぶりの安値圏に下落した。金利上昇が人工知能（ＡＩ）投資に影響するとの懸念からＡＩ関連株の売りが加速したほか、経済指標が米国の物価上昇圧力の強まりを示したことも重しとなった。

半導体メーカーの台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）が、マクロ経済の不確実性を理由に２０２７年の見通しについて慎重な姿勢を示したことも、投資家心理を圧迫した。

多額の債務を抱えるデータセンター運営会社コアウィーブは、最近のハイテク株急落の中心にあり、前日の１５％安に続いて８．５％下落。クラウド大手オラクルも、前日の約９％安に続き小幅安となった。

半導体株も下落し、エヌビディアは３．３％安、マイクロン・テクノロジーは５％安、アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイシズ（ＡＭＤ）は６．４％安となった。

サクソのチーフ投資ストラテジスト、チャル・チャナナ氏は「投資家は、将来の成長が株価評価にどこまで織り込まれているのか、事業拡大の資金をどう調達しているのか、そして投資がいつ十分な収益を生むのかについて、疑問を強めている。コアウィーブの社債価格の調整は、ＡＩインフラの拡大にどんな条件でも資金を提供しようとする投資家の姿勢が弱まっていることを示唆している」とした。

「恐怖指数」として知られるＣＢＯＥボラティリティー指数（ＶＩＸ）は２週間ぶりの高水準を付け、０．８３ポイント高の１７．７４となった。

items.title: Yemen's Houthis hit palace in Aden, coalition details attacks on Saudi infrastructure
items.author: Enas Alashray, Mohammed Ghobari, Eman Abouhassira
items.creator: Enas Alashray, Mohammed Ghobari, Eman Abouhassira
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure in the escalating conflict.
items.body:
Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure in the escalating conflict.
The attack was the first in the current conflict between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi Arabia on Aden's al-Maashiq palace, the seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed and internationally recognised government. The conflict is a new theatre in the wider regional war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.
The government's prime minister and cabinet members were safe following the attack, Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said. Witnesses told Reuters they heard loud booms near the palace. Yemen's cabinet said the attack involved missiles and drones, and officials told Reuters that two guards were killed.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the Houthis had bombed what he described as the Saudi military operations headquarters in Aden, as part of the group's declared policy of targeting "Saudi reinforcements wherever they were located".
The Houthi-run news agency SABA said the headquarters was run by Saudi officers and that there were weapons depots there. Reuters could not independently verify the claims.
The renewed fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed forces resumed in Yemen last month, and aid agencies [USN:L6N4600ML TEXT:"have warned"] of rapidly worsening conditions.
Last week, government forces launched a campaign to recapture areas controlled by the Houthis, recovering ground near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a global shipping artery.
Residents of Taiz, northwest of Aden, have said they face [USN:L1N45Z0S1 TEXT:"intensifying bombardment"] and dwindling supplies as the Houthis tighten their grip on areas around the city, Yemen's third-largest.
War broke out in Yemen in 2014 when [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"the Houthis"] seized the capital Sanaa, driving the government south. A Saudi-led military intervention the following year led to a bloody stalemate before a 2022 truce that held until this year.
In that phase of the conflict Houthi fighters and allied forces briefly seized al-Maashiq palace during a battle for Aden, before withdrawing.
COALITION SAYS HOUTHIS ARE GETTING MISSILES, FAST BOATS As Saudi Arabia backs government forces, the Houthis [USN:L1N4610L5 TEXT:"have been firing"] ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a [USN:L1N46108L TEXT:"pressure point"] in the wider war [USN:L6N45Y0GN TEXT:"and threatening"] its ambitious economic plans.
On Thursday, the Saudi-led military coalition said the Houthis had attempted to attack dozens of such sites, highlighting the risk to Saudi civilian infrastructure. The governing council of the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization condemned the recent attacks on civilian airports, aircraft, and aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.
Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki told reporters that the Houthis had launched 20 attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh this month, killing 17 people and wounding 333 others. The airport is one of Saudi Arabia's main international aviation hubs.
The coalition said Houthi attacks on Abha airport in southwestern Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border had killed three people and wounded 28.
Maliki said the Houthis had acquired advanced military technology with the help of "regional actors," including ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats.
Iran [USN:L1N43P0D6 TEXT:"has provided"] weapons, money and training to the Houthis, although Tehran has officially denied arming them in violation of a UN arms embargo.
Maliki also said the coalition had destroyed 127 weapons storage facilities and launch platforms in Yemen's mountainous areas, calling on the Houthis to immediately halt operations targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Shortly afterwards, the Houthi military spokesperson said Saudi airspace and airports were unsafe, renewing a warning to airlines while excluding airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.
Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority also issued an early-warning alert over a potential threat in the southern province of Najran, before saying the danger had passed.
Later, the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a drone in the southwestern Saudi Arabian city of Khamis Mushait, and another launched towards the country's southern region.

Oct 15 : Spain has put forward some of the country's biggest football stadiums, including Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu and Barcelona's Camp Nou, as part of its bid to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup, the Spanish Rugby Federation said on Thursday.
The RFER submitted its detailed applicant questionnaire to World Rugby this month and has now unveiled a list of potential venues that also includes Atletico Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium, as Spain seeks to host the event for the first time.
Backed by LaLiga, the bid plans to capitalise on infrastructure developed for the 2030 football World Cup, which Spain will co-host with Portugal and Morocco.

In a statement, the RFER said the proposal would draw on the "venues, transport infrastructure, security and volunteer management" associated with staging the football showpiece.
"World Rugby has established this tournament as the pinnacle of our sport and it is a great honour for Spain to bid to host it," RFER Executive President Juan Carlos Martin 'Hansen' said in the statement reported by the BBC.
"Rugby is becoming part of our country's identity. Working together with World Rugby, we can make Rugby World Cup 2035 a turning point in the global growth of the sport, for the benefit of generations to come."
Spain faces competition from more traditional rugby nations. Japan has confirmed its interest in hosting the tournament, while Argentina has outlined a South American bid involving neighbouring countries.
If successful, Spain would become the first European hosts of the Rugby World Cup since France staged the 2023 edition, which was won by South Africa.
Spain have qualified for the 2027 tournament in Australia, which will be their first appearance at a men's Rugby World Cup since 1999. The 2031 edition will be held in the US for the first time.

Oct 15 : Norwegian alpine skier Aleksander Aamodt Kilde has ruptured his Achilles tendon in a crash during downhill training in Chile, the Norwegian Ski Federation said on Thursday.
The 34-year-old is returning home to Innsbruck, Austria, for further medical examinations and to evaluate treatment options with his medical team. No timeline was given for his recovery. 
Kilde has already had multiple surgeries and faced a life-threatening infection following a high-speed crash in Wengen in January 2024. He was named in Norway's team for this season.  
The speed specialist sat out the second half of last season and withdrew from the Winter Olympics in February.

Oct 15 : Bodo/Glimt’s Aspmyra Stadium reinforced its reputation as one of European football’s most forbidding venues on Wednesday when Borussia Dortmund became its latest high-profile casualty, losing 1-0 in the Champions League.
Situated above the Arctic Circle, the modest 8,270-capacity ground presents visiting teams with a distinctive combination of biting coastal winds, a slick artificial pitch and Bodo/Glimt’s relentless pressing game.
The results speak for themselves. Since 2020, Bodo/Glimt have won 37 of their 48 European home matches, with AS Roma, Porto, Lazio, Manchester City, Inter Milan and Sporting among their victims at Aspmyra.
"In windy, chilly conditions, the Norwegian opposition made more effective use of the ball on the artificial surface of Aspmyra Stadion," Dortmund's club website noted in its post-match summary, echoing a familiar sentiment from defeated visitors.

Bodo/Glimt midfielder Patrick Berg acknowledged the unique psychological edge their home ground provides.
"We feel confident playing here at home. Many teams don't like to come here," he said after Wednesday's victory.
THE ASPMYRA TRAP
A string of upsets has earned the ground the nickname "The Aspmyra Trap".
More than 800 kilometres north of Oslo, the stadium subjects visiting teams to sub-zero Arctic temperatures, biting gales and limited winter daylight.
"To play football in Bodo in February, that is special for many teams and players, but we are used to it," manager Kjetil Knutsen has said.
The stadium's synthetic pitch is engineered to withstand the harsh Nordic climate, but visiting players used to grass can struggle with the ball's unique bounce and speed, and the physical demands on the body.
The home fans endure the elements to roar their team on at a draughty, outdated venue where only one corner of the stadium is fully sealed against the wind.
SURFACE TENSION
The surface has long been a point of contention for visiting managers.
In 2022, then-Celtic boss Ange Postecoglou chose not to let his squad train on Aspmyra's surface the evening before their match, opting instead to complete their session in Glasgow.
Celtic subsequently suffered a 2–0 defeat on the night, crashing out 5–1 on aggregate in their UEFA Europa Conference League tie.
Former Roma manager Jose Mourinho, whose side suffered a 6–1 humiliation at Aspmyra in 2021, was among the pitch's most outspoken critics.
"High-level football on a plastic pitch is not high-level football," Mourinho remarked. "The ball is slow and the players can't dribble... I don't understand why UEFA allows Champions League matches on a plastic pitch."
Others regard the surface as integral to Bodo/Glimt's fast, aggressive style.
"I love artificial turf. I love that style of football. It is tiki-taka, lightning-fast transitions, and a high tempo," Norwegian commentator Sverre Krogh Sundbo said.
While the artificial pitch is likely to remain central to the club's identity, Aspmyra itself is nearing the end of its life.
A new 10,000-seat stadium is under construction with fully enclosed stands, which should offer greater protection against the wind.
Whether it will weaken the club's formidable home advantage remains to be seen.

Dasharatha’s dilemma: What economics Nobel teaches central banks about keeping promises

Dasharatha’s story in the Ramayana and Robert Hall & Michael Woodford's economic insights have a common lesson on promises and changing circumstances.

Bidisha Bhattacharya

15 October, 2026 07:42 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Images of Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford being displayed as they are announced as winners of the 2026 Nobel economics prize at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Sweden | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

New Delhi: “ Raghukul reet sada chali aayi, pran jaaye par vachan na jaaye .”

Every Indian familiar with the Ramayana recognises this well-known line from Tulsidas’s Ramcharitmanas, expressing King Dasharatha’s commitment to a defining principle of the Raghu dynasty: life may be sacrificed, but a promise must never be broken. For centuries, this unwavering reliability has been regarded as a cornerstone of righteous governance—a ruler who honours his word allows citizens to place their trust in his decisions and plan their lives accordingly.

Yet Dasharatha’s story also reveals the dangers of an unyielding commitment when circumstances change. This conflict between keeping promises and exercising judgement offers an understanding of the work of the two economists awarded the Nobel Prize for their contributions to understanding economic expectations and stabilisation. Their research helps explain why credible commitments are important for central banks, but also why credibility need not mean following a predetermined course of action regardless of what happens.

Show Full Article

Robert E. Hall of Stanford University and Michael Woodford of Columbia University were recognised for their contributions to understanding the “microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation”. At the heart of their work is a deceptively simple idea: an economy is not a machine that responds predictably to policy interventions. It comprises millions of households and businesses that continually form expectations about the future. This means that those who can influence expectations about the future can, in turn, influence present actions.

Their work developed against the backdrop of the economic turbulence of the 1970s, when oil shocks brought high inflation and unemployment simultaneously, challenging conventional approaches to economic stabilisation. Rather than treating the economy as a system that policymakers could steer through immediate interventions alone, their research helped explain how individual decisions and expectations shape macroeconomic outcomes.

Also Read: Anne Carson is a literary Houdini. Her diabolical brilliance got her the Nobel

Living in tomorrow
In 1978, Hall found an important insight in household behaviour. Building on Milton Friedman’s idea that families allocate spending based on anticipated lifetime earnings,

Hall envisioned individuals who incorporate all known future information into their current decisions.

Consider a young engineer in Patna who receives a job offer from a Bengaluru firm. Upon receiving the offer, she may begin planning for a motorbike or a flat rather than waiting for her first salary.

Hall’s research showed that, if families made decisions this way, current spending already reflects foreseeable future events and changes in consumption depend on new information that was not previously anticipated. Since genuinely new information is inherently unpredictable, consumption changes can, in this model, follow a pattern of random fluctuations, known in economics as a random walk.

This insight had important implications for economic policies: what people expect can matter as much as the immediate effects of a policy intervention. An announcement about future policy can therefore influence behaviour well before the government or central bank acts.

Woodford developed a broader theory of central banking centred on this forward-looking behaviour. Initially trained as a lawyer at Yale before transitioning to economics, he published his influential work ‘Interest and Prices’ in 2003. He examined how expectations about future monetary policy influence current economic decisions, including how businesses set prices.

Consider a dhaba owner who rarely updates his menu board. Knowing that he may not be able to revise prices immediately, he set prices today with anticipated future costs in mind.

Taken together, Hall’s work on household consumption and Woodford’s work on businesses showed that the economy is influenced more by public expectations about what policymakers will do over the next two to three years than current policy settings.

Woodford’s work consequently concluded that monetary policy primarily involves managing expectations, with a central bank’s communication serving as its most potent tool.

Following the 2008 financial crisis, when policy rates in several economies approached zero, central banks adopted his “forward guidance” strategy to commit to maintain low rates for an extended period. This commitment alone helped reduce borrowing costs and stabilise the economic recovery.

Dasharatha’s dilemma
The Ramayana offers a cautionary message for central bankers. When Kaikeyi invoked the boons Dasharatha had granted her, demanding Rama’s exile, Dasharatha honoured his promise despite its devastating consequences. This part of the story shows that a promise made under one set of circumstances and fulfilled uncritically in another can become a liability rather than a virtue.

The lesson for central banks is that a commitment to an objective need not require inflexibility about the means of achieving it.

Central banks faced this challenge after the pandemic. The US Federal Reserve, having committed to keeping interest rates near zero for an extended period, faced constraints as inflation surged in 2021, delaying rate increases until March 2022.

This predicament had been foreseen by economists.

In a 2012 paper, Jeffrey Campbell and his colleagues at the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago discussed what they called “Odyssean” and “Delphic” guidance. Odyssean guidance involves a binding commitment analogous to the Greek hero securing himself to his ship’s mast to resist the Sirens’ song. Delphic guidance, by contrast, refers to a sincere projection of the central bank’s responses to evolving conditions. Woodford was among the paper’s discussants.

The discourse has since resurfaced, with the Federal Reserve, under its new chair, reducing its reliance on inflexible guidance. Woodford argues that credibility comes not from following a predetermined path, but from consistently and reliably responding to unfolding events.

The wiser vow on Mint Road
In 2016, India codified this philosophy into law by amending the RBI Act to establish a 4 percent inflation target with a tolerance band of two percentage points on either side. The framework also established a six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), with its decisions, voting records and minutes made public.

This framework marked its tenth anniversary this month, and the RBI’s decision on 7 October demonstrated its maturity. The repo rate increased by 25 basis points to 5.50 per cent, marking the first hike since February 2023.

However, the most significant aspect was the adoption of a new stance termed “calibrated tightening.” This approach signals commitment and discipline rather than rigid adherence to a predetermined path. It signals to families and shopkeepers that the RBI will prevent an oil shock from shaping their expectations while allowing flexibility as data evolves. This reflects a blend of Delphic wisdom and steadfast resolve.

If Woodford were to meet Tulsidas, they might agree in a more nuanced interpretation of an enduring principle—an authority’s strength lies in the promise it is trusted to uphold, yet the most prudent course of action is not following a fixed path regardless of the circumstances.

The principle of “ Pran jaaye par vachan na jaaye ” holds, provided the vachan is judiciously chosen.

(Edited by Chingkheinganbi Mayengbam)

items.title: Diálogo sigue estancado en mina chilena Centinela de Antofagasta en huelga: sindicato
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Las negociaciones entre los dos sindicatos en huelga de la mina chilena de cobre Centinela y Antofagasta Minerals continuaban el jueves sin avances, aunque la firma aseguró que esta semana se ha abierto una oportunidad concreta para alcanzar un acuerdo.
items.body:
Las negociaciones entre los dos sindicatos en huelga de la mina chilena de cobre Centinela y Antofagasta Minerals continuaban el jueves sin avances, aunque la firma aseguró que esta semana se ha abierto una oportunidad concreta para alcanzar un acuerdo.
Los gremios Distrito Centinela y Minera Esperanza, con más de 700 socios, iniciaron la paralización el 7 de octubre tras fracasar su negociación contractual, pero volvieron a la mesa de diálogo el martes en un intento por resolver el conflicto.
"Hasta el momento, tras tres días de mediación voluntaria, la empresa se ha negado a abordar un mecanismo que ponga término a la discriminación durante la vigencia del contrato colectivo", dijeron los sindicatos en un comunicado.
En tanto, tres trabajadores cumplían siete días en huelga de hambre en un intento por presionar una pronta solución al reclamo de los sindicatos de que los trabajadores cuenten con los mismos beneficios independiente del gremio al que estén afiliados.
"Tras estimar desproporcionada la medida de protesta (de huelga de hambre), insiste la empresa en informar una oferta económica que fue rechazada por los trabajadores, pero oculta que la real razón del conflicto es la vulneración de los derechos fundamentales de igualdad de trato y no discriminación", agregó.
En un comunicado, la empresa aseguró que durante esta semana ha presentado nuevas propuestas con materias relevantes y una mejora significativa en las condiciones económicas.
"Esperamos que los socios y las socias puedan evaluar íntegramente las propuestas entregadas y decidir de manera informada. Tenemos la convicción de que el diálogo desarrollado esta semana ha abierto una oportunidad concreta para alcanzar un acuerdo", agregó.
Antofagasta (ANTO.L) reiteró que ha logrado sostener su producción en niveles normales "lo que hasta ahora ha evitado los efectos negativos" de la huelga. La compañía reportó el jueves un [USN:L6N4610GA TEXT:"aumento del 7% en su producción del tercer trimestre"] y mantuvo sus previsiones de sumar entre 625.000 y 655.000 toneladas de cobre este año.
Centinela produjo unas 240.000 toneladas de cobre en 2025.
La huelga en Centinela, además del [USN:L6N4600MP TEXT:"riesgo finalmente no consumado de paralización"] de supervisores en Escondida, de BHP (BHP.AX) , ha dado apoyo a los precios globales del cobre en medio de los temores sobre la dificultad de impulsar la oferta para abastecer el consumo estimado hacia adelante.

items.title: ＷＥＦ、ラガルド氏を次期会長に指名か　11月2日にも＝関係筋
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Dave Graham　Francesco Canepa

[チューリヒ／バンコク １５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Dave Graham　Francesco Canepa

[チューリヒ／バンコク １５日 ロイター] - 世界経済フォーラム（ＷＥＦ）が来月にも欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁を次期会長に指名する可能性があることが分かった。同組織の関係筋４人がロイターに明らかにした。実現すればラガルド氏はＥＣＢ総裁を任期前に退任することになり、ＥＣＢ首脳部の広範な人事刷新につながる。

関係筋によると、ＷＥＦの理事会は１１月２日に開催され、ラガルド氏自身も参加する。この会合でラガルド氏を次期会長に選出する可能性がある。ただ、最終決定にはまだ至っていないという。

また、理事会は代わりに、来年１月のダボス年次総会でラガルド氏の次期会長選出のための投票日を設定することもあり得るという。

ラガルド氏のＥＣＢ総裁任期は２０２７年１０月まで。早期退任となれば、ＥＣＢの他２つの要職を含む人事を巡る複雑な政治的駆け引きが始まる見通し。

関係筋は、ラガルド氏の選出は確実ではないとしながらも、ラガルド氏は理事会で幅広い支持を得ていると述べた。

ＥＣＢはコメントを差し控えた。

ラガルド氏は、来年までＥＣＢにとどまると述べてきたが、１０月の任期満了まで正式に職務を続けると明言するには至っていない。

2026年10月14日撮影　REUTERS/Athit Perawongmeth

Dave Graham　Francesco Canepa

[チューリヒ／バンコク １５日 ロイター] - 世界経済フォーラム（ＷＥＦ）が来月にも欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁を次期会長に指名する可能性があることが分かった。同組織の関係筋４人がロイターに明らかにした。実現すればラガルド氏はＥＣＢ総裁を任期前に退任することになり、ＥＣＢ首脳部の広範な人事刷新につながる。

関係筋によると、ＷＥＦの理事会は１１月２日に開催され、ラガルド氏自身も参加する。この会合でラガルド氏を次期会長に選出する可能性がある。ただ、最終決定にはまだ至っていないという。

また、理事会は代わりに、来年１月のダボス年次総会でラガルド氏の次期会長選出のための投票日を設定することもあり得るという。

ラガルド氏のＥＣＢ総裁任期は２０２７年１０月まで。早期退任となれば、ＥＣＢの他２つの要職を含む人事を巡る複雑な政治的駆け引きが始まる見通し。

関係筋は、ラガルド氏の選出は確実ではないとしながらも、ラガルド氏は理事会で幅広い支持を得ていると述べた。

ＥＣＢはコメントを差し控えた。

ラガルド氏は、来年までＥＣＢにとどまると述べてきたが、１０月の任期満了まで正式に職務を続けると明言するには至っていない。

items.title: Nvidia, Apple each gave $25 million for Trump's ballroom, Washington Post reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Nvidia and Apple each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private donations for the project.
items.body:
Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Apple (AAPL.O) each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private donations for the project.
The Adelson family, longtime financial supporters of Trump and his Republican Party, committed $25 million as well, as did billionaire Charles Ergen, co-founder and chairman of telecommunications company Dish Network, the report added.
The president himself is not on the list, according to the Post.
Reuters has not verified the report. The White House said it would not release information about the donors, which spokesman Davis Ingle said "represent a wide array of great American companies."
"The same critics who are alleging fake conflicts of interests, would also complain if American taxpayers were footing the bill for these long-overdue renovations," Ingle told Reuters.
Nvidia said it was proud to make a donation to a nonpartisan trust that serves Americans. "As an American company, our support for the United States is paramount, and independent of any business interests," a spokesperson said.
Apple declined to comment.
The scale of the ballroom project and the administration’s handling of fundraising and disclosures have drawn criticism from watchdog groups and legal experts, who say it raises questions about transparency, donor influence and adherence to longstanding ethics and oversight norms.
Trump initially said he and wealthy donors would pay for the estimated $400 million project, but he later unsuccessfully sought $1 billion from Congress for an underground bunker and security features to harden the facility.
The Post reported that the "vast majority of the funds raised came from companies and wealthy individuals with interests before the federal government" and that half the total came from companies or executives of firms that have had federal government contracts in Trump's second White House term.
The planned ballroom is among [USN:L1N3YZ1G0 TEXT:"several projects"] Trump is pursuing in his efforts to remake Washington with sweeping, unilateral changes that his opponents have challenged in court and called a power grab.
The US Supreme Court, in a 5-4 [USN:S0N42U037 TEXT:"ruling"] in August, allowed Trump to continue construction of the ballroom while he challenges a judicial order that would halt much of the development. In a dissent, Chief Justice John Roberts said the project was "likely unlawful."
The ballroom, which Trump has said will seat 1,000 guests, has faced public backlash. Preservationists and opponents say Trump exceeded his authority by demolishing the historic East Wing, which housed the first lady's offices and the White House movie theater, to make room for the structure.
Trump says a planned 90,000-square-foot (8,360-square-meter) White House ballroom will include bomb shelters, medical facilities, defenses against drones and missiles and other security features. Confronted with criticism of the project, his administration now says the facility is needed for national security, an argument the president has also made about a proposed triumphal arch.

ＡＩを巡っては、安全性やサイバーセキュリティー上の脅威、悪用など、潜在的なリスクへの監視が強まっている。

書簡でレビン氏は「同社はＩＰＯに向けて突き進むのではなく、こうした前例のないリスクへの対処に力を注ぐべきだ」と記している。

市会計監査官室によると、市の公的年金基金はプライベートエクイティ（ＰＥ）投資を通じ、アンソロピックに合計７００万ドルの投資エクスポージャーを持つ。

ニューヨーク市の会計監査官は市の財政を監督し、年金基金を管理するとともに、公的支出や財務慣行を監視する役割を担う。基金の資産総額は３２５０億ドルを超える。

items.title: Brazilian Camara to replace Ocon at Haas F1 team next season
items.author: Alan Baldwin
items.creator: Alan Baldwin
items.summary: Brazilian Rafael Camara will race for Haas next season on a multi-year deal, with the US-owned Formula One team saying on Thursday he was clearly the quickest in a shoot-out test for the seat.
items.body:
Brazilian Rafael Camara will race for Haas next season on a multi-year deal, with the US-owned Formula One team saying on Thursday he was clearly the quickest in a shoot-out test for the seat.
The 21-year-old Ferrari Academy driver leads the Formula Two standings with two rounds remaining, after winning the F3 title last year.
He will be the second Brazilian on the starting grid, with Gabriel Bortoleto already racing for Audi, and plans to take the number 50 since his compatriot races with the 5 that would have been his first choice as a driver born on May 5, 2005.
Camara replaces Frenchman Esteban Ocon, whose [USN:L6N45M0IZ TEXT:"departure was announced last month,"] at the Ferrari-powered team. Britain's Oliver Bearman, who also came through the Ferrari Academy, is yet to be confirmed but sure to stay as the more experienced team leader.
The signing dashed the immediate hopes of [USN:L4N3YZ0T7 TEXT:"Australian Jack Doohan"], the reserve who had been hoping for a return to a full-time race seat after a [USN:L4N3YE0PV TEXT:"split from Renault-owned Alpine"] last year.
"He (Camara) was the quickest, very simple answer. He was impressive," Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu told reporters on a video call when asked what had decided the choice.
RESERVE DOOR REMAINS OPEN FOR DOOHAN Komatsu said Doohan's future with the team was "still up in the air" but the door remained open for him to continue in his current role.
"We've been talking with him and his manager to see if we can do something together beyond this year," he added.
Camara, a former teammate of Mercedes' 20-year-old Formula One championship leader Kimi Antonelli in the FRECA European junior series, showed his pace when he drove last year's Haas in a Testing of Previous Cars (TPC) outing in Portugal at the Algarve Circuit in August.
"He showed... that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car, he showed us more than just raw speed," said Komatsu. "Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special."
The Recife-born Brazilian, who leads Red Bull-backed Bulgarian Nikola Tsolov by seven points in the F2 standings, said his first reaction when Komatsu called to say he had the job was to reply, "Are you sure?"
"I'm extremely happy, especially for my parents," he told reporters. "It was a lot of sacrifice on their side. We are not even from the motorsports world, we didn't really know exactly what was the way to go and to be here.
"We moved from Recife to Sao Paulo and then eventually they were always travelling with me. So their life, the normal life that they had, they couldn't be doing any more."
Camara revealed that his grandmother had raced with a DKW Vemag in the 1960s, but said that was not the reason he had started.
Instead the adventure began when the son of a work colleague of his father began karting and his brother then also got the chance but proved reluctant and eventually stopped.
"I was always the one that was following and wanting to go but I was still too young, I was five," explained Camara, who has the late triple champion Ayrton Senna as his racing hero. "When I was six I kept asking my dad... and it became something a bit more serious now."
Haas are seventh of 11 teams ahead of next week's US Grand Prix in Austin, Texas. Bearman has scored 23 of their 30 points.

items.title: 米9月ＰＰＩ、前年比6.3％上昇　22年12月以来の大きな伸び
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ワシントン １５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ワシントン １５日 ロイター] - 米労働省が１５日発表した９月の卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ、最終需要向け財・サービス）は前年比６．３％上昇し、２０２２年１２月以来の大幅な伸びとなった。前月比では１．３％上昇し、２２年３月以来、４年半ぶりの大きな伸びを記録した。財（モノ）・サービスの両面でコスト上昇が進んでおり、エネルギー関連以外にもインフレが広がっていることが改めて示された。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は前月比０．５％上昇だった。８月は当初の０．４％上昇から０．５％上昇に上方改定された。

前日には消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）で幅広い品目が上昇したことが示されており、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が月内の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で利上げに踏み切る可能性が改めて意識された。

オックスフォード・エコノミクスの米国担当シニアエコノミスト、マシュー・マーティン氏は「インフレの定着と底堅い労働市場を踏まえ、ＦＲＢは市場の予想より早く動く必要があると確信しているため、月内のＦＯＭＣで利上げに踏み切ると予想する」と述べた。

＜モノ価格、エネルギー主導で急伸＞  

９月のモノの価格は２．６％上昇し、政府が０９年１２月に同統計の集計を開始して以来の大きな伸びとなった。エネルギー価格が１０．８％上昇し、幅広いモノの価格の上昇分の８０％以上を占めた。

ガソリン価格は２０．３％上昇したほか、ディーゼル燃料（軽油）、ジェット燃料、家庭用電力の価格も上昇した。食品価格は３カ月連続の下落から反転し、１．２％上昇した。食品の大半はトラックで輸送されており、９月の急伸は過去最高水準にあるディーゼル燃料価格が経済全般に波及し始めている初期の兆候である可能性がある。

変動が激しい食品とエネルギーを除くモノのコア指数は０．３％上昇。８月は０．４％上昇していた。

サービス価格は０．８％上昇。８月は０．２％上昇だった。卸売業者と小売業者が受け取るマージンが１．４％上昇したことが、サービス業全般の上昇の半分近くを占めた。

トラックによる貨物輸送、ホテル・モーテルなどの宿泊料金、航空運賃も上昇した。一方、自動車燃料・潤滑油の小売マージンは３０．３％急落。証券仲介の価格も下落した。 

エコノミストは９月の米個人消費支出（ＰＣＥ）価格のコア指数が、前月比０．３５％上昇し、四捨五入ベースで０．４％に達する可能性があると試算。前年同月比では３．１％上昇との見通しを示した。８月のコアＰＣＥインフレ率は前月比０．２％、前年同月比３．０％上昇だった。

items.title: 米9月小売売上高0.8％増、ガソリン高で予想上回る伸び　コアは減速
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Lucia Mutikani

[ワシントン　１５日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Lucia Mutikani

[ワシントン　１５日　ロイター] - 米商務省が１５日発表した９月の小売売上高（季節調整済）は前月比０．８％増加した。ガソリン価格の上昇を背景に予想を上回る伸びとなった。ただ、ガソリン以外の支出は総じて緩やかで、個人消費が力強く拡大した前四半期の勢いが今後も続くとのエコノミストの見方に水を差す可能性がある。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は０．３％増。予想レンジは横ばいから０．７％増まで幅があった。

９月の小売売上高の増加分の大半はガソリン価格の上昇によるものだった。米エネルギー情報局（ＥＩＡ）によると、９月のガソリン価格は７．１％上昇した。

９月の自動車、ガソリン、建設資材、外食サービスを除くコア小売売上高は前月比０．１％増。伸びは８月の１．２％から減速したほか、エコノミスト予想の０．３％を下回った。

ガソリンスタンドの売上高は６．４％急増。自動車販売店の売上高は０．２％増だった。家具、電化製品、オンライン小売店の売上高も増加した。

唯一のサービス部門である飲食店の売上高は１．１％増と、８月の１．４％増から鈍化した。建材・園芸用品、スポーツ用品・趣味・楽器・書籍店の売上高は減少した。その他小売店の売上高は３．０％減だった。

８月の小売売上高は１．３％増に上方改定された。国勢調査局は先月、過去の統計修正や新たに利用可能となった調査データを反映させるため、小売売上高の推計値を改定。８月は当初１．２％増と報告されたが、その後１．１％増に下方修正されていた。

items.title: ウクライナがロシア製油所攻撃再開　情報制限「意図的」　深まる米との亀裂
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Daniel Flynn　Max Hunder

[キーウ １５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Daniel Flynn　Max Hunder

[キーウ １５日 ロイター] - ウクライナは１５日、ロシアの製油所を攻撃した。これに先立ち、ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は、トランプ米大統領が発表したエネルギー施設への攻撃停止について、ロシアが順守していないとして、ウクライナも応じるのは「終わりだ」と表明した。

トランプ氏が１１日、ロシアとウクライナがエネルギー施設への攻撃停止に合意したと突然発表して以降、ウクライナはロシアの製油所への攻撃を停止していた。しかし、その後もロシアは発電所などのエネルギー施設を含め、ミサイルやドローン（無人機）による攻撃を繰り返し、死者が出たほか、数十万人への電力供給が途絶えた。

ゼレンスキー氏は１５日付の英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）に掲載されたインタビューで、ウクライナの忍耐は限界に達したと表明。「（製油所攻撃の）停止はもうやめる。終わりだ」と述べた。

また、スペースＸの衛星通信サービス「スターリンク」の軍用版端末の機能が今週変更され、ウクライナがドローン運用能力が制限されたことについて、「技術的な問題ではなく意図的」とし、政策上の決定だったとの見方を明確にした。

スペースＸを率いるイーロン・マスク氏は「速度や利用の制限は全て、米軍と、最終的にはＰＯＴＵＳ（トランプ氏）が決めている」とＸに投稿した。

ゼレンスキー氏は、製油所への攻撃停止を求めるトランプ氏の要求を事実上拒否することで、２０２２年２月のロシアによるウクライナ侵攻開始以来、米国との間に生じている最大の亀裂を一段と深める恐れがある。

トランプ氏は攻撃停止をロシアとウクライナ双方に求めていると説明してきたが、公の発言では主にウクライナによるロシア製油所への攻撃に焦点を当てている。トランプ氏は、こうした攻撃が世界市場での軽油価格上昇を招いていると批判している。 

ウクライナでは、米国が提供する技術になお依存する軍の戦闘に、この亀裂が深刻な影響を及ぼしかねないとの懸念が広がっている。ウクライナ当局者らはここ数日、ロシアのミサイル飛来について、西側同盟国から通常受けている警報が届いていないと報告している。警報は米国の衛星による探知に依存している。

トランプ氏は情報提供を差し控えていることを否定。ゼレンスキー氏によると、警報が提供されなかった理由について、ウクライナ側には技術的な不具合と説明された。

ウクライナ国防省の関係者は１５日、スターリンクの軍用端末は移動中でも機能するようになったが、時速１００マイル（１６０キロ）以下に限られると述べた。ウクライナ当局者らは、中距離攻撃やロシアからのドローン防衛のための迎撃用ドローンには、この速度では遅すぎるとしている。

１５日にはロシア中央部リャザン州の製油所が攻撃された。同製油所は国営石油大手ロスネフチが所有し、ロシアの石油精製処理量全体のほぼ５％を占め、首都への燃料供給の一翼を担っている。

ウクライナ当局者は、夜間にロシアの製油所を攻撃したと確認。ロシアが今週、エネルギー施設への攻撃停止に違反し、弾道ミサイルやドローンによる激しい攻撃を行ったことへの対応だと説明した。

これとは別にウクライナ海軍は１５日、ロシアのボロネジ州にあるボリソグレブスク飛行場を夜間に攻撃し、ロシア軍のＳｕ３４Ｍ軍用機６機を破壊したと発表した。テレグラムへの投稿で、沿岸ミサイルシステム「ネプチューン」を使用したと明らかにした。

ロシアは夜間に５００機超のドローンでウクライナを攻撃、中部キロボフラード州で３人が死亡、６人が負傷した。国営エネルギー会社ナフトガスは、ポルタワのガス採掘施設が被害を受け、操業を停止したと発表した。

ロシア大統領府は１５日、ウクライナによるロシアのエネルギーインフラへの攻撃は、米国の和平努力に反すると非難した。

ゼレンスキー氏はＦＴとのインタビューで、米政府がロシア政府との商業取引に熱心なことや、トランプ氏がロシアのプーチン大統領に称賛の念を抱いているように見えることを批判した。

両国の亀裂を受け、欧州各国やウクライナは米国の情報や技術に大きく依存していることへの懸念が高まっている。トランプ政権は既にウクライナへの武器供給を停止しているが、欧州の同盟国がウクライナに代わって米国製兵器を購入し続けることは認めている。

欧州には、スターリンクやロシアのミサイル発射を探知する米国の衛星システムに代わる利用可能なシステムが用意できていない。

ゼレンスキー氏によると、ウクライナ軍当局者は米側から、ロシアのエネルギーインフラへの攻撃を停止しなければ、米政府が情報提供を遮断すると警告されていた。

米政権との関係修復に向けてエネルギー施設への攻撃停止に応じる用意があるかとのＦＴの問いにゼレンスキー氏は、見返りとして米国製地対空ミサイル「パトリオット」の迎撃弾を追加供与される場合に限り同意できると答え、それが受け入れられる「最低限」の条件だとした。

BANGKOK, Oct 15 : Japan told its G20 counterparts that authorities must watch exchange-rate moves with a high sense of urgency, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Thursday.
The G20 finance leaders re-confirmed their commitment on currency policy, Katayama told reporters after attending the group's gathering, held on the sidelines of the annual IMF meetings in Bangkok this week.
"I told the gathering that we must closely watch financial market developments with a high sense of urgency," Katayama said on Japan's exchange-rate policy.
The remarks came as the yen's persistent weakness keeps market players on alert over the chance of another round of intervention by authorities to prop up the currency.

The G20 agrees that exchange-rate moves should be determined by markets but that excessively volatile and disorderly moves were undesirable - a line Japan points to as giving it authority to step into the market to arrest unwelcome yen swings.
A weak yen has become a source of concern for Japanese policymakers by pushing up the cost of imports, including for fuel, which has spiked due to the Middle East war.
Katayama said the G20 finance leaders did not produce a joint communique or a chair's statement during their meeting on Thursday.
When asked about the G20 group's discussions around rising long-term interest rates, Katayama said she told the group that each country must strive to achieve its fiscal sustainability goals, but at the same time use fiscal scope to boost investment in growth areas.
.

items.title: How the Houthis are helping Iran turn Saudi Arabia into a pressure point
items.author: Samia Nakhoul
items.creator: Samia Nakhoul
items.summary: The Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia are about more than Yemen.
items.body:
The Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia are about more than Yemen.
By targeting infrastructure and disrupting investment events central to Saudi Arabia's [USN:L6N45Y0GN TEXT:"economic ambitions"], they aim to pressure Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to both meet Houthi demands in Yemen and persuade US President Donald Trump to ease the US blockade choking Iran's economy, according to Saudi, Iranian and regional sources.
The campaign reflects a calculation by Iran and the Houthis that Saudi Arabia's prosperity, investment ambitions and exposure to disruption make it a vulnerable pressure point in a confrontation stretching from the [USN:L8N3YO10W TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"] at the mouth of the Gulf to [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb"] in the Red Sea.
Iran, under [USN:L6N45K0UX TEXT:"mounting economic"] and military pressure following the war launched by the US and Israel on February 28, is seeking to raise the cost of Washington's strategy by targeting its regional partners, said Michael Knights of strategic advisory Horizon Engage.
“The Iranians are in a chokehold,” he said. Unable to force Washington to change course directly, Tehran and the Houthis are “hammering Saudi Arabia, they’re hammering the weak point,” he added, exploiting the kingdom’s economic vulnerability and desire for stability.
[USN:L6N4010N9 TEXT:"The Houthis"] have a direct interest in easing the US blockade on Iran, their principal regional backer. A relaxation of pressure on Tehran would likely strengthen its ability to sustain the political, financial and military support and flow of weapons and cash on which the US says the movement depends.
But the Houthis also have their own demands, said two Saudi sources and three regional sources familiar with Saudi thinking: an end to Saudi military operations and restrictions on Yemeni ports and airports, regular flights to Iran, restored salary payments, war compensation and an end to Riyadh’s support for Yemen’s recognised government. Their terms would consolidate Houthi rule over much of Yemen.
A senior Iranian official said the Houthi attacks were part of a broader strategy by Iran and its allies to reshape the regional balance of power by targeting energy infrastructure and key shipping routes. He said Riyadh could not rely on US protection and must instead pursue negotiations, adding that Houthi attacks [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"would continue"] unless Saudi restrictions were lifted.
The strategy, however, leaves MbS facing a dilemma, the sources familiar with Saudi thinking say. Escalation risks a wider war that [USN:L6N45Y0GN TEXT:"could undermine his transformation agenda"], but concessions risk strengthening a movement that has challenged Saudi power for years. And the longer the conflict drags on, the greater the threat to Saudi security, investor confidence and Vision 2030.
The Saudi government media office and Iran's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Houthi spokesperson Mohammed Abdulsalam denied that the group was acting at Iran's behest, saying its demands were centred on longstanding humanitarian issues relating to Saudi Arabia, and included lifting restrictions on Yemeni ports, airports, easing economic restrictions, and paying civil servants' salaries from Yemen's own resources.
"Our humanitarian demands have nothing to do with Iran or anyone else," he said.
FLAGSHIP CONFERENCES DISRUPTED Saudi Arabia has faced a [USN:L6N4600NM TEXT:"widening wave"] of Houthi attacks over the past week, including deadly strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and a [USN:L6N4600QH TEXT:"strike on Saudi Aramco"], the world’s largest oil exporter and a backbone of the economy, which sparked a fire that spread across several floors.
The attacks have disrupted Riyadh's flagship oil conference, prompting top oil executives [USN:L6N45Y0GT TEXT:"to withdraw"], and forced organisers to [USN:L6N4600CJ TEXT:"offer remote participation"] at the Future Investment Initiative (FII), an annual global investment forum.
The Houthis have a record of striking deep inside the kingdom, including in 2019, when attacks on Aramco facilities temporarily disrupted about 5% of global oil supply. That was after Riyadh intervened in Yemen in 2015 following the Houthi takeover of the capital, Sanaa. The war became a bloody stalemate before a 2022 ceasefire.
However, Saudi leaders now see military pressure as their only viable option, said Abdulaziz Sager, chairman of the Saudi-based Gulf Research Center. "They reached a point of NO negotiations," he said. "They have no other choice except military action."
The Houthis increasingly see themselves as negotiating from strength, seeking recognition of their authority in Sanaa and an easing of restrictions on Yemen, said Fawaz Gerges, a Middle East analyst at the London School of Economics. "What the Houthis are asking now is a victor's peace," he said.
The United States has shown little appetite for another sustained campaign against the Houthis since bombing them last year over attacks on shipping in the Red Sea then agreeing a ceasefire, the sources familiar with Saudi thinking said. Washington's reluctance leaves Riyadh facing a conflict in which military pressure alone may not deliver a decisive outcome.
SAUDIS HAVE MORE TO LOSE At the start of the Houthi campaign, MbS [USN:L6N45308G TEXT:"asked Trump for help"] to fight the Houthis, but Trump did not agree to US strikes, sources told Reuters last month. Washington instead offered targeting assistance and intelligence-sharing. Trump later said he was considering possible action against the Houthis, while [USN:L1N45Z0S4 TEXT:"appearing to defer"] any response until after the US midterm elections.
The US State Department referred to previous remarks by Trump and by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
With drones and missiles exposing vulnerabilities in Saudi defences, analysts warn the conflict risks becoming a war of attrition in which the Houthis believe time and geography favour them. Former US negotiator Aaron David Miller said the group's advantage lies not only in its position near the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint but also in the asymmetry of what is at stake.
"Saudi infrastructure is much more valuable than Houthi infrastructure," he said. "They have so much less to lose than the Saudis."
Yemen analyst Farea al-Muslimi said the Houthis' campaign against Riyadh is a bid to assert regional primacy, risking a far broader conflict across the Arabian Peninsula.
At the heart of the crisis, he says, is the unravelling of a 2023 Saudi-backed peace roadmap that offered the Houthis a path to political legitimacy and reconstruction funding. Under the roadmap, Riyadh was set to help fund public sector salaries and rebuilding. The Red Sea conflict has derailed that process as the Houthis deepen their alignment with Iran.
"We're heading towards the worst outcome imaginable," al-Muslimi said. "A war worse than 2015. This time it will be bloodier, and Saudi Arabia will enter it with fewer allies."
He said no successful campaign against the Houthis was possible without Gulf unity, mainly between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. "The Houthis are not a threat to Saudi Arabia alone," he said. "They threaten the entire Gulf and the wider region. This is not simply a Saudi war. It is a Gulf war."
(This story has been refiled to remove a no comment reference to the Houthi spokesperson, in paragraph 10.)

items.title: US producer prices post largest gain in 4-1/2 years; expensive gasoline boosts retail sales
items.author: Lucia Mutikani
items.creator: Lucia Mutikani
items.summary: US producer prices increased by the most in 4-1/2 years in September amid rising costs for goods and services, the latest indication of inflation broadening out beyond energy products.
items.body:
US producer prices increased by the most in 4-1/2 years in September amid rising costs for goods and services, the latest indication of inflation broadening out beyond energy products.
The report from the Labor Department on Thursday also showed fairly large rises last month in key components that go into the calculation of the main inflation measures tracked by the Federal Reserve for its 2% target, leading some economists to still anticipate another interest rate increase this month.
Financial markets, however, continued to expect the next rate hike only in December. The government on Wednesday reported a broad increase in [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer prices"] in September. Inflation is being driven by the dragging US-Israeli war with Iran, which is keeping oil prices elevated.
Though other data on Thursday showed a stronger-than-expected increase in [USN:L1N460114 TEXT:"retail sales"] last month, that was mostly because consumers paid more for gasoline. The underlying trend in retail sales slowed, consistent with economists' expectations for softer consumer spending growth in the fourth quarter.
Inflation is outpacing wages, which have slowed amid tepid hiring, straining finances for consumers, particularly those in the lower part of what economists call a K-shaped economy.
"Today's data reinforce a challenging economic crosscurrent: inflation is heating up, the consumer is still spending but with less underlying momentum and the labor market appears frozen rather than broken," said Chris Osmond, chief investment officer at Fifth Third Wealth Advisors.
"For the Fed, that is an increasingly uncomfortable combination. A pause remains defensible, but the cost of waiting rises if inflation fails to cool."
The Producer Price Index for final demand jumped 1.3% last month, the largest gain since March 2022, after an upwardly revised 0.5% rise in August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the PPI increasing 0.5% after a previously reported 0.4% gain in August. In the 12 months through September, the PPI soared 6.3%, the biggest rise since December 2022. That followed a 5.6% advance in August.
Producer goods prices increased 2.6%, the largest increase since the government started tracking the series in December 2009. A 10.8% surge in energy prices accounted for more than 80% of the broad-based rise in goods prices. Gasoline prices rose 20.3%. Diesel fuel prices increased 21% and soared 115.2% year-on-year. Jet fuel cost more as did residential electric power.
Wholesale food prices rebounded 1.2% after declining for three straight months. Food is transported by road and rail, and last month's jump could be an early sign of the effects of record diesel prices spilling over to the broader economy.
Fresh and dry vegetable prices vaulted 41.0%, but egg prices dropped 31.9%.
Excluding the volatile food and energy components, producer goods prices rose 0.3%. The so-called core goods gained 0.4% in August. Services prices shot up 0.8% after climbing 0.2% in August. A 1.4% surge in margins for trade services accounted for nearly half of the broad-based increase in prices.
"The change in margins is an indicator firms are facing higher prices, and could pass those costs on to consumers," said Mark Streiber, economic analyst at FHN Financial.
TRANSPORTATION COSTS RISE The cost of transporting freight by road increased 3.8%, while airfares jumped 5.0%, both reflecting higher oil prices. Hotel and motel room prices shot up 5.6%. The cost of legal services rose 0.3%. Airfares, hotel and motel rooms, and legal costs are among the key components that go into the calculation of the Personal Consumption Expenditures price indexes.
Economists' estimates for the increase in September's core PCE inflation ranged from 0.31% to 0.36%, which could round up to 0.4%. That would translate to a year-over-year rise of 3.1%. Core PCE inflation gained 0.2% in August and advanced 3.0% on a year-over-year basis.
Financial markets saw a roughly 30% chance of a rate increase at the Fed's October 27-28 policy meeting, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. The odds of a rate increase were slashed by [USN:L1N45N170 TEXT:"underwhelming payroll"] gains in September as well as cooler-than-expected PCE [USN:L1N45M0L0 TEXT:"inflation readings"] for July and August.
The Fed in September raised its [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"overnight benchmark interest rate"] by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range.
Stocks on Wall Street were trading higher. The dollar eased against a basket of currencies. US Treasury yields slipped.
In a separate report, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said retail sales rose 0.8% in September after jumping 1.3% in August. Economists had forecast retail sales, which are mostly goods and are not adjusted for inflation, gaining 0.3%.
Receipts at service stations surged 6.4%. Sales at auto dealerships rose 0.2%. There were also increases in receipts at furniture, electronics and appliance stores as well as online retailers.
Sales at food services and drinking places, the only services component in the report, increased 1.1%, which economists tied to spending by higher-income households.
Receipts at building material as well as sporting goods, hobby, musical instrument and book stores fell. Sales at miscellaneous store retailers dropped 3.0%.
Retail sales excluding automobiles, gasoline, building materials and food services edged up 0.1% last month after surging 1.2% in August. These so-called core retail sales correspond most closely with the consumer spending component of gross domestic product. While economists believed consumer spending grew at above a 3.0% annualized rate in the third quarter, they saw the momentum fading by year end.
"Higher gas prices are beginning to bite because, unlike earlier in the year, there's no offset this time around from fiscal policy," said Michael Pearce, chief US economist at Oxford Economics. "We expect ... the rise in diesel prices to result in larger price hikes across a broader range of goods and services over the coming months."
Growth estimates for the July-September quarter are around a 3.0% rate. The economy grew at a 2.2% pace in the second quarter. A third report from the Labor Department showed [USN:L1N4600ZS TEXT:"initial claims"] for state unemployment benefits rose 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 199,000 last week, still near a 57-year low.
"Paychecks may not be keeping up with inflation, but at least people are still getting them," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union.

items.title: El Brent cotiza estable mientras EEUU evalúa suavizar sanciones a "flota en la sombra"
items.author: Georgina Mccartney
items.creator: Georgina Mccartney
items.summary: El precio del crudo Brent operaba prácticamente sin cambios el jueves, mientras los inversionistas sopesaban las posibles medidas de Estados Unidos para aliviar las restricciones sobre la "flota en la sombra" de petroleros, y el conflicto en Oriente Medio mantenía una prima de riesgo geopolítico en el mercado.
items.body:
El precio del crudo Brent operaba prácticamente sin cambios el jueves, mientras los inversionistas sopesaban las posibles medidas de Estados Unidos para aliviar las restricciones sobre la "flota en la sombra" de petroleros, y el conflicto en Oriente Medio mantenía una prima de riesgo geopolítico en el mercado.
* El Brent subía 2 centavos, o un 0,02%, a 106,08 dólares a las 1614 GMT. Los futuros del crudo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) de Estados Unidos ganaban 2,96 dólares, o un 3,11%, a 98,05 dólares el barril, después de que una importante reducción de las existencias de crudo de Estados Unidos contribuyó a sostener los precios.
* Los debates sobre la "flota en la sombra" se producen pocos días después de que el presidente Donald Trump levantó temporalmente las sanciones sobre el diésel ruso para mitigar la subida de los precios a nivel mundial. Las nuevas conversaciones se centran en la posibilidad de que Washington permita que el "petróleo legal" circule en buques anteriormente sancionados, dijo un funcionario estadounidense.
* El Departamento de Energía dijo que cualquier medida para aliviar las sanciones sobre la "flota en la sombra" no ayudaría a Rusia a transportar petróleo ni productos petroleros. El Departamento del Tesoro remitió las preguntas al Departamento de Energía.
* En tanto, los inventarios de crudo y de destilados de Estados Unidos descendieron, mientras que los de gasolina aumentaron la semana pasada, informó el jueves la Administración de Información de Energía (EIA).
* Las existencias de crudo descendieron en 8,6 millones de barriles, a 415,6 millones de barriles, en la semana que finalizó el 9 de octubre, según la EIA, frente a las previsiones de los analistas en una encuesta de Reuters, que apuntaban a una reducción de 288.000 barriles.
* La escalada del conflicto entre Arabia Saudita y los hutíes de Yemen, así como los nuevos ataques a buques en la región, respaldaban los precios. Un portacontenedores y un granelero se hundieron cerca del estrecho de Ormuz tras ser alcanzados por proyectiles en incidentes separados, informaron el miércoles fuentes marítimas.
* Los ataques en torno a esta vía navegable se han disparado en los últimos diez días, e Irán ha afirmado que está intensificando los ataques en respuesta al bloqueo estadounidense de sus puertos y a las sanciones más severas impuestas el mes pasado.
* En tanto, Ucrania reanudó sus ofensivas contra refinerías rusas con un ataque a una planta en la región de Riazán, después de que el presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, expresó su indignación por una "peligrosa" retirada de los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses.
* La Agencia Internacional de la Energía acordó el jueves liberar al mercado, lo antes posible, más de 20 millones de barriles de diésel, así como cualquier petróleo restante de la liberación récord de reservas de emergencia prometida en marzo, con el fin de impulsar la oferta y frenar la escalada de los precios.

FAST

Oct 15 : Scotland’s record try scorer Darcy Graham has recovered from injury more quickly than expected and been chosen to play for Edinburgh on Friday in a major boost to his country’s hopes for next month’s Nations Championship.
• The 29-year-old winger, who has 38 tries in 57 test appearances, ruptured his bicep playing for Edinburgh in a pre-season friendly last month and initial estimates were that he would be sidelined for the rest of the year.
• Graham, however, has made a speedy recovery and on Thursday was named in the Edinburgh side for their European Challenge Cup clash at home to Toulon on Friday.
• Lock Grant Gilchrist is also back after bicep surgery for Edinburgh while Scotland internationals Zander Fagerson and Kyle Steyn are in contention to return from injury for Glasgow Warriors when they take on Sale Sharks away in the Champions Cup on Saturday.
• Scotland face New Zealand, Australia and Japan at Murrayfield in the Nations Championship in November before a finals weekend fixture at Twickenham. After wins over Argentina and Fiji in July, Scotland are in contention for a place in the final.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Toby Davis)

Economist went looking into Musk’s charitable avatar. And this is what it found

The investigation, by The Economist, revealed that Musk Foundation’s leadership comprises just three people: Elon Musk, the head of his family office Jared Birchall, and another family-office employee, Matilda Simon.

Vitasta Kaul

15 October, 2026 06:14 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Elon Musk | Bloomberg photo

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

New Delhi: The world’s richest man has a complicated relationship with charity. Elon Musk has called philanthropy “bullshit”, attacked billionaire donors, and argued that his businesses do more for humanity than conventional charitable giving. But what complicates this position is that Musk runs one of America’s largest private charitable foundations, with $14.7 billion in assets.

A recent investigation by The Economist , which examined the Musk Foundation’s tax filings from July 2020 to the end of 2024, found an organisation that gives away money slowly, discloses little about its activities, and directs much of its funding toward entities linked to the billionaire himself.

The Musk Foundation is the fifth largest charitable private foundation in the US, with assets comparable to those of major philanthropic institutions. Yet its website offers just 33 words describing the causes it supports, including renewable energy, space exploration, and AI safety. Its leadership comprises Musk, the head of his family office Jared Birchall, and another family-office employee, Matilda Simon.

Show Full Article

The filings also raise questions about the tax advantages Musk receives from his donations. His largest contributions, around $8 billion worth of Tesla shares, went to the foundation in 2021 and 2022, when he acquired billions of dollars in shares and faced substantial tax liabilities.

Such donations can offer wealthy individuals a double benefit: they can avoid capital-gains tax on the shares while claiming a charitable deduction based on their market value. By the end of 2024, the Tesla stock held by the Musk Foundation had a book value of about $5.7 million, against an estimated market value of $14 billion, The Economist reported.

The bigger question is how much of this wealth reaches charitable causes. Under US law, private foundations that primarily make grants are generally required to distribute roughly 5 per cent of their investment assets annually. According to The Economist , the Musk Foundation repeatedly relied on a one-year grace period to meet its distribution obligations. By the end of 2024, it had an estimated $400 million in outstanding distribution requirements, according to Foundation Mark, a data provider.

Also read: Trump says he is No. 1 on TikTok, made $10 billion on the app. ‘Nobody appreciates me?’

‘One bucket to another’
Of the roughly $1 billion the foundation distributed between 2020 and 2024, almost a tenth went to Fidelity Charitable, which operates donor-advised funds. These accounts allow donors to set aside money for charitable purposes without requiring immediate distribution to end recipients. Such transfers are legal, but expert Brian Mittendorf told The Economist that they ran against the spirit of the rules, amounting to moving money “from one bucket to another bucket”.

More than 58 per cent of the foundation’s grants went to The Foundation, a charity led by Birchall that shares the Musk Foundation’s address. It says it aims to build schools focused on science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. However, its activities and use of funds remain unclear.

Musk previously funded Ad Astra, a private school near SpaceX’s former California headquarters that enrolled fewer than 50 students, including his children. The school was wound down around the Covid-19 pandemic, while its website says a new school in Texas is in development.

Other donations appear connected to Musk’s business interests. A $55 million contribution to a children’s hospital in 2021 helped fellow billionaire Jared Isaacman meet a fundraising target for a SpaceX mission organised as a charitable endeavour. The foundation also made donations to non-profit groups in southern Texas following a SpaceX rocket explosion that scattered debris across the area.

Its remaining grants span disparate causes, from sea-lion conservation to spinal medicine, without an obvious overarching strategy. Meanwhile, Musk has shown greater enthusiasm for political giving, donating at least $275 million dollars to Republicans ahead of America’s midterm elections.

(Edited by Aamaan Alam Khan)
