items.title: Market selloff, rising rates test AI data centre deal boom
items.author: Yantoultra Ngui, Kane Wu, Clare Jim
items.creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Kane Wu, Clare Jim
items.summary: A market selloff is forcing companies driving the global AI boom to delay fundraising plans or pay more for capital as investors demand proof they can absorb rising interest rates and computing-power costs.
items.body:
A [USN:L6N4610C5 TEXT:"market selloff"] is forcing companies driving the global AI boom to delay fundraising plans or pay more for capital as investors demand proof they can absorb rising interest rates and computing-power costs.
The shift comes as investors reassess whether the companies racing to build the infrastructure underpinning artificial intelligence can generate returns that justify soaring spending on computing power, land and energy.
In the past week alone, as AI-related stocks have weakened and the debt of data-centre operator [USN:L8N4610AR TEXT:"CoreWeave"] has slumped towards distressed prices, listings for a Blackstone-backed [USN:L4N45Z0H4 TEXT:"AirTrunk"] REIT, Nvidia-backed [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"Firmus"] and SoftBank-backed [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"SB Energy"] have either been pulled or paused.
The increased scrutiny is not derailing investment in the sector, analysts said, but it is forcing investors to distinguish more sharply between business models and levels of execution risk.
"The conversation has shifted from growth at any cost to a much sharper focus on quality," said Harry Evans, a partner at law firm Freshfields.
Evans said deal activity could hold up through next year, thanks to a strong pipeline.
Recent listing setbacks, however, show investors are becoming more discerning about valuations, leverage and business models.
M&A involving Asian data centres is still on track for a record year, reaching $21.3 billion as of Tuesday, according to Dealogic data, more than double the $10 billion recorded in all of 2025.
Debt financing has also remained strong, with syndicated loans and bond issuance totalling $22.3 billion so far this year.
Equity capital market fundraising for the sector, however, is down, at $5.4 billion so far this year, a 4.6% drop from the same period in 2025.
"General thoughts with IPOs are that they often seek 'hype', as they're largely looking for oversubscription," said Nicholas Tuan, director, APAC Advisory Services at real estate services firm Savills.
"There may not be fundamental asset value when you peel it all back."
Firmus, which had aimed to raise $5 billion in what would have been Australia's second-largest stock market listing, struggled to convince investors it could deliver on ambitious revenue projections while carrying about $30 billion of debt.
Nuclear services company [USN:L4N4581N6 TEXT:"Holtec"] cited a "[USN:L4N45H14U TEXT:"perfect storm"]", driven mainly by uncertainty around data-centre demand, when it pulled its US listing last month.
HIGHER RATES TEST VALUATIONS Higher borrowing costs are at the heart of the new scrutiny.
Benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields posted their sharpest quarterly rise this century last month, prompting investors to take a closer look at whether projected revenues can support growing debt burdens, bankers said.
Gary Goh, CEO of Sprint DC Consulting, an Asia-Pacific data centre consultancy firm based in Kuala Lumpur, warned higher financing costs could lead to sharp valuation corrections.
Valuations can vary widely depending on whether they are based on existing customer contracts or future projections, and whether capital expenditure requirements are fully reflected, said a banker who advises data-centre investors.
"There is not remotely enough data centres built for the demand," said the banker, who was not authorised to speak publicly. "Investors are still going in but the question is at what valuation."
Investors are also paying closer attention to execution risks.
Beyond higher power and water costs, developers face [USN:L1N45M0CN TEXT:"growing opposition"] in some markets over electricity use, noise and environmental concerns, adding to regulatory uncertainty around new projects.
Securing suitable land and power supplies is becoming more difficult in some jurisdictions, said a person at a US-based firm that invests in Asian data-centre platforms, adding that the company had tightened its underwriting criteria because of geopolitical and policy risks.
To be sure, major transactions are still [USN:L6N460198 TEXT:"moving ahead"].
Singapore-based DayOne is expected to go public as soon as November, seeking to raise up to $5 billion, Reuters [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"reported"] in September. DayOne did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
AirTrunk, despite postponing a planned REIT listing, is nearing a deal to sell its Johor data centre in Malaysia to a group of investors including local pension fund KWAP at a valuation of about $1 billion, according to two people familiar with the matter.
Bain Capital has also received final bids for at least 40% of its pan-Asian platform Bridge Data Centres in a deal that could value the business at around $5 billion, according to two people with knowledge of the process.
AirTrunk's backer Blackstone and Bain Capital declined to comment. KWAP said it was not in a position to comment.
Still, investors are likely to differentiate between established wholesale operators with long-term customer commitments and stable revenue, and higher-risk "neoclouds" and "AI-campus builders", said John Dinsdale, chief analyst at TechInsights.
"The question for investors is less whether demand will expand than which business models and companies will be best placed to capture that growth sustainably."

India scores zero on six parameters in global climate and health scorecard

The 2026 Global Healthy NDC Scorecard by the Global Climate and Health Alliance scored 132 countries on their climate action plans, or Nationally Determined Contributions.

Akanksha Mishra

15 October, 2026 06:12 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

A man sleeps in his rickshaw during a heatwave on a hot summer day in New Delhi, India, June 18, 2024. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) classified nine heat wave days in Delhi this June, up sharply from the historic norm of one during the month. Scientists say the heat is being worsened by human-driven climate change. | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

New Delhi: India is the fifth-lowest scorer in the annual Global Healthy NDC Scorecard, which assesses countries based on how much they integrate public health action into their climate commitments. Despite high air pollution deaths, the country’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement do not mention health-related impacts of climate change or implement specific climate-health-related policies.

The report, 2026 Healthy NDC Scorecard, was released on 14 October by the Global Climate and Health Alliance, an international organisation, which scored 132 countries on their climate action plans or NDCs. The scoring methodology evaluated how frequently the plans were mentioned and included health-related measures relating to climate change, especially in air pollution, just transition, health economics, and finance. 

Climate-preparedness report 
Colombia was the highest-scoring country out of all 132 countries, scoring 29 out of 32 points, with its integrated climate action plan, which mentions the right to a healthy environment and health. Also, Colombia’s plan mentioned climate-related illnesses, the impact on nutrition and food security, and also a comprehensive air pollution reduction programme. 

Show Full Article

Apart from Colombia, other high-scoring countries include Nigeria, Cambodia and Paraguay, all of which explicitly mention specific health impacts of climate change and actions taken by their governments, as well as targets for future action. 

“The Healthy NDC Scorecard enables us to evaluate how governments are considering health in their climate planning,” said Dr Nova Tebbe, postdoctoral researcher at GCHA and research lead of the study. 

India, Japan, Liechtenstein, and New Zealand are the lowest-scoring countries in the report, with very few links between their climate action plans and public health. Moreover, India and Japan’s emissions reduction targets too are seen to be not aligned with the Paris Agreement. 

India scored a zero on six out of eight parameters in the report, indicating that it did not quantify the health impacts of climate change, did not name air pollutants, did not have policies for adaptation in the healthcare sector, or refer to just transitions from the perspective of worker health and vulnerable populations. 

Also read: World’s oldest shipwreck discovered near Türkiye, reveals 4,700-year-old pottery vessels

High score for the Global South
Other high-emitting countries like China, EU, US and the UK, also did not score well, getting less than 10 points each. While they did mention health in their NDCs, they did not match it with strong emissions reduction targets.

“In the past months, floods have killed hundreds of people in Nepal, millions of children are at risk of hunger in Eastern and Southern Africa, Europe and the United States have seen widespread heat-related mortality and hundreds of wildfires have raged in Canada,” said Tebbe in the press release. 

“Clearly, climate action must be taken immediately, and implemented rapidly.”

The report mentioned how while most NDCs include mentions of health and air quality, fewer directly quantify these health-impacts of climate change. Only about 15 per cent of all NDCs surveyed actually linked health to just transitions, and only 15 per cent included their Ministry of Health in drafting their NDCs. 

“The fact that the highest scores go to countries in the Global South reflects lived realities – these countries do not have the luxury of pretending that climate change and health can be separated,” said Jess Beagley, Policy Lead, GCHA, in a press release.

US Treasury pushes global partners to rename AI as 'super intelligence'

Erin Browne, US Under Secretary of the Treasury for International Affairs, speaks during an interview with Reuters at the IMF/World Bank 2026 Annual Meetings at Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) in Bangkok, Thailand, October 15, 2026. REUTERS/Athit Perawongmetha

BANGKOK, Oct 15 : The United States wants its global partners to rename artificial intelligence as "super intelligence," convinced that the new moniker better reflects the emerging technology, a top US Treasury official told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
Treasury Undersecretary for International Affairs Erin Browne said Washington was in negotiations with other shareholders of the International Monetary Fund about using the new term in a statement being drafted by the fund's steering committee, the International Monetary and Financial Committee.
US President Donald Trump last month directed US government agencies to use the words "super intelligence" instead of "artificial intelligence" when referring to the technology.
Browne said the United States, which holds the rotating presidency of the Group of 20 major economies, wanted the change to take hold internationally as well.

"President Trump has been really clear on this, and he's, you know, using the term SI, and I think it's a clear priority for the US to use that term, and we think that more appropriately encapsulates the technology at hand," Browne said.
She declined to comment on whether Washington would refuse to sign off on the statement unless the switch was made.
"We're still in the middle of negotiations on that statement, so I'm not going to, you know, sort of run ahead of that," she said.
A source familiar with the matter said US officials had suggested during meetings on the IMFC statement that they would insist on the new language, raising eyebrows among some other IMFC members.
If Washington withholds its support for a consensus statement, the current IMFC chair, Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed Al-Jadaan, could still issue a so-called chair's statement summarizing the views of the members.
One possibility might involve skipping a mention of SI or AI and focusing on "new technology" instead, the source said.
The IMFC will hold a news conference and release any agreed statement led by Al-Jadaan and IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva on Saturday.
"We see this as a driving force behind American growth and global growth," Browne said.
"Many countries are looking to the US to set the standards, as well as to set the path forward for SI development and how that can really enhance and boost growth and productivity on a global basis."

Source: Reuters

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Clara Denina　Olivia Kumwenda-Mtambo

［ロンドン／ヨハネスブルグ　１５日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Clara Denina　Olivia Kumwenda-Mtambo

［ロンドン／ヨハネスブルグ　１５日　ロイター］ - 「カルティエ」や「ヴァンクリーフ＆アーペル」などを持つスイスの高級ブランド大手リシュモンが、英資源大手アングロ・アメリカンが売却を進めているダイヤモンド採掘大手デビアスの買収コンソーシアム（企業連合）に参加する方向で協議している。事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。

買収が実現すれば、リシュモンは、ダイヤのサプライチェーン（供給網）の重要部分に対する影響力を強化できる。

アングロは、ダイヤモンド価格の下落や人工ダイヤモンドの需要拡大を受け、大規模な事業再編の一環として２０２４年５月にデビアスを売りに出した。

デビアスの評価額は約１０億ドルとされている。ブルームバーグの報道によると、リシュモンは、デビアスのギャレス・ペニー元最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が率いる企業連合「グローバル・ダイヤモンド・コンソーシアム」への参加について協議している。協議は進展しているものの、リシュモンが企業連合に参加する確証はないという。

デビアスについては、ボツワナが優先交渉権を有する。同国政府は権利を行使するかどうかをまだ明らかにしていない。ボツワナ大統領府の報道官は１３日、合意が成立して署名されるまで政府としてコメントしないと述べた。

FAST

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 15 : Manchester City will attempt to keep their perfect Premier League start rolling at home to Ipswich Town on Saturday, with uncertainty over their punishment for financial rule breaches continuing to hang over the leaders.
Enzo Maresca's City have won their opening six league games and sit three points clear of Arsenal, making a fine start on the pitch while their future off it remains unresolved.
An independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League. City have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal.
The extraordinary backdrop has done little to derail City's domestic campaign. They underlined their strength with a 3-0 victory at 10-man Liverpool last Sunday.

The did lose 4-2 at home to holders Paris St Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday but return to the Etihad Stadium to face an Ipswich side sitting 10th on nine points.
Former Manchester United defender Gary Neville said the uncertainty over City's eventual punishment had created wider frustration around the league, with the club continuing to win while the significance of those victories, with potential sanctions still to come, remained unclear.
"This is not good for the Premier League, this is really bad for the Premier League — it's going to continue for a few months," Neville said on Sky Sports. "Up and down the country, (there's) a lot of annoyance that they see this team win football matches; it's just not going to be enjoyed."
For champions Arsenal, who demolished Lille 3-0 in the Champions League on Tuesday, there is little room to surrender points if they are to keep pace in the title race.
The London side sit second on 15 points and visit Nottingham Forest on Sunday knowing any slip could allow City to open a significant early gap. Forest are 15th with five points.
SPECTACULAR LIVERPOOL VICTORY
Liverpool will arrive at Brentford on Saturday with a different kind of momentum after a spectacular 6-3 Champions League victory at LASK on Wednesday.
The night in Austria belonged to Bradley Barcola, whose hat-trick represented his first goals for Liverpool after going scoreless in his opening six appearances for the club.
The French forward, whose frustrating start with the Reds had drawn increasing scrutiny, struck twice before halftime and completed his treble after the break as Liverpool made it two wins from two in the Champions League.
It was a badly needed breakthrough for 24-year-old Barcola and a welcome response from Liverpool after their humbling home defeat by City four days earlier.
Liverpool have been far less convincing domestically, however. They are ninth on nine points and face a Brentford side sitting a point above them in fourth, meaning Saturday could provide a sterner examination of whether the Reds' nine-goal European thriller has genuinely shifted their momentum.
Manchester United's problems are more acute as they make the short trip to Elland Road to face Leeds United on Sunday desperate to breathe life into a troubled campaign.
Michael Carrick's side have collected six points from their opening six games and sit 13th, already 12 points behind City after their worst start in 40 years.
United slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday and their latest assignment carries an additional edge against old rivals Leeds, who have made the stronger start and sit seventh with nine points.
Three teams are still searching for their first victory, including bottom side Fulham who welcome Hull City on Saturday, Bournemouth who host Sunderland on Sunday and Tottenham Hotspur who are at home to Coventry City on Monday.
With Manchester City trying to shut out the noise around their financial case, Arsenal determined to stay on their heels and Liverpool and United searching for a revival, the weekend should help show how the traditional heavyweights are coping.

Source: Reuters

Oct 15 : European physics research centre CERN and Mistral AI have established a long-term strategic partnership to develop a foundation model for scientific discovery, the two organisations said on Thursday.
The statement of intent gives the French AI company access to one of the world's largest scientific datasets as it seeks to compete on frontier science.
Mistral Chief Executive Arthur Mensch wrote in an article published in Le Monde on Thursday that frontier models were "now indispensable to scientific progress" and criticised companies that keep their advantages to themselves.
CERN Chief Information Officer Enrica Porcari said the new partnership would "advance AI capabilities that can serve the whole physics community and be shared".

The partners aim to build a "Large Physics Model", called "Flare", which CERN said in a statement would be the first foundation model for collider physics, trained on billions of simulated particle collisions. 
It will use the same idea as the large language models behind generative AI but be trained on collision data rather than text, a CERN spokesperson told Reuters.
It is meant to replace some specialised algorithms now used to reconstruct and identify particles.
The spokesperson said CERN has been using AI to turn raw data from experiments into pictures of the events for a decade, but with multiple tools used for each step.
CERN holds about one exabyte, or 1 million terabytes, of experimental data from the Large Hadron Collider, and expects the volume of collisions to increase tenfold after its ongoing upgrade, expected around 2030. 
"High-energy physics provides a unique environment in which artificial intelligence can be developed and tested with exceptional rigour," Porcari said. 
No timeline or budget was disclosed. Both sides said the models could later serve other sciences.
The Paris-based lab, broadly viewed as Europe's best chance to catch up with US and Chinese competitors, this month unveiled a new open-weight model it says can challenge its rivals. It will be released to the public on October 27.
Users can download open-weight models from platforms and use them on their own hardware.

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 15 : The dollar retreated from an 18-month peak on Thursday as investors looked past strong US inflation and spending data to focus on a shakeout in the securities of AI data center firms.
US producer prices rose by the most in 4-1/2 years in September as goods and services costs increased, adding to evidence that inflation pressures are spreading beyond energy.
Retail sales rose more than expected last month, lifted by higher gasoline prices, while weekly jobless claims marginally increased, pointing to resilient consumer demand and a stable labor market.
But government bonds rallied and the dollar pulled back, reflecting cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials that further cooled expectations for an October interest-rate hike.

"The hotter (producer prices) print reinforces the inflation concerns raised by CPI, but our view remains that much of the associated Fed hawkishness is already priced in, leaving limited room for further upside in US yields and the dollar," said Joel Kruger, a market strategist at LMAX Group in London.
AI COMPANIES' DEBT BURDENS
The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, fell 0.44 per cent to 102.00, having hit an 18-month high on Wednesday after US inflation figures came in stronger than expected.
That helped the euro bounce 0.48 per cent from an 18-month trough to $1.1210, putting it on track for its biggest daily gain in nearly two months. Sterling strengthened 0.45 per cent to $1.3251 after data showed Britain's economy unexpectedly grew 0.1 per cent in August. 
Markets grew choppy after Wednesday's hot US CPI reading initially bolstered bets on higher-for-longer Fed rates, while renewed concerns over AI companies' heavy debt burdens fuelled safe-haven flows into Treasuries.
"The selloff in chip stocks offers support to bonds, helping keep yields in check despite the inflationary signals," said Uto Shinohara, senior investment strategist at Mesirow Currency Management.
Traders now see a 72 per cent chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, compared with 53 per cent a month ago, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed.
The likelihood seen of a hike rose sharply after the CPI report, but bets eased after Fed officials including Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said the central bank could wait for more clarity before the meeting.
"FX markets are currently taking a break from the USD rally that began in mid-September, boosted by faith that the Federal Reserve was willing to hike interest rates to fight inflation," said Juan Perez, director of trading at Monex USA in Washington.
"If those tools are not working, then the worry is about stubborn 'stagflation'."
Investors will also watch remarks from Fed officials including Chair Kevin Warsh at IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday for clues on the US central bank's next move. 
The Australian dollar weakened 0.88 per cent to $0.6911, after local employment unexpectedly slid in September, while the Japanese yen strengthened 0.32 per cent to 157.82 per dollar.

items.title: US 10-year Treasury yield levels not unprecedented, BNY CEO says
items.author: Saeed Azhar, Arasu Basil, Pritam Biswas
items.creator: Saeed Azhar, Arasu Basil, Pritam Biswas
items.summary: The levels the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield has touched this year are not unprecedented, the CEO of the oldest US bank told Reuters, as a bruising selloff in government debt lifted yields to multi-decade highs.
items.body:
The levels the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield has touched this year are not unprecedented, the CEO of the oldest US bank (BNY.N) told Reuters, as a [USN:L1N45V0NY TEXT:"bruising selloff in government debt"] lifted yields to multi-decade highs.
The 10-year US Treasury yield, a yardstick for global borrowing costs and asset prices, posted its [USN:L8N45N0KW TEXT:"sharpest rise since 1994"] in the July-September period.
"We got 10-year rates to like, call it five and a quarter. There's nothing particularly unusual in history about 10-year rates at that level. We've had arguably low levels for a very long time," BNY CEO Robin Vince said in an interview with Reuters on Thursday.
"People get very caught up. It has happened quickly, for sure, but with what I would view as more of a normalization of the curve."
Global bond markets have come under intense pressure this year as energy prices remain elevated, while the AI boom is supporting economic growth, a combination that has heightened worries about inflation and rising interest rates.
"You can make a good case that it is actually the strength of the US economy that's one of the primary drivers of inflation and the move higher in rates," Vince said.
Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management, echoed Vince's views.
"The bigger adjustment may be psychological. Investors, borrowers and businesses may simply need to get used to these levels. There will be swings along the way, but I would not assume we are going back to the ultra-low-rate world anytime soon," Jacobsen said.
AI ROUT The latest hot US inflation report [USN:L6N4600XF TEXT:"sent rate-hike bets soaring"] and deepened investor concerns about the [USN:L6N460140 TEXT:"risks posed by rising borrowing costs"] in the capital-intensive AI industry.
[USN:L6N460140 TEXT:"This week's rout in AI stocks"] eased some pressure on the bond markets, with investors flocking to safe-haven government debt in the face of the tech selloff, pushing US yields down across the curve.
The 10-year Treasury yield was [USN:L8N4610QB TEXT:"headed for the largest one-day decline"] since early August 2025 on Thursday.
Asked about financial structures in the AI landscape, Vince said on a post-earnings media call on Thursday that over time weak structures will get exposed, and that's the evolution of financial markets and the development of things.
DEPOSITS EXPECTED TO PICK UP IN Q4 In a statement, Vince said that client demand is continuing to grow and BNY's sales and pipelines remain very healthy across products and regions.
[USN:L1N3I80VH TEXT:"BNY has grown into the world's largest custodian"]. The company sits at the center of global capital markets, safeguarding and administering trillions of dollars in client assets, while processing trades and moving securities and cash between financial institutions.
Average deposits are expected to pick up in the fourth quarter along with client activity, Chief Financial Officer Dermot McDonogh told Reuters.
BNY on Thursday reported a 20% jump in profit applicable to common shareholders to $1.61 billion in the third quarter, driven by interest income growth and stronger market levels that boosted the value of client assets. Assets under custody and administration rose 10% to $63.4 trillion from a year earlier.
The New York-based firm is also benefiting from a rise in interest rates as it reinvests cash from maturing investment securities at higher yields.
Net interest income — the spread between earnings from assets and costs on liabilities — accounts for roughly 25% of BNY's revenue, McDonogh said.

Oct 15 : India's Tech Mahindra on Thursday maintained its fiscal 2027 operating margin target after beating expectations for second-quarter revenue, helped by a ramp-up in large deals across communications and other businesses.
The IT services company said it remained on track to deliver a 15 per cent operating margin for the fiscal year, although Chief Executive Mohit Joshi said its focus was increasingly shifting to growth after an earlier push to improve profitability.
New deal wins during the quarter stood at $1.02 billion, up 25.4 per cent from a year earlier.
Indian IT firms are competing for large outsourcing and technology-transformation contracts as clients seek higher productivity from AI, even as concerns rise about the technology's impact on traditional labour-intensive work.

Almost all of Tech Mahindra's large deals now include an AI component, Joshi said, adding that the company plans to start reporting AI-related revenue in defined buckets in the second half of the fiscal year.
Tech Mahindra noted that higher productivity demands linked to AI were being offset by opportunities in modernisation, data and new applications, which the company expects to expand the market for technology services.
Consolidated revenue for the second quarter rose 15.6 per cent to 161.80 billion rupees ($1.70 billion) year-on-year, beating analysts' average estimate of 151.95 billion rupees, according to LSEG data.
Revenue from the communications division, which accounts for a third of the Pune-based company's total, rose 9.5 per cent year-on-year. Revenue from its manufacturing division, its second-largest, grew 7 per cent.
Banking and financial services segment revenue, which Tech Mahindra has been pushing to expand in recent quarters, was up 4.6 per cent.
Joshi said financial services business growth in the next quarter could return to the around 8.5 per cent year-on-year pace seen in the previous quarter, or higher.
Profit rose 32.7 per cent to 15.86 billion rupees, but missed estimates of 17.08 billion rupees.
The company's board also recommended a one-for-one bonus share issue and declared an interim dividend of 15 rupees per share.
Meanwhile, larger peer TCS posted its weakest September-quarter sequential revenue growth in three years despite a jump in AI-related revenue, while HCLTech flagged a volatile demand environment. Wipro reported higher quarterly revenue earlier on Thursday.

Netflix to layoff around 1,000 employees in biggest job cuts since 2022

The latest move comes as Netflix faces pressure from media rivals, including free platforms such as YouTube.

Himanshi Aggarwal

New Delhi: Netflix is set to lay off roughly 6 per cent of its workforce, or about 1,000 employees globally, in its largest round of job cuts since 2022.

According to a CNBC report , co-chief executives Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos informed employees of the layoffs in a company-wide email on Wednesday. Most of the reductions will affect the product, technology, legal, and human resources teams.  

“Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritise our people and resources,” Peters and Sarandos wrote in the memo. “Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast.” 

Show Full Article

Netflix had approximately 16,000 full-time employees at the end of last year. Its shares, which are down around 25 per cent so far this year, rose about 0.7 per cent on the day of the announcement.

Largest layoffs since 2022
The latest cuts mark Netflix’s widest round of layoffs since 2022, when the company reduced its workforce after recording its first subscriber losses in more than a decade. That year, about 450 employees were laid off across two rounds of cuts. 

The latest move comes as Netflix faces pressure from media rivals, including free platforms such as YouTube, and a consolidating entertainment industry. Earlier this year, Netflix lost a bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery’s streaming and studio assets to Paramount Skydance. 

“We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation,” the memo said.  

“Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.”

Also Read: Netflix ‘not growing as fast as I want’, says co-CEO Sarandos

Netflix looks beyond subscriptions
In recent months, Netflix has expanded beyond its subscription-based business by growing its advertising tier, experimenting with live programming and investing in gaming. Yet engagement metrics have softened, and Nielsen data show Netflix’s share of US television viewing time declining as YouTube’s has risen.   

At the Bloomberg Screentime conference in Los Angeles, Peters had previously acknowledged that the company was not growing as quickly as he wanted.

“Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster,” he said at the conference. “We are, though, also doing things that create a lot of headwind to that number.”

Revenue continues to grow
Despite the layoffs, Netflix remains profitable. In its most recently reported quarter, revenue rose 13 per cent year-on-year to $12.6 billion.

In their memo, Peters and Sarandos also emphasised support for departing employees.

“Decisions like these are never easy, and we don’t take them lightly,” they wrote. “Our top priority today is to support those who are leaving Netflix.”

LONDON, Oct 15 : The cost of insuring against the risk of potential US tech defaults has hit record levels, in the latest sign of credit stress building in the so-called AI trade, especially for data centre operators like CoreWeave that depend on future revenue.
Although shares in companies driving the AI boom are still among the biggest gainers on global equity markets this year, many have fallen sharply in the past few weeks, as investors reassess the cost of capital against a backdrop of rising interest rates and inflation.
There are also doubts among some investors and analysts about when, and in some cases, if, the billions of dollars pouring into data centres, computer power and other infrastructure will pay off.
Demand for AI-linked credit default swaps (CDS), a form of insurance against default that gained prominence during the 2008 financial crisis, meanwhile has soared, even for heavyweights like Apple, Amazon and Microsoft.

For some of their more heavily indebted competitors, suppliers and customers the cost of CDS has risen even faster.
WHAT IS A CDS?
A derivative that provides protection against the risk that a bond issuer, whether a company or government, fails to meet its debt obligations.
Bond investors expect to receive interest payments and repayment of principal when a bond matures, but they bear the risk that those payments may not be made.
Buying CDS helps investors hedge that risk by effectively providing insurance against a default or other credit event. If the value of a bond drops for any reason, an investor might add to their CDS holdings to help offset that, for example.
None of the companies whose CDS have risen recently have defaulted on their obligations or signalled that they may do so.
IS THIS A BIG MARKET?
The market for single-name CDS, which cover the bonds of a single issuer, is worth about $9 trillion, the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) said.
That is a small portion of global bond markets, which have more than $150 trillion of debt securities outstanding, Bank for International Settlements data shows.
The biggest CDS market is for government debt.
Average daily CDS trading across the market was $16 billion in the second quarter, up from $13 billion a year earlier, the most recent data from the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation shows. Saudi Arabia is the most actively traded.
But average daily trades, even for large companies, can sometimes be in the single digits, or fewer than 10 a day, meaning small transactions can have an outsized impact on prices.
WHO BUYS CDS?
Bond investors typically buy CDS through an intermediary, often an investment bank, which then finds a financial firm to issue an insurance policy on the bonds. These are "over-the-counter" deals that do not go through a central clearing house.
Hedge funds also participate in the market, selling CDS to investors seeking to hedge exposure.
The buyer pays a fee, called a premium, at regular intervals to the seller, which assumes the risk of a credit event.
CDS are quoted as a credit spread, which is the number of basis points (bps) that the seller of the derivative charges the buyer for providing protection. The higher the perceived risk of a credit event, the wider the spread.
A CDS quoted at 100 bps costs $1 annually to insure every $100 of debt.
WHAT'S GOING ON WITH TECH CDS?
CDS for CoreWeave, a heavily indebted data centre operator at the eye of the current storm, have now topped 1,100 bps for the first time, S&P Global Market Intelligence data show.
They suggest a roughly 63 per cent chance of a default over the next five years, up from around 30 per cent a year ago.
Tech CDS moves reflect investor concern over how quickly massive investments in AI will translate into profits, and whether heavily indebted companies can generate returns fast enough to service mounting interest costs.
Oracle has seen its CDS trade at nearly 300 bps, well above those of other AI-linked companies.
Nvidia CDS have also risen sharply in recent weeks to around 90 bps, Meta CDS are trading around 105 bps.
By comparison, an index of investment-grade CDS is trading around 62 bps.
WHAT TRIGGERS A CDS PAYOUT?
A CDS pays out following a credit event, which can include a bankruptcy or a failure by an issuer to make bond payments.
When concerns about an issuer's creditworthiness increase, demand for protection typically rises, widening CDS spreads.
Payouts are not a given. When Swiss lender Credit Suisse collapsed and was taken over by rival UBS in 2023, the EMEA Credit Derivatives Determinations Committee (CDDC) ruled that event would not trigger a CDS payout.
IF IT'S INSURANCE, WHAT'S THE PROBLEM?
CDS provide a hedge for bondholders. But rising perceived risk pushes up the cost of protection, which can prompt investors to sell bonds and raise borrowing costs for issuers.
That can amplify concerns about creditworthiness and potentially create a self-reinforcing cycle.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Venture Global inks deals with GE Vernova, Baker Hughes for power expansion
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Venture Global said on Thursday it had signed deals with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes to support up to 16 new power generation units, advancing plans to develop off-grid power capacity that could support AI data centers and its LNG operations.
items.body:
Venture Global (VG.N) said on Thursday it had signed deals with GE Vernova (GEV.N) and Baker Hughes (BKR.O) to support up to 16 new power generation units, advancing plans to develop off-grid power capacity that could support AI data centers and its LNG operations.
The rapid growth of data centers has fueled interest in behind-the-meter power projects as developers seek to secure dedicated electricity supplies without adding strain to already constrained public power grids.
Here are more details:
The agreements cover up to 16 power-island units of 720 megawatts each, alongside associated transformer equipment
Venture said the units could support up to 10 gigawatts of compute capacity by the end of 2034, subject to customer commitments and market demand
The company expects to place its first order for a power island by the end of 2026
The gas-fired, combined-cycle units would operate behind-the-meter, without drawing on public power grids or water utilities, the company said
Any third-party data center development would be separate from and complementary to its LNG operations and would not affect existing LNG sales commitments, Venture said
The company plans to file its first permit applications this week. Additional equipment orders will depend on future commercial and operational requirements
This new capacity would expand on the company's 4.5 GW of gas-fired generation that powers its facilities in island mode, allowing the plants to operate independently of the grid

items.title: CoreWeave's slump spotlights growing burden of debt behind AI boom
items.author: Aditya Soni, Anhata Rooprai
items.creator: Aditya Soni, Anhata Rooprai
items.summary: Shares and bonds of Nvidia-backed CoreWeave tumbled again on Thursday despite CEO assurances about its strong deal backlog, laying bare a growing crisis of confidence in an AI build-out increasingly financed with borrowed money.
items.body:
Shares and bonds of Nvidia-backed CoreWeave (CRWV.O) tumbled again on Thursday despite CEO assurances about its strong deal backlog, laying bare a growing crisis of confidence in an AI build-out increasingly financed with borrowed money.
The loss-making AI cloud company is burdened with about $50 billion in debt and has become the poster child for concerns that the data center boom is being fueled by credit, straining newer players and pressuring cash flows even at giants such as Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Meta Platforms (META.O) .
CoreWeave's slump has fueled a global rout in AI stocks, underscoring investor doubts about whether future revenue from the technology can keep pace with the spending.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company is CoreWeave's second-largest investor with about a 10% stake, played down the fears. "CoreWeave’s financial strength is improving every day," Huang told reporters at a Stockholm event, adding that he does not see a need for Nvidia to backstop the company. "I'm optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing."
CoreWeave stock was last down nearly 2% after slipping as much as 8.3% to its lowest level since May 2025, extending the more than 15% slide from Wednesday and ranking among the biggest decliners in the tech selloff.
"The market is waking up to the fact that AI demand and a profitable business model are two very different things," said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG Group.
"It looks more like investors questioning how the build-out is being funded than a sudden collapse in appetite for AI computing. But if the cost of capital keeps rising, even strong demand may not be enough to protect the most heavily leveraged players."
The jitters come as [USN:L6N4601DE TEXT:"investors await Anthropic's IPO"], which would be a test of whether the Claude AI model maker's rapid revenue growth can ease worries about runaway AI spending.
The market selloff has already led some companies such as [USN:L4N45L0SK TEXT:"smart ring maker Oura"] (OURA.O) to [USN:L4N45V00M TEXT:"push back their listings"].
The yield on CoreWeave's April-issued bonds due 2031 was near 16%, above the level that typically signals distress, drawing a "yikes" from Elon Musk on social media. The bond was last down 0.3 cents on the dollar to 79.15 cents, according to Tradeweb data.
The [USN:L1N46104Z TEXT:"cost of insuring its debt"] against default has climbed to around 1,000 basis points, implying a nearly 63% chance of default in five years, up from about 30% a year ago. That is despite a deal under which Nvidia (NVDA.O) will buy any unsold CoreWeave capacity through April 13, 2032.
CoreWeave, [USN:L3N3QB14S TEXT:"which went public in March 2025"], leads newer cloud providers known as neoclouds that rent out computing power from scarce and costly Nvidia processors to meet soaring demand, often borrowing heavily to buy the chips. It counts Microsoft and OpenAI among its customers, according to media reports.
That leaves neoclouds exposed to any cooling in AI demand, critics have said, while the chips lose value as newer ones arrive, forcing another round of heavy spending to replace them.
CoreWeave [USN:L4N4481ER TEXT:"raised its annual capital spending forecast"] by $4 billion to as much as $39 billion in August. It is expected to post revenue of nearly $13 billion this year and a loss of $2.13 billion, according to analysts' estimates.
Worries about the build-out, on which US tech giants are expected to spend more than $700 billion this year, have in recent days rippled through the stocks that have been the biggest winners since ChatGPT's November 2022 launch.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (.SOX) , a closely watched gauge of chip stocks, has erased over $1.6 trillion in market value in an 11.6% slide over the past six sessions. The Nasdaq (.NDX) has declined more than 3% in the period.
On Thursday, tech shares fell across Asia, Europe and the US, dragging broader markets lower on fears that rising interest rates could hurt the sector.
CoreWeave's neocloud rivals Nebius (NBIS.O) , Applied Digital (APLD.O) and Iren (IREN.O) fell between 3% and 7%. In Asia, SoftBank (9984.T) , which has bet heavily on OpenAI, closed down 9.3%.
'UNLIMITED' POOLS OF CAPITAL The CoreWeave selloff came as its co-founder Brannin McBee told the Financial Times that the company was seeking an investment-grade rating that would open the door to "unlimited" capital.
The same day research firm Gartner said about 80% of neoclouds could shut down by 2030 and that more than $3.5 trillion of AI spending could face impairment if AI providers keep up their current pace of investment.
"In 2026, AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure, and are forecast to invest an additional $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030," said Will Sommer, analyst at Gartner.
"However, our research indicates enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures during this period."
CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator pushed back on the concerns in an [USN:L4N4601XL TEXT:"internal memo on Wednesday"] seen by Reuters, telling employees the company's deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations and that markets can sometimes "misunderstand and act irrationally".

On Thursday, tech shares fell across Asia, Europe and the US, dragging broader markets lower on fears that rising interest rates could hurt the sector.
CoreWeave's neocloud rivals Nebius, Applied Digital and Iren fell between 3 per cent and 7 per cent. In Asia, SoftBank, which has bet heavily on OpenAI, closed down 9.3 per cent.
'UNLIMITED' POOLS OF CAPITAL
The CoreWeave selloff came as its co-founder Brannin McBee told the Financial Times that the company was seeking an investment-grade rating that would open the door to "unlimited" capital.
The same day research firm Gartner said about 80 per cent of neoclouds could shut down by 2030 and that more than $3.5 trillion of AI spending could face impairment if AI providers keep up their current pace of investment.
"In 2026, AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure, and are forecast to invest an additional $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030," said Will Sommer, analyst at Gartner.
"However, our research indicates enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures during this period."
CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator pushed back on the concerns in an internal memo on Wednesday seen by Reuters, telling employees the company's deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations and that markets can sometimes "misunderstand and act irrationally".

Source: Reuters

items.author: ロイター

items.summary: [イスラマバード １５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[イスラマバード １５日 ロイター] - パキスタン北西部ペシャワルで１５日午前、授業中だった学校の屋根が崩落し、生徒少なくとも３２人と教員１人が死亡した。警察と救助当局が明らかにした。

救助隊は私立学校「アルハイル教育センター」のがれきの中から子どもたちを助け出す作業を数時間にわたり続けた。校舎の外には、安否を案じる保護者や親族が詰めかけた。救助当局によると、死亡した生徒の大半は１３歳未満で、少なくとも４５人が重軽傷を負った。

上階の屋根が下の教室にいた児童・生徒の上に崩れ落ち、校舎の２つの階が押しつぶされたという。

ペシャワルの警察署長は「建物の構造が脆弱だった。その上に増築され屋根に過大な荷重がかかり崩落につながった」と指摘。学校の所有者を逮捕し、捜査を開始したと明らかにした。

シャリフ首相は犠牲者の家族に哀悼の意を表した。

Oct 15 : Financial technology startup Ramp said on Thursday it had raised $1.85 billion in a primary financing round led by Dragoneer Investment Group, valuing the company at $60 billion, as the company expands its artificial intelligence offerings.
The funding underscores growing investor interest in financial automation, as corporate software companies add artificial intelligence to expense management, procurement and treasury functions once dominated by legacy enterprise players.
Ramp's valuation marks a rise from $44 billion in June, when it raised $750 million in a funding round.
The New York-based company, which provides corporate cards and expense management software, said it generates more than $2 billion in annualized revenue and has positive cash flow.

Founded in 2019, Ramp serves more than 85,000 companies, which collectively account for more than $275 billion in annualized purchase volume, up 175 per cent from a year earlier.
The company is also expanding into artificial intelligence tools, including software to monitor AI spending and optimize the cost of running AI models.
The latest round was co-led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital and Avenir Growth. Other investors included Fidelity Management & Research Company, T. Rowe Price, GIC and Coatue, the company said.
Ramp said it has raised approximately $5 billion in total equity financing, including the latest round.

items.title: Cobre toca mínimo de casi dos semanas por toma de ganancias, se reducen temores sobre oferta
items.author: Eric Onstad
items.creator: Eric Onstad
items.summary: Los precios del cobre bajaron a su menor nivel en casi dos semanas el jueves, afectados por una toma de beneficios tras el alivio de las preocupaciones sobre el suministro, una ola de ventas en las acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial y los temores por el aumento de la inflación y las tasas de interés.
items.body:
Los precios del cobre bajaron a su menor nivel en casi dos semanas el jueves, afectados por una toma de beneficios tras el alivio de las preocupaciones sobre el suministro, una ola de ventas en las acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial y los temores por el aumento de la inflación y las tasas de interés.
* A las 1625 GMT, el contrato referencial del cobre a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) restó un 1,3%, a 14.298 dólares por tonelada, tras tocar su mínimo desde el 2 de octubre, a 14.256 dólares.
* "Están ocurriendo dos cosas al mismo tiempo: el alivio de las preocupaciones sobre el suministro y el fuerte reporte de la inflación", dijo Ole Hansen, responsable de estrategia de materias primas del Saxo Bank en Copenhague. "Eso fue demasiado para que el mercado lo asimilara de golpe y está surgiendo cierta toma de beneficios".
* Las perspectivas técnicas también se están deteriorando, con el cobre poniendo a prueba la tendencia alcista iniciada en marzo y algo por debajo de la media móvil de 50 días, añadió.
* Los inversores se mostraron menos preocupados por las interrupciones en las explotaciones mineras después de que BHP (BHP.AX) y el sindicato de supervisores de su mina de Escondida, en Chile, anunciaran el miércoles que habían llegado a un acuerdo, evitando así una huelga en la mina de cobre más grande del mundo.
* La minera chilena Antofagasta (ANTO.L) comunicó el jueves un aumento del 7% en la producción de cobre del tercer trimestre y mantuvo sus previsiones anuales a pesar de la huelga de los trabajadores sindicados en su mina Centinela.
* Una ola de ventas de acciones tecnológicas asiáticas también presionó al mercado de metales. MKTS/GLOB
* El contrato de cobre más negociado en la Bolsa de Futuros de Shanghái cayó un 1,9%, a 108.940 yuanes (16.276,46 dólares) por tonelada.
* Mientras, el aluminio en la LME avanzó un 0,3%, a 2.995,50 dólares la tonelada, recuperándose después de tocar más temprano su menor nivel en más de nueve meses, en 2.953,50 dólares.
* En otros metales básicos, el zinc cayó un 1,1%, a 3.677,50 dólares por tonelada; el plomo perdió un 0,7%, a 1.883 dólares; el níquel restó un 1,7%, a 15.240 dólares; y el estaño cotizó con pocos cambios, a 50.440 dólares, tras alcanzar su nivel más bajo desde junio.

items.body:
Tom Balmforth　Edward Carron

[ロンドン １５日 ロイター] - ロシアが、高速で迎撃が困難な「ジェット推進型」ドローン（無人機）の発射拠点をわずか６週間でほぼ完成させたことが、防衛専門家への取材や衛星画像の分析で分かった。ロシアはこの高速ドローンをウクライナへの攻撃に投入し、ウクライナは迎撃に苦戦している。

ロシアはウクライナへの無人機攻撃に少なくとも１１カ所の固定発射拠点を使っており、今回の施設はそこに新たに加わる。場所はロシア南西部のロストフ州。 プラネット・ラボとエアバスが提供した商業衛星画像によれば、８月３１日時点では何もない原野だったが、１０月１４日までに、サッカー場約１２６面分の広さの複合施設に変わっていた。 約３．５キロメートルの場所にはミレロボ空軍基地がある。

建設期間は、ジェット推進型ドローンを使ったウクライナに対する攻撃が急増した時期と重なる。軍事アナリストは、ロシアが無人機の生産をジェット推進型にシフトしていると指摘する。

ジェット推進型ドローンは最高時速６００キロに達する。ウクライナ軍のデータによると、ロシアは夏の３カ月間でこの無人機の使用を約６倍に増やした。最も激しく攻撃されたのはキーウとその周辺地域だった。ウクライナが開発した迎撃用無人機は、旧型無人機を念頭にしたもので太刀打ちできない。ウクライナ政府は今、対策を急いでいる。

民間情報会社ドローンセックの創業者で最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）のマイク・モニク氏によると、施設の西端に最新型のジェット推進型ドローン「ゲラン４」と「ゲラン５」を発射できるレールを置くための台が８基ある。施設は完成が非常に近いように見え、「完全に稼働するまでにはおそらく数週間、もっと早い可能性もある」と述べた。 ロイターの分析では、８基の発射台のうち２基には既にレールが設置され、ほかの２基でもレールの設置が進んでいた。

ドローンセックは、新しい発射拠点は、ミレロボ空軍基地の防空システムの防御範囲（バブル）内とみられ、ウクライナがこの施設を攻撃するのは困難との見方を示した。

Rae Wee　Phoebe Seers

[バンコク／ロンドン １５日 ロイター] - イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）のブリーデン副総裁は１５日、深刻なサイバー攻撃を受けた場合の復旧策について、銀行と協力して検討していると明らかにした。

同氏は人工知能（ＡＩ）を使ったサイバー攻撃を防御できると想定することはできないと指摘、ＡＩの進歩は世界の金融インフラに「システミックリスク」をもたらす水準に達したと警告した。

バンコクで開かれた国際金融協会（ＩＩＦ）の年次総会で「サイバー攻撃による侵入を防げると想定するだけでは十分ではない。中核サービスに必要な『ベアメタル復旧』の選択肢を検討する必要がある。金融システム全体を通じて、これを考えなければならない」と述べた。

いわゆる「ベアメタル」システムは、銀行の主要な技術基盤から完全に独立しており、主要システムが侵害された場合に稼働できる。

世界の銀行規制当局は、拡大するＡＩリスクの抑制に向けた取り組みを強化している。ロイターは１３日、英国でも監督当局が大手銀行にベアメタル復旧計画の検討を促していると報じた。

ブリーデン氏は、ＡＩの発展により、大規模で複雑なサイバー攻撃のリスクが高まっていると警告。「サイバーセキュリティーの基本的な対策が、これまで以上に重要になっている」と述べた。

「夜も眠れなくなる懸念は何かと聞かれれば、いつもサイバー問題だと答えている。最も心配しているのは、目覚めた時に、金融システム上極めて重要な銀行の一つや中核インフラの一部が攻撃を受け、まひしていることだ」と語った。

items.title: Northern Ireland's Donaldson sentenced to 15 years in jail for child sex offences
items.author: Amanda Ferguson
items.creator: Amanda Ferguson
items.summary: The former leader of Northern Ireland's largest unionist party, Jeffrey Donaldson, was sentenced to 15 years in jail on Thursday for child sex offences that were described by the judge as representing "a catastrophic descent into disgrace".
items.body:
The former leader of Northern Ireland's largest unionist party, Jeffrey Donaldson, was sentenced to 15 years in jail on Thursday for child sex offences that were described by the judge as representing "a catastrophic descent into disgrace".
Donaldson [USN:L1N42U0JD TEXT:"was convicted"] in June of one count of rape, 13 counts of indecent assault and four counts of gross indecency against two children between 1985 and 2008 in one of the highest-profile cases in the British-run region in recent times.
He was one of Northern Ireland's best-known politicians and its longest-serving lawmaker in the British parliament when he was arrested and charged in March 2024.
The 63-year-old stared straight ahead as Judge Paul Ramsey handed down the sentence. Ramsey described the case as "disturbing and disquieting" and assessed Donaldson as having a medium chance of reoffending.
Donaldson, who has been in prison awaiting sentence since June, denied all charges and is [USN:L8N43J1N7 TEXT:"seeking to appeal"] against his convictions.
Prosecution lawyer Rosemary Walsh told a pre-sentencing hearing last month that one of the victims described the abuse as "the worst moment of her life" and that it had affected all her relationships since.
The other victim believed her childhood had been stolen and that she had carried around feelings of "shame" ever since. The victims, neither of whom can be identified for legal reasons, gave evidence during the trial.
Ramsey said he was in no doubt whatsoever of the permanent mark left on both victims and that this, the length of abuse and age of the victims, were aggravating factors in the severity of the sentence. He said Donaldson had doubled down on his denials and not offered one word of apology or shame.
Donaldson qualifies for an automatic 50% remission of his sentence as the offences were committed before a change in the law that gave judges discretion over what portion is spent in custody, meaning he will spend 7-1/2 years in prison, the Lady Chief Justice's Office of Northern Ireland said.
Donaldson immediately stepped down as head of the Democratic Unionist Party, founded by Protestant cleric Ian Paisley at the height of three decades of sectarian bloodshed, which ended after a 1998 peace deal.
He was knighted by the late Queen Elizabeth for his political services in 2016 and was central to the negotiation of a key post-Brexit trade deal just two months prior to his arrest.
He asked for his knighthood [USN:L8N42W1PI TEXT:"to be renounced"] two days after his conviction.
The jury also found that Donaldson's wife, Eleanor, aided and abetted her husband. She has also denied the charges.
The court ruled her unfit to stand trial last month, due to mental health issues, meaning she could not face criminal conviction.

items.title: Ataque de drones contra dos petroleros deja siete desaparecidos frente a costa rumana
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Equipos de rescate buscaban el jueves a siete marinos desaparecidos después de que unos drones atacaron dos buques cisterna para productos químicos cerca de la costa rumana del mar Negro, provocando un incendio y suscitando preocupaciones de seguridad en una ruta vital para Ucrania.
items.body:
Equipos de rescate buscaban el jueves a siete marinos desaparecidos después de que unos drones atacaron dos buques cisterna para productos químicos cerca de la costa rumana del mar Negro, provocando un incendio y suscitando preocupaciones de seguridad en una ruta vital para Ucrania.
El presidente rumano, Nicusor Dan, afirmó que los dos buques fueron alcanzados por drones, pero se negó a precisar si Rusia era la responsable.
"Dos drones aéreos los alcanzaron", declaró Dan a la prensa en Bruselas antes de una cumbre de líderes de la Unión Europea, y añadió que Rumanía seguía recabando información apenas unas horas después de los ataques. "Habrá una reacción por parte del Estado rumano".
Los buques estaban fondeados cerca de la desembocadura del canal de Sulina, que conduce al río Danubio, una importante ruta de exportación usada por Ucrania ante los repetidos ataques rusos contra sus puertos del mar Negro. Uno estaba en aguas territoriales rumanas y el otro, justo fuera.
Los tripulantes desaparecidos formaban parte de los 12 marinos a bordo del petrolero Wine Trader, con bandera de San Marino, que fue alcanzado a 13 millas náuticas al sureste del canal, cerca de aguas rumanas. Cinco tripulantes fueron rescatados, según las autoridades rumanas.
El segundo buque, el petrolero y químico Yara J, con bandera de Comoras, se incendió tras ser alcanzado a entre 8 y 10 millas al sureste de Sulina, dentro de aguas rumanas, a última hora del miércoles. Todos sus tripulantes estaban a salvo.
Estos ataques son los últimos de una serie de ataques contra la navegación mercante en la parte occidental del mar Negro.
Al menos otros cinco buques de carga han sido atacados cerca de las costas de Rumanía y de la vecina Bulgaria, miembros de la OTAN, en los últimos diez días, con al menos 23 marineros desaparecidos o fallecidos. Los incidentes ocurrieron fuera de las aguas territoriales de la alianza.
El Ministerio del Interior informó de que envió dos helicópteros Black Hawk para la misión de búsqueda y rescate, así como dos buques con personal médico a bordo. "En este momento, el rescate no puede realizarse de forma segura debido al fuerte oleaje", señaló en un comunicado.
La OTAN dijo en un comunicado que está en contacto con las autoridades rumanas.
NUEVOS ATAQUES Añadió que otros dos buques fueron atacados en el mar Negro: el granelero Sea Destiny, con pabellón de Islas Marshall, que estaba en aguas rumanas, y el petrolero Dania J, con bandera de Tanzania, amarrado en el puerto ucraniano de Izmail, en el Danubio. No se mencionaron víctimas.
"La OTAN seguirá colaborando de forma estrecha con nuestros aliados en el mar Negro, ajustando nuestra postura de disuasión y defensa según sea necesario", indicó el secretario general de la OTAN, Mark Rutte, tras reunirse con Dan y el primer ministro búlgaro, Rumen Radev.
Rumanía comparte una frontera de 614 kilómetros con Ucrania, gran parte de ella a lo largo del Danubio. Ha denunciado reiteradas incursiones de drones rusos en su espacio aéreo desde el inicio de la invasión de Ucrania por parte de Moscú en 2022.
La escalada de ataques contra la navegación en el mar Negro ha agravado la preocupación por las exportaciones de cereales de la región.
Los ataques rusos contra los puertos ucranianos del mar Negro han obligado a Kiev a depender más del Danubio y las rutas marítimas cercanas a las costas de Rumanía y Bulgaria. Ucrania, por su parte, ha atacado buques rusos cerca de la desembocadura del río Don, en el mar de Azov.
Radev afirmó que los líderes de la UE debatirán una propuesta de moratoria sobre los ataques a buques civiles en el mar Negro.
"Consideramos el mar Negro una arteria del suministro mundial de alimentos", dijo la ministra rumana de Relaciones Exteriores, Oana Toiu, en una conferencia de seguridad celebrada en Varsovia esta semana.
"Actualmente es, por desgracia, el mar más mortífero si se tiene en cuenta el número de víctimas entre los marineros en los últimos meses. Eso significa que tenemos que aumentar nuestras inversiones en disuasión y defensa", agregó.

items.title: El oro repunta por la debilidad del dólar y la caída de los rendimientos en EEUU
items.author: Pablo Sinha
items.creator: Pablo Sinha
items.summary: El oro subió más de un 1% el jueves, para romper una racha de tres sesiones de pérdidas, respaldado por la debilidad del dólar y el descenso de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, mientras que las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas este mes eran moderadas a pesar de que los datos de inflación fueron más altos de lo esperado.
items.body:
El oro subió más de un 1% el jueves, para romper una racha de tres sesiones de pérdidas, respaldado por la debilidad del dólar y el descenso de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, mientras que las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas este mes eran moderadas a pesar de que los datos de inflación fueron más altos de lo esperado.
El oro al contado ganó un 1,1%, a 4.149 dólares por onza, a las 1636 GMT, tras caer a un mínimo de una semana en la sesión anterior. Los futuros del oro estadounidense para entrega en diciembre avanzaron un 1,5%, a 4.170,10 dólares por onza.
El dólar (.DXY) caía un 0,4%, mientras que el rendimiento de referencia de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años se situaba en un mínimo de tres semanas.
"Creo que el mercado ya anticipaba en gran medida los altos datos del índice de precios al productor (IPP), tras las cifras del índice de precios al consumidor (IPC) de ayer (miércoles), que superaron las expectativas", dijo Peter Grant, vicepresidente y estratega sénior de metales en Zaner Metals.
"El mercado está empezando a darse cuenta de que la Fed tiene las manos atadas en cierta medida debido a la situación fiscal y de que subir las tasas de interés mucho más supondrá una carga considerable para la economía".
Unas tasas de interés más altas hacen que los activos que no generan rendimiento resulten menos atractivos.
Los precios al productor de Estados Unidos anotaron en septiembre su mayor subida en cuatro años y medio, en un contexto de aumento de los costos de los bienes y servicios, lo que constituye el más reciente indicio de que la inflación se está traspasando de la energía a otros productos.
Los datos se sumaron al informe sobre los precios al consumidor publicado el miércoles, que mostró una aceleración de los precios en septiembre debido al aumento de los costos de la gasolina.
Sin embargo, la presidenta de la Fed de San Francisco, Mary Daly, y la vicepresidenta de Supervisión, Michelle Bowman, subrayaron que quizá no sea necesaria una subida inmediata de las tasas, lo que moderó las expectativas de un alza en octubre.
Entre otros metales, la plata al contado trepó un 2,3%, a 56,90 dólares por onza; el platino subió un 0,4%, a 1.613,75 dólares; y el paladio sumó un 3,2%, a 1.129,20 dólares la onza.

items.title: TSX rises as lower bond yields offset tech, energy weakness
items.author: Utkarsh Hathi
items.creator: Utkarsh Hathi
items.summary: Canada's main stock index rose on Thursday, as lower bond yields boosted risk appetite, offsetting weakness in energy shares caused by falling oil prices and a global selloff in AI-related technology stocks.
items.body:
Canada's main stock index rose on Thursday, as lower bond yields boosted risk appetite, offsetting weakness in energy shares caused by falling oil prices and a [USN:L1N4610FG TEXT:"global selloff "]in AI-related technology stocks.
The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) was up 0.52% at 35,770 points by 10:41 a.m. ET, rebounding after sharp declines in the previous session.
Canada's benchmark 10-year bond yield slipped about 8 basis points to 3.795%, driving broad sectoral gains
Materials sector (.GSPTTMT) , including metal miners, gained 1.4% as precious metal prices rebounded on a softer dollar
Chip stocks globally extended losses as concerns about increased borrowing costs unsettled investors, dragging Wall Street's Nasdaq down 0.7%
Canadian tech equities (.SPTTTK) declined 0.7%, with e-commerce platform Shopify (SHOP.TO) slipping 1.4% and electronics equipment firm Celestica (CLS.TO) down 7.7%
"The sector has continued to be under pressure that started at the beginning of the year, except (for) the relief rally in the spring and summer," said Shiraz Ahmed, CEO of Sartorial Wealth
"The moat around their (software) business is not quite as strong, now that AI and the ability to effectively recreate software has become very commoditized"
Energy sector (.SPTTEN) slipped 0.5% as oil prices eased 0.7% after a US official on Wednesday signaled potential US steps to ease restriction on Russia's "shadow fleet" tankers
Canadian [USN:AQN2MO654 TEXT:"factory sales"] grew 1.5% in August from July on higher sales of primary metals, data showed on Thursday
Still, economists remain cautious about recovery in manufacturing considering limited sectoral gains
"This reinforces our view that the Bank of Canada will deliver only two of the roughly four rate hikes currently priced in by markets, with tightening serving more as a risk-management exercise against upside inflation risks," said Thomas Ryan, senior North America economist, Capital Economics

BENGALURU, Oct 15 : Wipro's quarterly deal bookings plunged to an almost four-year low, deepening worries that India's fourth-largest IT firm is ceding market share to rivals.
Thursday's news dragged down the company's US-listed shares 4.5 per cent in premarket trading and highlighted CEO Srinivas Pallia's struggle to revive growth more than two years after taking the helm.
"Wipro is still not out of the woods, and this will persist," Indsec Securities analyst Rishubh Vasa said, highlighting how the firm's ability to win new business has weakened over the past two to three quarters. "Their order book is in stress."
AI has disrupted India's $315 billion IT industry, forcing firms to revamp business models and offer deep discounts to win deals. Wipro, meanwhile, has also struggled with top-level exits and acquisition-related challenges.

The company's total contract value bookings plunged to $2.6 billion in the quarter ended September 30 from $4.7 billion a year earlier.
Underscoring Wipro's need to bag large deals, Pareekh Jain, founder of IT research firm EIIR Trend, said its "dual focus on margin and revenue is not working." While Cognizant has been gaining ground with aggressive pricing and Tech Mahindra has revived margins after exiting low-yield accounts, Wipro is still trailing the pack, Jain added.
DEMAND WOES
Wipro forecast third-quarter revenue of $2.57 billion to $2.63 billion, implying a roughly 1.5 per cent decline to 0.5 per cent growth. That was modestly ahead of analysts' expectations for revenue to decline up to 2 per cent or remain flat.
Seasonal furloughs would weigh on third-quarter performance, Pallia said.
Consolidated second-quarter revenue rose 9.1 per cent to 247.53 billion rupees ($2.60 billion), edging past analysts' average estimate of 246.27 billion rupees, according to LSEG data.
Net profit, hurt by higher wage and subcontracting costs, fell 1.5 per cent to 32.01 billion rupees, below expectations of 33.69 billion rupees.
($1 = 95.0550 Indian rupees)

items.title: Trump donor leading Caucasus fund has major Armenia holdings, Russia business history
items.author: Jonathan Landay, Alexandra Ulmer, Maria Tsvetkova
items.creator: Jonathan Landay, Alexandra Ulmer, Maria Tsvetkova
items.summary: US President Donald Trump’s pick to lead a $201 million investment fund in the Caucasus holds major telecom and mining interests there and formerly ran a Russia-focused investment firm that touted close ties to the Kremlin, documents reviewed by Reuters show.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump’s pick to lead a $201 million investment fund in the Caucasus holds major telecom and mining interests there and formerly ran a Russia-focused investment firm that touted close ties to the Kremlin, documents reviewed by Reuters show.
Konstantin Sokolov, a 51-year-old Russian-born businessman, was put in charge of the investment vehicle, now called the Trans-Caspian Enterprise Fund, in January, according to its incorporation documents.
He holds major stakes in Armenia’s top mobile phone company Viva Armenia, and purchased Armenia’s second largest copper and molybdenum mine earlier this year after receiving a special permit from the US government to buy it, according to the Reuters reporting.
A Reuters review of public documents related to the only three other US enterprise funds now operating showed no indications that any of their heads have major investments in the countries where those funds invest.
Bo Cutter, chairman of a US enterprise fund focused on Tunisia told Reuters he had "no business interests of any kind in Tunisia," without elaborating on whether and why that might pose a problem. Cutter declined to comment on Sokolov or the Trans-Caspian fund.
Still, according to six ethics experts who reviewed the Reuters reporting, Sokolov’s business interests create a conflict of interest because his role gives him control of government money that could potentially benefit his companies.
Ann Skeet, an ethics expert at Santa Clara University, said, "I think Congress should be asking questions."
Reuters found no indication of any wrongdoing by Sokolov. US legislation governing such investment funds does not forbid directors from holding investments in regions of operation.
A representative for Sokolov’s private equity firm, IJS Investments, said the fund was prohibited from investing in any of his businesses and that Sokolov had complied with "all due diligence and security requirements."
A State Department spokesperson said the enterprise fund would comply with annual reporting requirements and independent audits "as well as with applicable grant provisions including conflict of interest requirements."
Sokolov had been among a list of 37 corporate and individual donors to Trump’s White House ballroom project distributed by the White House last year. The Washington Post reported on Thursday that Sokolov donated $1 million to the project.
Sokolov has also donated some $13 million to Republican political groups, according to Federal Election Commission data.
ASCENDANT IN ARMENIA The Trans-Caspian fund is part of a broader US push to develop trade routes and investment across the South Caucasus and Central Asia, an effort that could reduce the region's reliance on Russian and Chinese infrastructure.
The Trans-Caspian fund’s board, led by Sokolov, has the power to make grants, loans and investments across Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. Its website lists critical minerals, energy and rail infrastructure among its top investment priorities.
Sokolov has built up his business presence in Armenia rapidly in recent years.
He and a Chinese business partner, Zhe Zhang, acquired control of Viva Armenia in January 2024 from Russia's largest mobile provider, MTS, according to company statements and Armenian corporate records.
Zhang, a former Chinese Commerce Ministry diplomat, did not respond to requests for comment. Viva Armenia did not comment.
More recently, Sokolov’s Texas-based Dynamic Frontier Holdings company said it was granted legal authorization from the US Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control on June 1 to buy Armenia’s Teghout mine from a sanctioned state-owned Russian bank, VTB.
OFAC licenses authorize transactions that would otherwise be prohibited by US sanctions and typically take several months or years to process.
Sokolov and a representative for the Teghout mine did not respond to questions about when they first applied for a license. A representative for Teghout said licenses and approvals for the transaction were obtained through OFAC’s "standard independent regulatory process."
The US Treasury Department and VTB did not respond to requests for comment.
None of the heads of the only other active US enterprise funds - which focus on Egypt, Tunisia, and Ukraine-Moldova - appear to have significant business interests in those countries, according to a Reuters review of public documents and their official biographies.
James Harmon is chairman of the Egyptian fund, and Dennis Johnson is chairman of the Ukraine-Moldova fund. They did not respond to requests for comment.
BACKGROUND IN RUSSIA Sokolov’s biography on his personal website highlights his modest upbringing in St. Petersburg and his dislike of the Soviet government, which he said sent his grandmother to a gulag. It says he immigrated to the United States at 21, several years after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
But his ties to Russia went on long after he left, according to a Reuters review of corporate and government records.
The businessman’s purported ties to the Russian government warrant scrutiny to ensure US interests come first in the fund’s management, said two of the ethics experts Reuters interviewed.
"I'd want a very thorough security clearance review if I were in the US government," said Richard Painter, a University of Minnesota professor who served as ethics counsel to former Republican President George W. Bush.
A 2015 promotional brochure reviewed by Reuters for the now-defunct Liechtenstein-registered Gotthard Investment Fund, a Russia-focused real estate investment operation, listed Sokolov as a fund manager and emphasized the fund’s "strong and long-lasting personal and professional trust relationships forged over the last 20 years with Moscow, St. Petersburg and Federal governments."
A former project manager with the fund, speaking to Reuters on condition of anonymity, said they recognized the brochure as authentic.
Lawyers representing Sokolov said that Sokolov "does not believe" the brochure is authentic, and that the logo on the brochure did not appear to be one used by the fund.
"Mr. Sokolov has no relationships with Russian government officials or the Russian government," his representative told Reuters, adding "he does not hold a Russian citizenship."
Reuters could not independently confirm Sokolov no longer has Russian citizenship.
Sokolov used a Russian passport for international travel as late as 2016, according to travel records reviewed by Reuters.
The White House referred requests for comment about Sokolov to the State Department. The State Department did not provide details on Sokolov’s background check or whether he had a security clearance.
When asked for comment about Sokolov, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said: "We don’t know who you are talking about."

items.title: UK's FTSE 100 closes at seven-week high on fiscal reassurance, defensive buying
items.author: Darshan R
items.creator: Darshan R
items.summary: London's blue-chip stocks closed at a seven-week high on Thursday after the finance minister reaffirmed the government's commitment to fiscal discipline, while a shift into defensive sectors amid a deepening global selloff in AI-related stocks also supported the benchmark.
items.body:
London's blue-chip stocks closed at a seven-week high on Thursday after the finance minister [USN:S8N4040BJ TEXT:"reaffirmed"] the government's commitment to fiscal discipline, while a shift into defensive sectors amid a deepening global selloff in AI-related stocks also supported the benchmark.
The benchmark FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) closed higher by 1.1% to 10,840.35 points, its highest since August 26, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) also rose 0.26%.
Investors sought refuge in defensive sectors as a global chip stocks selloff intensified, benefiting UK's large caps with limited exposure to AI
"It's a rotation towards long-term; almost an infrastructure play without the risk of a rate increase and healthcare, consumer cyclicals are a safer heaven as they are not overly leveraged," said Nick Saunders, CEO of Webull UK
Drugmakers AstraZeneca (AZN.L) and GSK (GSK.L) climbed 3.2% and 2.9%, respectively
Dove soap maker Unilever (ULVR.L) rose 1.8% and cigarette maker British American Tobacco (BATS.L) advanced 2.5%
British finance minister John Healey said this month's budget would aim at bolstering economic resilience, adding that he and Prime Minister Andy Burnham were aligned on maintaining fiscal discipline
Financials (.FTNMX301010) , including heavily weighted banks, was up 0.3%
UK's [USN:L8N4610AT TEXT:"gross domestic product"] rose 0.1% in August, boosted by AI optimism, against expectations of a 0.1% drop
Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said that any [USN:L1N461041 TEXT:"future interest rate increase"] should not be interpreted by investors as the start of a prolonged series of rate hikes
[USN:L6N4600XN TEXT:"Economists polled"] by Reuters expect the BoE to raise rates to 4% in November
Industrial metal miners (.FTNMX551020) were down 1.4%, on weaker copper prices
Antofagasta (ANTO.L) fell 4.1%, after the Chilean miner's third-quarter [USN:L1N46106S TEXT:"copper production"] declined year-on-year
E-commerce group THG (THG.L) surged 16.3% after lifting its annual profit forecast
Paper and packaging firm Mondi (MNDI.L) slumped 7.9% after hiking prices for several paper grades to offset higher energy costs
